name: Casa Belgrado
orgDescription: Casa Belgrado was founded in 2013 in the Balvanera neighborhood of Buenos Aires, operating from the visible margins of the city’s art scene. Since 2015, it has run an international artistic residency program. In 2019, it expanded to include La Vitrina, a street-level exhibition and experimentation space. We are a team of Latin American artists and cultural managers from diverse disciplines. We provide each resident with close professional and personal support, and connect them with the cultural ecosystem of Balvanera and the broader Buenos Aires scene — offering a perspective rooted in the Southern Cone. Casa Belgrado functions as a space for research, rehearsal, workshops, intensives, and performance. We work with contemporary art in a post-disciplinary sense: performance, dance, theater, sonic art, film, multimedia, and more. Our interest is in dialogue, exchange, and the convergence of divergent creative energies.
residencyDescription: Casa Belgrado welcomes artists, creators, activists and cultural managers seeking time and space for reflection, research, and creative development. We are especially interested in projects that work at the intersection of disciplines — blending scenic, visual, and sound practices — and that explore themes such as border, migration, territory, community, history, heritage, and margin. Projects outside these themes are also welcome.

name: 18th Street Arts Center
orgDescription: Founded in 1988, 18th Street Arts Center is one of the top 20 artist residency programs in the US. 18th Street encourages contemporary artists from around the globe to create new work within a supportive environment. We provide artists the space and time to take risks in ways that further the development of their practice. Our mission is to provoke public dialogue through contemporary art-making. 18th Street Arts Center values art making as an essential component of a vibrant, just, and healthy society, and we believe that the creative process is just as important as the outcome. Through our artist residencies we are a contemporary art hub that fosters inter-cultural collaboration and dialogue. 18th Street’s residencies, exhibitions, public events, talks, and publications encourage, showcase and support the creation of cutting-edge contemporary art, and foster collaboration and interaction between artists locally, nationally, and internationally. We host over 30 visiting artists at 18th Street annually, and have supported the work of over 6,000 artists since our founding. Our campus of five buildings in Santa Monica, on the west side of Los Angeles, is home to a diverse community of artists including established mentor artists and emerging voices. Our Visiting Artist in Residence Program functions within a larger arts center that includes our formal gallery, other nonprofit arts organizations who offer their own programs (theater/dance/music), and long-term artist studios for local LA-based artists.
residencyDescription: 18th Street Arts Center’s visiting artist residency program has hosted more than 500 artists from dozens of countries around the world since it first began in 1992. There are dedicated four live/work artist studios at the center where artists are in residence from 1 to 3 months at a time (sometimes longer). This program hosts artists of all disciplines as well as art curators, writers, and musicians. It includes invited artists as well as artists selected through an open application process. The program is open to artists of all generations, nationalities, and disciplines.

name: Neshat Art Residency & Gallery
orgDescription: Neshat residency, as a haven and sanctuary for creative work located in Darya Kenar, which is one of the oldest and largest residential towns in northern Iran and within just 100 walking distance to Caspian sea. Residents will be provided with accommodation in a furnished homestudio suitable for various disciplines and purposes. it is furnished with working table,bed,tv and audio system. The most effective part of the residency as a social living space is the backyard, which overlooks the community and contact the artist to the community. This connection make it suitable for screenings, meetings, workshops, exhibition and is shared area with community.
residencyDescription: Neshat residency is designed to enable creative exploration, encourage intercultural dialogue and concentrated work in a private and individual environment in one the famous towns of Iran named Daryakenar which is one of the oldest and largest residential towns in northern Iran. This residential-recreational coastal town is famous for being located along the Caspian Sea and having dense green spaces and a pleasant family environment. The construction of this coastal town began with the support of Mohammad Reza Shah Pahlavi in ​​the early 1940s and ended in the late 40s, which at the time was one of the first and largest towns in Iran in the Middle East. The design of the open space and its villas is influenced by Western architecture, and Mr. “Hossein Amanat”, the famous designer of Azadi Square and Tower, has also contributed to the design of this town.

name: IVYNODE
orgDescription: IVYnode is an independent and non profit program based in Barcelona but with strong roots in Sardinia. The aim is to bring together people from different backgrounds, experiences and knowledge, involving local communities, organizations, private persons, public institutions, for working together in a multi- and interdisciplinary environment, with a focus on culture, art, science, environment and innovation. We believe that communication, creativity, interaction are fundamental instruments for building a community where the different actors of the society cooperate together, rediscovering the importance of social relationships for a human dimension. We work mainly with artists who have a social practice and work with sustainable materials or food, or have a strong interest in collaboration or research, The character of the residency is transdisciplinary. Our residencies, exhibitions, international projects and workshops PROGRAMS act as bridges connecting international and local artists with the members of the communities, who normally don’t have easy access to the conventional galleries and museums of large urban centres. Many small communities in Sardinia are semi-abandoned as youth migrate towards cities for education and work. The idea is to rejuvenating the smaller villages giving to the youth a possibility to stay or return. At the same time the international artists involved it the cultural exchange projects, will have the possibility to learn the language and to stay in contact with cultural traditions or even to work with artisans which still maintains ancient knowledge. We also have the focus to empower the locals communities giving them the possibility to re-evaluate their cultural identity.

name: Lakkos Artist Residency
orgDescription: The residency is self-funded and artist-run. It’s a casual space for all creative disciplines. There are no formal programs. Murals are a popular choice for visiting visual artists. We often have presentations of artistic projects, but this is up to each individual. The island of Crete is a great place to discover and research ancient and modern Greek culture. The residency has three bedrooms in a shared city apartment. Plus a new residency in a beautiful village. We make connections with the local community, according to the needs of each resident.
residencyDescription: There is no set program, artists come with their projects and the residency is there to help with connections or information as needed. The aim of the residency is to bring life back to a neglected part of Heraklion City’s old town. That project went very well so now the residency has moved to a new location in the Old Town which is currently in need of an artistic injection. This is mainly done via murals.

name: 2415 Space
orgDescription: 2415空间是一个独立的、艺术家主导的创意中心，位于中国丽江境内2415米。2415空间以艺术探索精神为根基，是一个实验、合作和跨学科交流的平台，旨在培育与环境、工艺和文化叙述相关的创新项目。 2415空间在前传统的纳西庭院内，是一个充满活力的场所，建筑、自然和艺术实践在这里交汇。该空间举办艺术家驻地、展览、研讨会和研讨会，为艺术家、策展和创意人士创造了一个开放的环境，可以让开发和分享想法、探索新方法，并与周围的景观和灯光建立联系。 2415空间高度以、时间和创作转变为中心，邀请艺术家进入一个视角转变的场景，过去、现在和未来之间的界限变得模糊不清。 2415 Space is an independent, artist-led creative centre located at 2415m in Lijiang, China. 2415 Space is rooted in the spirit of artistic discovery and serves as a platform for experimentation, collaboration and cross-disciplinary exchange, aiming to cultivate innovative projects related to the environment, craftsmanship and cultural narratives. Housed in a former traditional Naxi courtyard, 2415 Space is a vibrant venue where architecture, nature and artistic practice converge. The space hosts artist residencies, exhibitions, workshops and seminars, creating an open environment for artists, curators and creatives to develop and share ideas, explore new approaches and make connections with the surrounding landscape and light. Highly-centred on, time and creative transformation, Space 2415 invites artists to enter a scenario of shifting perspectives where the boundaries between past, present and future become blurred.
residencyDescription: 2415艺术驻地是一个独立的、由艺术家运营的非营利驻地项目，促进艺术发展、跨学科交流和特定的现场探索。驻地位于中国丽江省2415米，为艺术家提供了一个独特的环境、省份、时间和交通相互组成，以同样的方式塑造艺术体验。

name: 32M Center for Creative Work
orgDescription: The 32M Center for Creative Work is an arts community/space that has as one of its organizing principals the convergence of more than one art discipline—functioning both independently and in a collaborative overlap, under the same roof. 32M is an emerging space for writers, artists, typographers, musicians, theater makers, performance artists, cinematographers, and artists of all kinds to make new work or explore new processes. A strong commitment to multi-disciplinary conversations and cross-pollinations is a guiding principle. Promoting an expansive, integrated dialogue between artists allows us to see the world differently and thus increase our creativity. We are located in the southwest corner of New Hampshire nestled between Pisgah State Park and the Ashuelot River.
residencyDescription: 32M offers a self directed residency for artists to work on their projects. The artist may choose to have access to critiques or coaching sessions either in person or via Zoom with members of our team, when available. Weekend workshops of book making, bookbinding, improvisational/experimental music and printmaking are held on certain weekends, and special week-long broadside retreats are offered on specific dates for writers wanting to add making a printed broadside of their work to their residency.

name: 33 Officina Creativa
orgDescription: 33 Officina Creativa (33OC) is a nonprofit cultural association based in Toffia, Italy, with the aims of diffusing contemporary art and preserving local cultural heritage, especially amongst the younger generations. This is achieved through international artistic exchanges and promotional activities that enable the inclusion of the territory where the association operates within a broader cultural horizon. 33OC is a cultural collective which hosts an international Artist Residency program and produces theatre and music performances, film programs, workshops, classes, and other public programs. It aims to operate as a regenerative social and cultural meeting place while becoming a discussion platform for artistic production. Our goal is to preserve the diversity of nature and culture of the Sabina region and to prevent the museification of Toffia – a small and quiet medieval hilltop village in the middle of Sabina – by offering a shared place of cultural and social exploration for national and international artists, the local community, and people from various cultural fields.
residencyDescription: 33 Officina Creativa (33OC) Artist Residency program was developed to become a space & community where international artists can share spaces, experiences, and sensibilities. Conceived of as a regenerative intercultural meeting place, the residency is aimed at international artists who are enthusiastic about working within Toffia’s environment.

orgDescription: The Rijksakademie van beeldende kunsten in Amsterdam focuses on developing talent in the fine arts. The institution selects and facilitates top talent and offers selected artists a platform for further development of their work. Presentation of the work and connections to an international network form a part of the two-year residency program. For many alumni the residency has led to their international breakthrough.
residencyDescription: The Rijksakademie’s artist residency has a unique ecology, which is highly international, multi-disciplinary, experimental and critically engaged. Artists are supported with a studio, a stipend, by a wide range of artistic and technical advisors, including artists, curators and thinkers, and have access to well-equipped workshops, a library and discursive engagement. This allows them to challenge themselves, experiment and deepen their practice. We have a commitment to diversity, to working with a global perspective and with sensitivity to the local. There is no fixed programme, dominant conception of style or ideology. The Rijksakademie offers time, people and opportunities.

name: Galerie Huit Arles
orgDescription: Galerie Huit Arles is located in the historic and pedestrianized heart of Arles, in the PACA region (Provence Côte d´Azur) between Marseille, Avignon and Montpellier, and borders the Camargue national park. The city of Arles has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1981. With 2,500 years of history, well-preserved Roman monuments including a Roman amphitheater and arena, Renaissance palaces and religious buildings, 3 world-class museums and several international art festivals (Arles hosts the famous international photography festival Rencontres d’Arles, as well as the new Festival du Dessin), it is not surprising that Arles is one of Europe’s top cultural destination, Arles has been the inspiring setting for many artists, especially the painter Vincent Van Gogh.
residencyDescription: The artists in residence live and work within the thick stone walls of a prestigious 17th century mansion, magnificently restored. Exhibition spaces and convivial living spaces occupy the ground floor and lower floors. The floors include occasional seminar rooms, guest rooms, self-catering apartments and studios for artist residencies.

orgDescription: A.I.R. VALLAURIS Located in the heart of the old town of Vallauris, the non-profit Association A.I.R. Vallauris welcomes international artists from all horizons to meet and collaborate with local artists and to research and create new work in an artistic laboratory created specifically for them. The Association has three primary objectives: The hosting of resident artists and the support of contemporary creation Education in the field of the arts The organization of cultural events
residencyDescription: ARTISTS IN RESIDENCE A.I.R. Vallauris accommodates several artists at a given time for a period of between one and two months, in its residence and studios. Using different mediums (ceramists, sculptors, painters, photographers, video and multimedia) artists work from equipped studios, live in individual furnished spaces and are afforded access to a gallery where their works are displayed and celebrated at the end of their residency period. Media involvement encourages the interest of an invited and engaged audience. The quality of artistic creation is one of the major concerns addressed by the programme. A selection committee evaluates applicants based on their artistic experience, merit and project proposal. Over the twenty-one year period from April 2002, over 400 artists of 30 different nationalities have participated in the A.I.R. Vallauris programme.

name: A Position on Retreat Inc
residencyName: A Position on Retreat Artist Residency
orgDescription: A Position on Retreat isn’t just about stepping back; it’s about taking a stance to retreat with purpose. Just as we take positions in life—whether political, social, or personal—there is a time to take a conscious position to pause and withdraw. This residency invites you to reconnect with yourself and your craft by immersing in the tranquil beauty of Vancouver Island’s temperate rainforest, a landscape as inspiring as it is unique. Apply now for an artist residency on Vancouver Island. Create, reflect, and connect in one of Canada’s most beautiful natural settings. Your stay includes a cozy home base equipped with both traditional and digital studio spaces, with the serene Lake Cowichan and its lush surroundings as your canvas. “Something is healing about this island.” “Lake Cowichan is such a quiet and friendly town, perfectly positioned to explore the island’s natural beauty.” “I feel like I am going home changed.” Our residency is designed to welcome artists from around the world, at all stages of their careers, and across as many disciplines as we can accommodate. This diversity fosters mentorship, friendship, and collaboration in an inspiring community setting. From guided nature excursions to relaxed studio days, you’ll have the space to explore, rejuvenate, and transform. Nestled in the vibrant small town of Lake Cowichan, you’ll be close to everything you need yet surrounded by the towering majesty of old-growth forests, stunning mountain views, and the shimmering lake. Whether it’s the Mediterranean climate, the proximity to Pacific Ocean beaches, or easy day trips to neighbouring gems like Salt Spring Island and Victoria, you’ll find both inspiration and relaxation at every turn. “Uncover new perspectives and let nature guide your next creative chapter.” Apply today and be part of a residency that will nurture your spirit, expand your artistry, and offer a retreat unlike any other in Canada.
residencyDescription: Our artist residency offers a serene, self-directed environment where creators across all disciplines can immerse themselves in nature and artistic exploration. Activities include guided nature trips, technical and conceptual discussions, and access to high-end digital and traditional studio spaces, fostering growth and rejuvenation. The objective is to provide artists with the resources and inspiration to advance their work, reconnect with their creative practice, and cultivate new perspectives amidst Vancouver Island’s breathtaking landscapes.

orgDescription: We are an experimental arts initiative that aims to create opportunities for artists and audiences, at different locations, some of the time. Formed in Autumn 2024 we have so far curated 6 exhibitions and one residency. We aim to take things slowly, provide the kinds of opportunities we would wish to have, and provide the support and encouragement that we would wish to have. We aim to create a gentle, convivial and creative atmosphere for all involved.
residencyDescription: Each Residency has a unique theme, and two lead artists or specialists who will inspire and provoke you to think, create and respond differently to this theme. Each residency takes place in a stunning location in Devon/on Dartmoor, in accommodation with shared dorm-style sleeping arrangements, and social spaces that have open fires. A chef will provide breakfast, lunch and evening meal. There is no expectation to create new work (we cannot offer exhibition opportunities attached to the residencies). We ask for one page of something made on site to include in a future zine-style publication. The residencies are self-funded.

name: AADK Spain
orgDescription: AADK Spain is an international artistic platform that opens up spaces for research and contemporary creation. With a focus set on experimental and creative processes, its primary interest is to explore the notions of body, territory, and spatiality through an interdisciplinary approach. The platform advocates the decentralization of culture and access to contemporary art in non-urban areas. It addresses local issues as a means to understand global problems. Currently based in Centro Negra (Blanca, Murcia), AADK Spain holds several programs among which its Artistic Residency Program stands out. Deeply rooted in its context, the program constitutes a framework for research and debate where knowledge exchange and creative collaboration are always encouraged. Besides the aforementioned, the platform also holds a wide number of activities, workshops and events that enrich the stay of the artists in residence. Furthermore, AADK Spain weaves networks with other cultural and artistic enterprises in order to facilitate mobility for the artists that it hosts and fosters their work at national and international circuits.
residencyDescription: AADK Spain understands residency programs as contextualized spaces where location models the practices and modifies both its participants and the local communities. Thus, our Artistic Residency is an interdisciplinary and socially committed program that offers its attendants a space for analysis and production. It aims to facilitate research in rural environments, highlighting the value of local knowledge as a means to re-think how these locations can position themselves in an era of massive urbanization through a social, historical and geographical perspective.

name: Absolute Arts Group
orgDescription: Newton’s “absolute space” law of motion has long been disproved by Albert Einstein’s theory of relativity. However, aesthetically, the concept of an eternal static value of art and its definite existence is yet to be explored. Following the belief that art can bring change to people’s lives and situations, the gallery is named Absolute Space and so, it advocates for the appreciation of beauty, the politics of discourse & representation and the creative act. The art gallery is therefore an exhibition hall, a house for expression and ultimately an open space for the conversation of art. As a non-profit art gallery, Absolute Space is set to satisfy the following three functions; exhibition, interaction, and archive. Regarding exhibition, we aim to provide artists with a stage where they can meet their public, free of commercial interests and expressive limitations. Secondly, on interaction, we view Absolute Space as a meeting platform designed for artists, audiences, and the art market, where conversation on art are held through workshops, dialogues between artists and speeches. Accordingly, we aim to make Absolute Space a perfect place for young artists in Tainan to exchange ideas, communicate, and interact with one another. Last but not least, Absolute Space now focuses on the construction of archives of Taiwanese artists, aiming to help make artists’ voice heard and stand the passage of time. Located in Tainan, the cultural capital of Taiwan, Absolute Space pursues to build up local aesthetical appreciation. We consider important to build up over our own traditions while eagerly advance art-promoting activities with the focus on modern art, hoping to make Absolute Space a place with local special features and global perspectives.
residencyDescription: Based on past residency experiences with artists and groups in Thailand, Japan, Denmark, Malaysia, and Vietnam, Absolute Arts Group initiates the Absolute Space AIR program in 2024.

name: Acasă la Hundorf/At home in Hundorf Association
residencyName: At home in Hundorf international artist residency
orgDescription: « At home in Hundorf » stands for a meeting point between two worlds : the community of the village back home, filled with tranquility, new meanings waiting to find the right intersections, unknown memories, steadfastness, and the artistic community, usually coming from urban areas, in need of a break from familiar places and instances, in order to be able to come back with an enhanced appetite for the artistic endeavors they conduct in the spaces of the big cities and communities amidst which they live and work. The At home in Hundorf Association, created in 2016, established as a primary goal, on the long-term, to set up a creative space that would generate concrete events and experiences as a result of the direct relation between the members of the Hundorf community and the artists in residence. This direct collaborative relationship would not be mediated by outsiders nor would it be coordinated by other artists. The two communities would set out on a journey together, in order to bridge tradition and contemporary creation, in a joint effort leading to the discovery and reinterpretation of the local heritage. The association has created, throughout its numerous activities, a widespread network of young professionals, university professors and lecturers, anthropologists, theater specialists, writers, film makers, acclaimed artists (national and international) all of whom have been directly involved, in all the years of its existence, in the growth of this programme at a national level. Currently, the „At home in Hundorf” residencies programme is one of the most important and relevant collaborative artistic initiatives in Romania leading, during its almost seven years of existence to a considerable number of partnerships with cultural institutions in the country, with well-established artists and professionals, but also individual partnerships with some of the most relevant cultural projects, initiatives and programmes in Romania (biennale, education programmes, film festivals etc.), becoming a brand in its own right and creating a professional network around this brand. Among the public institutions that have shown a constant support towards the association’s activities, we can name: the Romanian Ministry of Culture, the Romanian Cultural Institute, the National University of Arts in Bucharest, the George Enescu University of Arts in Iași, The Romanian Peasant Museum, etc.
residencyDescription: The national artistic residency « At home in Hundorf » has been taking place for six years in the village of Viișoara (Hundorf), situated in the heart of the mythical land of Transylvania, in the Mureș county. The project appeared organically, out of the need of small rural communities to find themselves and connect with the perpetual changes and challenges faced by the current urbanized world. This need of connection also entailed a search for a certain balance between the engagement in the big debates of the world and what allows these often untouched communities, to preserve their cultural essence, constituted by their multi-ethnic background typical to the geographical area they subscribe to, that has been kept intact, somehow, by the last « keepers » living in these areas.

We work collaboratively with partners to deliver affordable and secure artist studio provision, and develop pioneering residencies and awards programmes that support artists at all stages of their careers. Acme is the single largest provider of permanent affordable artist studios in England, supporting over 800 individual artists across 15 buildings in Greater London each year. name: ACOSS International AIR
orgDescription: Akos Cultural NGO was founded in 2002, Yerevan, Armenia and now it is a leading model for similar institutions internationally. In 2006 it established ACOSS AIR program in Armenia which was an artist initiation. The aim of the organization is to support the development of contemporary creativity and realizing projects by Armenian and international artists and theorists, to organizing exhibitions, conferences, discussions, researches, seminars and workshops concerning the local art, political and social situation on the background of nowadays worldwide movements. ACOSS promotes and diffuses contemporary creativity in Armenia. name: Akademie Schloss Solitude
orgDescription: Die Akademie Schloss Solitude ist ein internationales Artist-in-Residence-Programm, das seit seiner Gründung 1990 mehr als 1.700 junge Künstler*innen und Wissenschaftler*innen aus über 120 Ländern gefördert hat. Es bildet für die internationale Kunstszene ein wichtiges globales und transdisziplinäres Netzwerk. Der Name Akademie Schloss Solitude vereint den Glauben an künstlerisch-wissenschaftlichen Austausch mit dem Gedanken eines Refugiums, ein Credo, das dem Bau von Schloss Solitude von Anfang an zugrunde lag. Residenzen an der Akademie Schloss Solitude ermöglichen es Stipendiaten, sich unter günstigen materiellen und intellektuellen Bedingungen ihren Forschungsprojekten zu widmen. So können die vorhandenen Ressourcen optimal und bedarfsgerecht eingesetzt werden. Für das Selbstverständnis der Akademie Schloss Solitude ist es wesentlich, Stipendiaten aller Fachrichtungen ein Arbeiten und Forschen frei von Alltagsdruck und Abgabeterminen zu ermöglichen. Dennoch bietet die Akademie die Möglichkeit, Projekte öffentlich zu kommunizieren und zu präsentieren. Neben der Durchführung zahlreicher öffentlicher Veranstaltungen ermöglicht die Online-Präsenz der Akademie Schloss Solitude die internationale Sichtbarkeit der Stipendiaten und ihrer Projekte und schafft Raum für neue digitale Projekte. Ein Aufenthaltsstipendium an der Akademie Schloss Solitude ist auch als Investition in die Zukunft zu verstehen, da es unter Umständen erst zu einem späteren Zeitpunkt Früchte trägt, sowohl für den Stipendiaten als auch für die Institution. Die Akademie Schloss Solitude wird vom Land Baden-Württemberg finanziell unterstützt.

orgDescription: Akiyoshidai International Art Village, designed by the architect, Arata Isozaki, was founded in 1998 with the aim of providing a platform for artists in residence as well as for a variety of art forms and cultural activities. AIAV’s main hall has a capacity of approximately 300 and its residence hall can house 100, and the village also features a restaurant, seminar room, studios, gallery, and cafe. AIAV is located far away from the noise of everyday city life and is surrounded by natural resources. Isozaki himself referred to it as an “archipelago”, (an expanse of water with many scattered islands), and it consists of many different facilities. The term “village” suggests that AIAV is not a one monolithic structure but rather a collective of small neighboring buildings reminiscent of a traditional Japanese village.

The Arts Center is located in a historic Trading Post building in the rural community presently known as Homer, Alaska. Founded in 1991, Bunnell’s mission is to spark artistic inquiry, innovation, and equity to strengthen the physical, social and economic fabric of Alaska through the arts. name: All That We Are
orgDescription: All That We Are is a not-for-profit artist residency and research environment based in Tasmania. It supports artists, researchers and organisations to step outside everyday demands, reconnect with their practice, and develop new directions in their work. At its core is a simple belief: creativity has a powerful capacity to enable individuals and communities to make meaningful, life-enhancing connections — with themselves, with others, and with place. Founded and hosted by Simon Spain and Victoria Ryle, All That We Are draws on over 60 years of combined experience across the arts, education and community-led practice. The residency brings this experience into a contemporary context, integrating creative practice with environmental awareness, learning, and new models of living and working. The name reflects an approach that resists simplification. Rather than separating disciplines, roles or ways of thinking, All That We Are supports a more holistic understanding of creative life — one that values complexity, collaboration and the interdependence between people, practice and environment. Artists are invited into a lived setting: a home, a landscape, and a working practice. Time here is shaped by quiet rhythms, close attention to place, and opportunities for reflection, exchange and development. All That We Are is part of a growing international ecology of artist-led environments that explore how creative practice can inform not only what we make, but how we live.

name: Anderson Ranch Arts Center
orgDescription: Anderson Ranch Arts Center is nestled among the high peaks of the Rocky Mountains in the resort community of Snowmass Village, Colorado, 10 miles west of Aspen and 160 miles west of Denver. Formerly a turn-of-the-century working ranch, Anderson Ranch became an artists’ community over 40 years ago. In 1966, a handful of artists cleared out the historic barns for studios, set up a gallery, and began to offer classes. Since its incorporation as a nonprofit visual arts community in 1973, Anderson Ranch has matured into an internationally recognized visual arts institution. At Anderson Ranch, we recognize human beings’ lifelong need to develop personal creativity and to discover, learn and grow. Through our various programs such as our year-round workshops, community outreach, public events, exhibitions and residencies we nurture and inspire imaginations of all ages, encouraging experimentation, intensive inquiry and creative production. Anderson Ranch is an international center for the creation of new work and untried art forms for leading artists of our time.

While in residence, all artists will share in an established community of interaction, conceptual development and intense production of work. Given the staffing and facilities available at the Ranch, its artist residency program will become one of the most robust programs of its type in the United States.

name: Antrodia Energy Estate
orgDescription: 安特羅迪亞能量莊園位於台灣台中，是個致力於大自然、能量與人類對話的靜謐之地。莊園的核心在於培育珍稀的牛樟樹（Antrodia cinnamomea）及其寄主木材－珍貴的桂樹（Cinnamomum kanehirae）的保護。 作為 You Can Antrodia Biotech 生態研究的延伸，莊園精心打造了一個融合森林原始能量與精緻現代美學的場所。我們致力於透過接待探索「材料敘事」的國際藝術家，建構一個持久的能量與美學體系。莊園內設有一個獨特的“健康隱秘空間”，旨在提供沉浸式、多感官體驗，為藝術家們提供了一個難得的機會，讓他們能夠在專業的生物技術環境中運用高價值的天然材料進行創作。
residencyDescription: 該駐留計畫以材料為導向的藝術探索為核心，著重於創作過程以及蘊含於天然材料之中的敘事。位於台中市的安特羅迪亞能源園區為創作者提供了一個獨特的平台，讓他們得以接觸珍稀的樟樹（Antrodia cinnamomea）及其珍貴的寄主木材－肉桂（Cinnamomum kanehirae）。

name: Aomori Contemporary Art Centre, Aomori Public University
residencyName: Aomori Contemporary Art Centre, Aomori Public University
orgDescription: 青森公立大学附属国際芸術センター青森（ACAC）は、八甲田山麓のダイナミックな自然環境に佇む現代美術施設です。その特徴的な建築様式は、アーティスト・イン・レジデンス（AIR）、展覧会、教育・学習という3つの創造の柱に見事に調和しています。青森市制100周年記念事業として設立され、2001年12月に開館。現在は青森公立大学が運営しています。 優れた現代美術の発信と、それによる国際的なネットワークの構築、そしてアーティストと地域住民・学生との新たな出会いと学びの機会を提供することを目指しています。建築設計は、国際的に著名な建築家・安藤忠雄氏が手掛けています。安藤は、起伏に富んだ地形を崩すことなく周囲の自然環境を巧みに利用し、「見えない建築」というコンセプトに着想を得て、複合施設を森の奥深くに埋もれさせるように設計しました。ACACは、山腹に架かる橋をイメージした直線的なクリエイティブ・レジデンスホールと、ギャラリーと野外円形劇場を備えた馬蹄形の展示ホールの3つの主要な建物で構成されています。これらのユニークな建築空間は、滞在するアーティストの創造性を解き放ち、ACACは訪れるすべての人々に刺激的な新しい芸術体験を提供することを目指しています。春から秋にかけては、緑豊かな森を散策しながら、敷地内に設置された20以上の野外彫刻を鑑賞できます。
residencyDescription: ACAC（アジア芸術文化センター）は、アーティスト・イン・レジデンス（AIR）プログラムを公募しています。現代美術作家、キュレーター、研究者など、文化芸術活動に携わる方々に、展覧会、パフォーマンス、ワークショップ、トークなどの活動に向けた準備の実践機会を提供しています。これらの活動を通して、世界中からアーティストが集まり、青森の地域社会と国際交流を行う機会を提供しています。選考に選ばれたアーティストは、最長3ヶ月間ACACに滞在することができ、滞在費、渡航費、制作費が支給されます。滞在中は、リサーチと制作活動に加え、ワークショップ、トーク、共同制作、地域社会との交流プログラムなどに参加し、展覧会やパフォーマンスなど、様々な形で成果をあげることができます。ACACは、アーティスト、学生、そして地域住民が多様な交流を通して芸術体験を育む機会を提供することで、芸術教育と芸術文化の振興を目指しています。

name: Aqtushetii Residency
orgDescription: AqTushetii is a festival/residency program that fosters the arts, culture, history, and traditions of Tusheti while bringing together creatives from around the world to collaborate, create, and share knowledge Mission Statement: AqTushetii is a DIY ‘self-organised’ exchange platform. This flexible system tries to resist hierarchy and incite experimentation, in a hospitable environment that fosters autonomy towards each person that takes part. While some events are pre-organised by the co-founders of the residence, most of the happenings of the space/s are decided upon and produced by the residents themselves. Each person who steps into AqTushetii is encouraged to contribute back to the building somehow – the form and shape this takes is entirely up to the resident. This is made possible by the material and human resources available on site. If you want to see something happen: make it happen, and make it possible for others to do so too: e.g. if you need help setting up a projector or the sound for a talk you want to put on that evening; or could use a hand moving a table or installing something, etc. – ask around and do it. The residents of the building are there to help you just as you are there to help them. It is through this ethos that the building functions and produces interesting scenarios and content.
residencyDescription: Aqtushetii is a self-organized, non-profit artist residency in Georgia, founded in 2017 in Omalo, Tusheti. Set in one of Europe’s most remote mountain regions, it operates within a landscape defined by high altitude, ancient defensive architecture, and living craft traditions. The program brings together artists and researchers for independent practice, exchange, and collaboration.

name: ARCUS Project
orgDescription: ARCUS Project aims to support promising artists who engage in creative activities across the world, and also, to promote the Ibaraki area through art. This project started in 1994 as a test artist-in-residence program that was an initiative of the Ibaraki Prefectural Government. After six years of successfully running the test project period, it then began officially. By collaborating with emerging artists, curators, and prospective art managers, ARCUS Project connects the Ibaraki area with art, and encourages residents of the city of Moriya to voluntarily participate in various art projects that include exhibitions, workshops, lectures, and film screenings.

Since 2003, artists from around the world have been selected through applications from open calls and screenings.

name: ARD Art Institution
orgDescription: ARD is an art institution founded by Hana El-Beblawy in 2022 and specialized in the field of contemporary art practices within the local and international art scene. It presents a diversified program that includes many artistic activities stemming from the surrounding affairs and is open to the world. The program includes artistic residencies, exhibitions, workshops, and other art alternatives which ARD is seeking to provide as services that would contribute to effective artistic patterns in the society. It also strives for a fruitful art scene that is not constrained by the traditional standards of the art market. Our vision and goals: With its prime location in Garden City, central Cairo, ARD aspires to become a vibrant meeting point bringing together artists, cultural activists, and art institutions with a broad and extended audience through its programs of intertwined projects and activities. ARD aspires to achieve its objectives in: Filling the gap resulting from the scarce art residency programs within the Cairo art scene. Therefore, we hope, through our programs and cooperation with various institutions, to become an effective hub to provide and host programs for art residencies from all over the world. Encouraging artists to re-create, produce, and present their ambitious artistic projects, ideas, and experiences by facilitating a flexible work environment that is not subject to the common restrictions imposed by the local art market. Building a platform for artistic creativity based on cultural diversity and exchange of knowledge and experiences. Also connecting the local and international artists, as being in one place together, in parallel with the various activities taking place. Encouraging artists of the younger generation from various governorates of Egypt by providing opportunities for direct contact with the Cairo art scene. Presenting an institutional model based on an integrated economic system, as a practical alternative – and at the same time – not isolated from the history of practicing art as a profession. ARD offers, in its premises, art residencies based on research, experimenting, and producing (optional); in addition to facilitating the opportunities to exchange and network with foreign and local artists who are – staying periodically – in the art residencies programs offered by ARD. This aims to contribute to the crystallization of art as a profession.
residencyDescription: ARD International is a process-based, one-to-three month artist residency that includes talks, workshops, and exhibitions by resident practitioners.

name: Are | are-events.org
orgDescription: Are | are-events.org (ARE) is an art organisation operating in rural environment in Czechia. In order to study the problems associated with environmental grief, accelerating processes of degradation in agricultural and forest landscapes and the soil, increasing drought and extinction of animals and insects, ARE purchased a parcel of forest in the Orlické Mountains in 2019 to be used for community purposes. It aims to create a sustainable, biodiverse forest as a friendly habitat for different life forms from microorganisms, bacteria, plants, mushrooms, animals all the way to humans. One of ARE’s main activities is the Woods – Community for Cultivation, Theory, and Art project.
residencyDescription: We invite artists and researchers to apply for the 2025 residency programme as part of the Pastoral Twilight project which is held in collaboration with the organisations BAU (Italy) and Inland (Spain). The residency will relate to the specific rural location and activities of the organisation. Thematically, it will be linked by exploring the topics of pastoralism and regenerative agricultural practices and sustainable education.

name: ARE (artist Residencies Enschede)
orgDescription: Artist Residencies Enschede (ARE) has an artist-in-residence program with 6 international artists each year. Each residency period lasts 3 months, during which artists can focus on their work and process, as well as collaborate on projects with cultural organizations, local artists, and/or communities in and around Enschede. At the end of the residency, the artists present their work and process to the public. ARE is a funded residency that provides free housing and studio space, access to a variety of tools and media equipment, and a work budget. Travel expenses and living costs not included. Facilities: During the residency, each guest artist has access to a private studio with their own sleeping area, kitchen, living, and working space. Within the building, artists also have access to a washing machine and dryer, and the studios are equipped with basic utensils, cooking equipment, linens, and other essentials for comfortable living. Additionally, artists are provided with a bicycle for the duration of their residency. As the building is standalone, guest artists can work day and night. Artists have access to basic tools, power tools, and media equipment during the residency, including a jigsaw, drill, sewing machine, projectors, and photo and video cameras. Additionally, there is a work budget available for each artist of €750 for materials or project related costs. Location: ARE is located in the building of art initiative B93. The artists of B93 work in this building and ARE rents two studios with living spaces. The studios are 700 meters from the city center and 1.3 kilometers from the central train station. Although the residency is in an urban setting, you can reach various landscapes, including meadows, wooded areas, and water-rich regions, within a 10-minute bike ride. Enschede has an active and vibrant art scene, with visual art, sound art, digital culture, and crossovers.
residencyDescription: ARE’s artist-in-residence program brings together professional artists from diverse cultures and societies, where artists work for three months in relation to the local community and environment.

Part of this dream was to develop an art residency for emerging or mid-career artists from anywhere in the world.
residencyDescription: Set in the pre-alps of the Ligurian region of Italy, the Arroscia Valley offers the artist a quiet retreat in which to conduct their research and work, while offering quick access to cosmopolitan cities. The Arroscia Residency is located 25 minutes from the Italian Riviera, 45 minutes from a ski resort, and 1 hour from France and Monaco. Six international airports within 1.5 to 4 hours drive provide easy access to European hubs: Nice, Genoa, Turin, Pisa, Florence, and Milan. name: Art Center Ongoing
orgDescription: Art Center Ongoing is a compact art complex with a gallery, library, and café, which opened in January 2008 and has introduced numerous artists with the idea of “a place where ongoing experimental forms of expression can be pursued. Since 2013, we have also been involved in an artist-in-residence program and continued to actively build a network with the international art scene. In addition to exhibitions, we have held various events such as talks, performances, and workshops, aiming to create a place where a diverse range of people can gather around the arts. However, social and global conditions have changed dramatically since the opening, and we find ourselves confronted daily with a variety of problems that are difficult to solve. In such circumstances, it may be time for Art Center Ongoing to change its role and direction. As an independent art space, there is no doubt that there is much that we can do. What can art do for us now? We would like to continue to search for an ongoing answer to this big question from a small art complex, with all those who believe in art.
residencyDescription: Ongoing AIR is a residency program launched by Art Center Ongoing in April, 2013. Domestic / overseas artists and curators are all welcome to join the 2-month residency program where the Art Center offers an accommodation and an exhibition opportunity at Art Center Ongoing.

name: Pushkinskaya-10 art center / St. Petersburg Art Residency (SPAR)
orgDescription: The art center Pushkinskaya-10 is a collective work of art, a monument to the victory of free culture over conformist Soviet ideology, and the country’s sole example of an independent and self-organized artist commune. It started in 1989 when a group of underground artists occupied a large building in the center of Leningrad and was later transformed into a multidisciplinary art center. During the thirty years of its existence, Pushkinskaya-10 has become a point of interest for local and international artists and collectives, and it continues to generate creative energy within its walls. Today the art center with a total area of over 4 500 sq. m. is home to a museum, archive, galleries, clubs, studios of artists and musicians, an international residency program, and other creative spaces.
residencyDescription: The St. Petersburg Art Residency (SPAR) was founded in 2012 and became the city’s first residency program. It is located in the historical center of St. Petersburg in the Pushkiankays-10 art center, offering the participants a unique experience of living and working in a lively creative surrounding next to studios of local artists and musicians, independent galleries, a museum center and concert venues.

name: Art Commune International Artist-in-Residence Program
orgDescription: The “Art Commune” international artist-in-residence program is a significant hub in the field of contemporary art of Armenia both locally and internationally. The goal of the “Art Commune” is to create an intellectual space where the residents will get the chance to penetrate the local cultural and socio-political contexts, as well as to combine their artistic practices (research, production, etc.) with meetings, seminars, lectures, and other discursive events with local and international artists, cultural experts, critics, and curators. The program has evolved to include a residency, and the Platform FemLab The FemLab is an open platform that welcomes international critics, curators, scholars, and artists to conduct their research and studies on gender and feminist issues and create their own works independently or in collaboration with local feminist and queer activists, scholars and artists. In addition, the platform is directed toward developing a kind of context which is oriented towards community-based projects, producing situations, processes, and collective work within studio and post-studio practices. As of the fall of 2017, the “”Art Commune” has partnered with AGBU Armenia, a major stakeholder and strategic supporter of cultural projects in Armenia. This new partnership allows residency participants to connect with a larger international platform through AGBU various facilities and extensive global network of different professionals.
residencyDescription: The major cluster of the “Art Commune”Residency Program is located at the AGBU Vahe Karapetian Centre. The centre consists of a newly constructed residence that houses a consortium of artist residency programs, as well as international and regional students studying in Yerevan, Armenia. The centre is equipped with single and double rooms with access to shared and private bathrooms, laundry and cleaning services. All residents have access to shared facilities like industrial-sized kitchen, a reading room, library, and table tennis for entertainment and social exchange. The centre has 24/7 security and reception service from 10-5pm.

name: Art-Residence of Bishkek School of Contemporary Art “Bulbul”
orgDescription: The Bishkek School of Contemporary Art (BiSCA) is a socially engaged art platform that offers to accumulate and promote art practices, reflections and experiences in their various manifestations, both at the level of mediums and at the level of artistic decisions / gestures / acts. Our platform works on the principle of circulation, accumulation, formation of “knowledge” about art, creation of a space for communication, interchange, and, possibly, but not necessarily, will contribute to the development of a methodological and theoretical basis, the creation of archival space and practices for the implementation of contemporary art in Kyrgyzstan and beyond. We are an informal, self-organizing association that is interested in exchanging thoughts, emotions and energy in connection with art as a practice. We are involved in the creation of our School for free. We do not have the resources, premises and infrastructure for physical events and the ability to be a point in the city. However, we have like-minded people, accumulated experience and a small team, as well as the possibilities of the Internet and virtual communication. Participants and initiators of the Bishkek School of Contemporary Art have different experiences, areas of interest and activities, however, we are all united by an interest in art in its various manifestations. Some of the representatives of the school adhere to feminist, Marxist, ecological views, and we think it is important to indicate this here. There are 9 actively involved people in the creation of the School program and its functioning, including contemporary artists-curators-researchers have been working in this sphere for the last 10 years, architects, designers, musicians and others. Since the establishment of the School in autumn 2020 we have held several exhibitions, research, festivals and interventions, residencies, educational programs, a series of lectures, artist talks, meetings and open discussions with artists, workers of culture, specialists in different areas both online and offline. We also published 8 issues of the “Aralash” zine (on various topics: pandemic, ecology, culture and politics, museum of participation) in the form of exhibition catalogue, journal and study book. One of the important events in the life of the BiSCA collective in 2022 is participation in the documenta fifteen contemporary art exhibition (Kassel, Germany) in the space of the Gudskul collective and Gudskul Study Kolektif educational program as part of the La Tabebh collective. More information about our collective can be found here: Web-site: https://bishci.com/ Telegram: https://t.me/bishci Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/bishkek_art_school/
residencyDescription: Bulbul was opened in 2023 in the village of Besh-Kungei, just 15 minutes from Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan. The residency is curated by artist Syinat Zholdosheva and her husband, Ruslan Ismailov, together with the founders of the Bishkek School of Contemporary Art (BiSCA).

name: artanywayresidency
orgDescription: The idea was to create a space for creating art that is different in an ecological environment. This idea came from traveling, accumulating experiences and ideas since 1996 until now, which is more than 29 years of traveling and working abroad, both in Asia and Europe. Each trip aims to create art and exhibit with artists in the participating countries. These experiences made us understand that traveling can create good experiences in creating art, but it still takes time to develop and create more work. Although short trips encourage us to think quickly and produce pieces to present, the work may not be as perfect as when we work in familiar areas. However, this is an interesting experience because we experience cultures, people’s ways of thinking, food, and politics, and ways of life that are different from what we are used to. These experiences are the starting point of the idea that developing oneself in a new area should take time and be open to experience the atmosphere, culture, and people of that place. These ideas have led to the specific vision of ARTANYWAY Residency, which is defined as a space for Retreat, Relax, Recover and Recharge. These four key words are the guidelines that will allow the artists who stay to have new experiences: release, rethink and exchange. We aim to provide new experiences to the artists who stay. I believe that opening up the space within our minds and brains will allow for more diverse ideas and creations. This is the main principle that defines the personality of ARTANYWAY, which is connected to nature, openness and reciprocity.
residencyDescription: Art For Self-Growth And Learning At ARTANYWAY : A New Experience From Traveling In Different Areas These ideas have led to the specific vision of ARTANYWAY Residency, which is defined as a space for Retreat, Relax, Recover and Recharge. These four key words are the guidelines that will allow the artists who stay to have new experiences: release, rethink and exchange. We aim to provide new experiences to the artists who stay. I believe that opening up the space within our minds and brains will allow for more diverse ideas and creations. This is the main principle that defines the personality of ARTANYWAY, which is connected to nature, openness and reciprocity. name: Art Center Botopasi
orgDescription: ARTCEB is an Art Centre in Botopasi, a small village in the interior of Suriname, Carribean South America. ARTCEB hosts an international residency program to demonstrate its commitment to enhancing artistic production through cultural exchange. ARTCEB, the platform for progressive art exchange, is supported by the Sepu foundation and working closely together with artist run initiative ARTOTS The Netherlands. ARTCEB, a non-profit organisation, is working to widen artistic production possibilities outside the traditional institutional framework. It is available as a residency for artists and as a location for workshops, exhibitions and conferences. Through art ARTCEB wants people to see possibilities and open their minds for cultural and social developments and to preserve the local artistic heritage in the interior of Suriname. Therefore we encourage local art education by developing cultural activities in cooperation with schools and artists. Strategy and working method Development and execution of educational art projects. Collecting and presenting contemporary art. Offer working-, housing- and exhibition facilities. Initiate, maintain and extend collaborations We do that by Artists in residence Exhibitions and events Putting together an art collection and to lend out art Educational programmes Assignments Seminars and lectures ARTCEB moved into the first experimental phase in November – December 2011. Various types of creative activity and diverse creative practices, from exhibitions and performances to lectures, symposia and international art residencies were tested and implemented. The experimental character of this phase foresees both long-term projects and spontaneous activities. They were carried out both by the members of the local artist community, as well as artists and curators working outside Botopasi. There will be an on-going search for the ideal model for using the residency.
residencyDescription: The residency is non-prescriptive allowing the artist to develop work in response to the environment. The selected artists will reside in Botopasi for a period between four weeks and three months. ARTCEB’s residency program offers visual artists a critical and practical support for the development of new work and exhibition opportunities.

name: Fundación ArteSumapaz
orgDescription: Artists Residency Intentional Community Reforestation project Art Park Exhibition center ArteSumapaz is located on 152 fanegadas (98 hectares, or 242 acres). The property is located in the municipality of San Bernardo, Cundinamarca. In most recent years, the property had been used as a cow farm, although historically the farm was part of a larger coffee plantation. The program was initiated in 2019 by co-founders Pedro Crump and Ric Dragon. Each of the parts of the center complements the activities of the other parts. The residencies expose students to the thinking of international artists, while the community creates a backbone of social continuity. In turn, members of the local community participate in and benefit from the activities of the school and residency. ArteSumapaz is focused on the arts as its principal mission. Also see, our statement of values and mission, and our manifesto.
residencyDescription: ArteSumapaz is a non-profit arts and culture nonprofit organization located on a magical piece of terrain in the Andean mountains, about four hours outside Bogotá. The artist residency program (AIR) is designed for visual artists, musicians, writers, architects, clay artists, performers, and other makers. It is a self-directed residency, where artists have full access to studio spaces of all kinds (visual art, music, movement, writing, etc.) throughout the vast and beautiful campus that includes a natural park in process of about 230 acres. Artists are given the space, freedom, and encouragement to explore and experiment with their work. The artists are welcome to participate in weekly “open critique” sessions (group discussions about their work), to share workshops or exhibitions with ArteSumapaz’s artist community or the communities of nearby towns as San Bernardo Cundinamarca and Pandi.

name: arteventura
orgDescription: Arteventura is an ecological artist’s residency on a wooded estate of 25 hectares, deep in the Spanish inland. A philosophy of autonomy and back to basics form the foundation of the project. The whole 25 ha – with its hills, the spring, the holm- and cork oaks – is at the disposal of the artists. Arteventura offers silence, space and time to engage in research and development, or create new and adventurous work. Not only, does the finca – Spanish for “rural estate” – offer its literal spaces, but the interaction with nature and the desire for autonomy of the estate is also meant to be inspiring for all residents. There are maximum 4 artists at any given moment in time (except groups). Each resident has its own selfcatering apartment, set up as a flexible working area. There are 2 individual flats of ±40 m2 for a single artist and 1 two-bedroom apartment that can be used by a single artist (bedroom + workspace), or by a duo that wants to work on a joint project. The communal studio of 300 m2 consist of an inside and outside working area.
residencyDescription: For whom? For anyone who is professionally involved with art. This could be a single artist, a duo or a group that wants to work on a joint project. A visual artist, a writer, a musician, a performer, an architect,… for those who are looking for quietude and emptiness.

name: arthereistanbul
orgDescription: arthereistanbul is an art center founded in 2014 in Istanbul, Turkey. It is situated in Rasimpasa, a vibrant and growing neighborhood of Kadik0y on the Asian side of Istanbul. Rasimpasa has seen significant changes over the last few years and particularly the emergence of a new art scene (artists studios, galleries and cafes). arthereistanbul is an artist-run center, which is comprised of a studio, an art gallery and a cafe, and is led by artists and arts professionals from Syria, Turkey and France. The center gathers artists from all over the world and particularly the Middle East and Turkey. The primary target of arthereistanbul was to provide a space for Syrian newcomers, responding to their need for a place to continue their artistic practice and (re)create artistic and social networks. Now our center continues to function as a shelter for displaced Syrian artists, and has also evolved into a local open cultural hub for the neighborhood. arthereistanbul is an interdisciplinary and collaborative working space where artists, curators, researchers or arts professionals can develop their projects, connect, and be in touch with the particular diversity of the neighborhood and Istanbul. Thus arthereistanbul hosts artists working in diverse artistic fields such as visual arts, music, performing arts, writing etc. We also organize special artistic events and exhibitions, and collaborate with local and international festivals. We sometimes invite professionals to give workshops and training in art management or curating. It also a co-working coffee space as a meeting point, where people from the neighborhood, freelancers, visitors, come, sit, chat, work, or simply rest. It is an open space where different people pass by, meet, and come back. It is meant to be a space for encounter and for multicultural exchange.
residencyDescription: arthereistanbul, a multicultural space located at the crossing-bridge between Europe and Asia Istanbul is often considered as one of the Art Cities of the Future: a city rich a vibrant and vital art scene, connected both to Europe and Asia, while also relating to the Middle-East. The city is often seen as a bridge between the East and the West, a cosmopolitan space where hundreds of cultures coexist.

name: Artist and Researcher in Residence Guiniguada – Canary Islands
residencyName: Artist and Researcher in Residence Guiniguada – Canary Islands
orgDescription: Exceptional artist / researcher resident / guest community, or solitude if you please, in a bold vast space that invites for musing, far away from heavy civilization and buzzing crowds, and still within easy reach, in an unconquerable castle, a landscape straight out of a fairy-tale, in one of the world’s best climates by common consensus. Las Palmas, the capital city is easily accessible, where the culture of the three continents meet: Europe, Africa and Latin-America. Historical, acheological, art and conteporary art museums and various off-grid venues, festivals, carnevals, concerts offer a rich cultural experience. The natural monuments of the volcanic landscape meeting the ocean, the unique endemic flora and fauna are also our main attractions. Our valley is located in the north of the island (not affected by mass tourism), with a mainly agricultural / recreational profile. We are not about consumer comfort; those who like to stay with us prefer to get one step closer to nature – both their own physique and the outside, non-artificial environment – and are not wary of adventure. Yes, this is a rural setting, neighbours live here, cut the branches, the dogs do bark, also there are goats and roosters, even an owl you can hear at times! In order to be able to slow down life, we believe it is worth breaking our routines from time to time – this is why artist-in-residencies have spread as a way of enhancing creativity through (re)settling our minds. Our idea was that the notion of the AIR could be expanded by not having artists exclusively at the specific location, but enabling them to mix with academic researchers. We believe heterogeneity always helps, thus, the more people could broaden their comprehensions of their worlds, the better for humankind! This is why we start our venture in this house, not for too many persons, and not for too few. Our goal is to host, in this hybridised form of staying, people who are ready to leave the routines of their home behind and spend time in our company thinking, working, relaxing, discussing in our house. Run by an art historian and a social researcher, living on the same venue.
residencyDescription: The programme runs all year round (spring, summer, autumn and winter periods).

name: Artist Retreat in the wilds of Celtic Cornwall
residencyName: Artist Retreat in the wilds of Celtic Cornwall
orgDescription: This artist retreat and residency is run by practising artist Wendy Rolt who also has a studio nearby. The vision is share the quiet and vibrant space where nature is full and breathing all around you. It asks you to slow down and value your process and self. There is much to sit with and be inspired by. The farmhouse is over 400 years old and like many of the local buildings made in granite. Wendy has spent years renovating the small farm dwelling so there is now water and electricity throughout and it is habitable too but still has the same magical feeling of old. The residency is run as a grass roots small and private organisation and is a way of earning money to keep the place ticking over whilst also remaining close to its creative roots. Rather than making money though holiday lets as much of Cornwall does Wendy believes that the artist is sacred and needs deep time and space and nature and so has chosen to make this a place that flourishes with artists and making. Cornwall has so much of its history in the arts from the Celts to Peter Lanyon and this artist residency continues to carry the torch.
residencyDescription: This celtic and Cornish residency offers you the quiet spaciousness to still and be and let what comes up be felt while also tussling for your attention are the many ancient natural forms within reaching distance. Huge granite rocks, part of the Cornelian Massif, surround you and invite you to climb up and sit on them remembering the gift of life and time. The temperate rainforest calls you with its streams and woven tree trunks. The Saints Way, an ancient celtic path from north to south of Cornwall, winds below and takes you to Helmon Tor or the local pub, open daily. The wild life carries on around you as rarely disturbed deer take their breakfast contently while owls fly across to remind you dawn and dusk have come. It is a place to become small and gaze in wonder at all that is alive and the brightest stars above.

name: Artistic Residency: In process
orgDescription: ”In process” is an independent, community-rooted residency program based in Guarapuava, Brazil, founded to support the artistic production and visibility of underrepresented groups, including women, LGBTQIA+ people, Black, Indigenous, and deaf artists. With a strong emphasis on collaborative processes and public engagement, the residency promotes intersectional practices that center identity, resistance, and belonging as core themes. We operate with hybrid formats, integrating in-person creation with online mentoring and documentation, aiming to foster sustainable, accessible, and culturally situated forms of artistic exchange. Our work is grounded in pedagogical experimentation and philosophical inquiry, especially through the use of a creative observation tool based on Charles Peirce’s semiotics. With support from the Art Department of the State University of the Center-West (UNICENTRO), the Municipal Secretariat of Culture of Guarapuava and the State Secretariat of Culture of Paraná , this project strengthens the commitment to the democratization of access to art, the appreciation of diversity and the strengthening of the regional creative economy.
residencyDescription: The residency provides a 15-week program combining collective workshops, artist talks, peer mentorship, and a final exhibition (physical and virtual). It supports artists in developing new work connected to personal and collective experiences of social tension, cultural identity, and political resistance. The program is free to selected artists and includes accessibility tools such as LIBRAS (Brazilian Sign Language), audio description, and inclusive materials.

name: ARTS 14C
orgDescription: ARTS 14C operates a 125,000 sq ft (11,613 sq m) facility in the Powerhouse Arts District of downtown Jersey City, New Jersey, 5-minutes from New York City. Originally built in 2020 to house a university dormitory, the space now serves as an arts incubator, furnished artist live/work residency and exhibition and performance venue. The building is the landmarked former warehouse for the Atlantic & Pacific Tea Company, and ARTS 14C occupies three entire floors, plus a 5,000 sq ft gallery on another floor. Being in an urban setting, we invite the public into the space on a regular basis – with open studio events, exhibitions and performances, allowing our resident artists to build an audience and mailing list. We also invite arts professionals into the space each week to meet with our artists, and offer frequent field trips to the cultural offerings of the area.
residencyDescription: ARTS 14C offers both free and subsidized residencies for artists of all disciplines – short-term project-based residencies and long-term development based residencies.

name: Arxiu Comarcal de l’Urgell (ACUR)
orgDescription: The Arxiu Comarcal de l’Urgell (ACUR) was created in 1982, following an agreement signed between the Department of Culture and the Tàrrega Town Hall. In 1986 its new headquarters were opened in the old part of the town, and it joined the Network of Regional Archives of the Generalitat de Catalonia. The Archive is the custodian of public and private (from institutions, families or individuals) documentation collections, both old and modern, that exist in various formats (such as photographs, films, letters, maps, posters, printed material…etc.) on various supports (parchment scrolls, paper, glass, plastic, digital media, etc). ACUR’s basic mission is to collect, treat, preserve, conserve, diffuse and assess the area’s public and private documentation heritage. And also, to facilitate documentation access and consultation so as to respond to citizen rights and public administration functions. In the field of cultural action, ACUR promotes facilitating, creating and diffusing ideas through publications, courses, exhibitions, and reusing their contents. name: Associaltion BeArtz
orgDescription: BeArtz is a non-profit organization dedicated to offering residencies and workshops for artists from around the world, at any stage of their creative journey—whether they are seasoned professionals or beginners. For many individuals with intellectual backgrounds, the need for creative play and a retreat space is essential. Vacations are not only about relaxation, but also about rediscovering the value of play. Our organization provides a nurturing environment where artists can explore their unique paths and creative expression. Located in the enchanting medieval village of Sauveterre de Béarn, on the Camino de Santiago de Compostela, our residency offers a one-of-a-kind experience. The village’s breathtaking medieval buildings, castles, and towers create a stunning backdrop, while the panoramic views of the surrounding nature leave a lasting impression. The location, in the south-west of France, offers a mild microclimate near the Pyrenees Mountains, the Atlantic Ocean, and the Gave Rivers, as well as proximity to Spain. At BeArtz, we provide a unique opportunity to live and work in a 1,000-year-old fortified castle with a five-story tower accessed by a stone spiral staircase. Surrounded by awe-inspiring skies and nature, artists can experience both tranquility and inspiration. We maintain an intimate atmosphere, limiting the number of residents to a maximum of eight, with a focus on providing dedicated studio space for five working artists. The project’s main developer, Magdalena, was inspired by Ballinglen in Ireland, where an artist residency and workshop space was founded in a rural village and continues to thrive. Prior to moving to southwest France, Magdalena ran workshops in Paris. With degrees in Fine Art and Design, as well as in Psychology, she is passionate about holistic living, sustainability, and local food production—values that are integral to the organization. In addition to founding BeArtz, she has collaborated with local artists to create a non-profit aimed at fostering a community space where artists can work, learn, and share their experiences with the local community. Furthermore, BeArtz emphasizes eco-conscious practices, such as recycling materials in building and renovation projects. Through this organization, we invite creatives from around the world to immerse themselves in a supportive, collaborative environment that encourages artistic growth, connection, and community engagement.
residencyDescription: The primary goal of the BeArtz residency is to provide you with a space to reconnect with yourself and to create an incubatory environment that nurtures your personal and artistic growth. The main building, a centuries-old castle with thick, sturdy walls, embodies the essence of the BeArtz name—where being is just as important as doing, and creativity flows naturally within the embrace of the space. Here, we offer a supportive atmosphere, primarily led by Magdalena, with assistance from local artists and team members.

Whether you’re deep in a manuscript, exploring new ideas, or simply needing time to reconnect with your voice, Bara Skriv provides an environment where your writing comes first. Lily brings her background in writing, critiquing, and creative practice to each retreat, creating an atmosphere that is gentle, inclusive, and free of pressure. While the weather is unpredictable, even in summer, you can be sure of the wind. name: Bored Peach Club
orgDescription: Bored Peach Club is an artist-led platform dedicated to supporting contemporary artistic practice through residencies, workshops, and public programming. Rooted in care, experimentation, and collaboration, the organization creates conditions for artists to develop work over time while engaging critically with their surroundings and peers. At the core of Bored Peach Club’s activity are its residency programs, which provide artists with time, space, and curatorial support to research, produce, and reflect. These residencies emphasize process over output, encouraging risk-taking, dialogue, and meaningful exchange between local and international practitioners. Alongside residencies, Bored Peach Club organizes its “boring workshops,” a series of hands-on and discursive sessions that focus on practical skills, artistic methodologies, and critical thinking. These workshops are designed to demystify artistic processes, foster peer learning, and strengthen professional sustainability for artists at different stages of their practice. Public engagement is further developed through exhibitions and events hosted at the Brewhouse. These exhibitions function as sites of encounter where artistic research is shared with wider audiences, often presenting works-in-progress or outcomes from residencies and workshops. By activating the Brewhouse as a cultural space, Bored Peach Club bridges artistic experimentation with community engagement. Through these interconnected activities, Bored Peach Club supports artists holistically while contributing to a vibrant and inclusive cultural ecosystem that values depth, process, and long-term impact.

name: Nancy B. Negley Artist Residency program
orgDescription: The Nancy B. Negley Artists Residency Program, based at the Dora Maar House in Ménerbes, France, hosts residencies of one to two months for mid-career professionals in the arts and humanities to concentrate on their fields of expertise. Conceived in 2006 by Mrs. Negley, the program has an international reputation as one of the most respected residency for people working in the arts and humanities. Our Fellows—which included artists, poets, novelists, playwrights, filmmakers, historians, curators, performers and scholars from a wide range of fields—immersed themselves in the creative aspects of their work and engaged with their peers and community through cultural activities and events. Located in Ménerbes, one of the most beautiful villages in France, this 18th century town house was the property of General-Baron Robert (1772-1831), a native of Ménerbes who received numerous honors during the Napoleonic wars in Spain, and was bought in 1944 by Dora Maar, surrealist artist and photographer. Companion and muse of Picasso from the late 1930s to the early 1940s, following their breakup Dora spent each summer in solitude in Ménerbes. After her death in 1997, an American arts patron, Nancy Brown Negley, bought and renovated the house to make it a retreat for writers, academics and artists.

name: Caetani Centre
orgDescription: The Caetani Centre is the former home of renowned artist, writer, mentor and teacher Sveva Caetani. Sveva Caetani was a visionary figure in the North Okanagan community with a deep belief in the power of art, culture, and the pursuit of knowledge to enrich and change lives and cultivate community. Sveva left her 1.3 acres of gardens and historic home to the City of Vernon (British Columbia, Canada) in 1994 with the express wish that it serve as a community cultural facility for artistic and critical exploration. Now open to the public, the Caetani Centre is available for both guided and self-guided heritage tours. Visitors can learn about the fascinating royal Italian Caetani family history and story and see select displays of treasured family artifacts in the heritage home. The mysterious and heartbreaking story behind the history of the house and its inhabitants provides a gateway to understanding our recent past, and opens a window to a much different world, shedding light on the many artworks and writings created by our benefactor Sveva Caetani. In the art gallery, for part of each year selections of Sveva Caetani’s heralded and stunning Recapitulation painting series, are on exhibit, having recently returned permanently to the Caetani Centre after 35 years of being held by the Alberta Foundation for the Arts. Sveva’s vision for her home has become reality and is now being carried out through creative and thought-provoking programming. The Caetani Centre also provides a venue for visual artists from around Canada and the world to explore a diverse range of arts practices, theories and experiences through our Self-Directed Artist-in-Residency Program for visual artists, writers, curators, and creative individuals.
