name: Casa Lü Parque Artist Residency
residencyName: Casa Lü Parque Art Residency in Mexico City
orgDescription: Casa Lü is a visual arts residency program in Mexico City founded in 2017. The program supports artists by combining time and space for independent work with structured feedback, peer dialogue, cultural excursions, studio visits, and engagement with members of the local art community. The name “Lü” comes from Tibetan and means “body,” reminding us that life is temporary. Casa Lü offers artists a temporary home where they can focus on their work, engage with a new context, and explore new creative directions. Since its founding, Casa Lü has hosted more than 700 artists from over 40 countries. The residency is conducted in English and brings together an international community of artists working across visual arts and interdisciplinary practices. Casa Lü has been featured in residency guides and cultural publications, including ArtConnect, Art Residency Guide, and Coolhunter MX, as part of their coverage of art residencies in Mexico City and internationally. Casa Lü offers two Mexico City residency formats. Casa Lü Parque is the more immersive shared-house format, designed for artists whose work develops through proximity, exchange, urban context, and experimentation. Its central location and smaller scale create a close cohort dynamic, making it especially suited for artists who want daily interaction and direct engagement with Mexico City’s cultural life to influence the development of their work. The Residency Includes Private room with ensuite bathroom Studio space, with shared and private studio options available Logistical and technical support from the Casa Lü team Weekly meetings with Casa Lü hosts and fellow residents Organized visits to galleries, museums, artist studios, and cultural spaces Feedback sessions with invited members of Mexico City’s art community Group exhibition with an opening reception Funding and Scholarships Casa Lü offers partial scholarship support to accepted artists who request financial assistance. Scholarships are applied directly as a reduction of the residency fee. Additional support is available for artists who were born and currently live in Latin America. Many residents also secure support through cultural ministries, arts councils, universities, foundations, or private organizations. Once admitted, Casa Lü provides an official acceptance letter to support external funding applications. Requesting funding does not affect acceptance. Application Information Applications are open year-round. A portfolio is required, and there is no application fee. Applicants are selected based on the strength of their work, the clarity of their artistic direction, and their potential to benefit from Casa Lü’s structured residency environment. name: Casa Na Ilha
orgDescription: Casa Na Ilha Art Residency Program is based in the island of Ilhabela, Brazil. The Residency Program is an initiative born from the idea of artists from different disciplines to create a space where creativity is encouraged, focusing in the construction of the creative process, development and curatorial process of artistic and environmental engaged projects in one place away from the city and distractions of daily routine. THE ISLAND Casa na Ilha Art Residency Program takes place in the island of Ilhabela, at the north coast of the state of Sao Pablo, Brazil. Located at 200 km from the city of Sao Pablo, is the largest island of an archipelago formed of this and other of minor dimension. Ilhabela is an ecological paradise, covered by Mata Atlantica (atlantic rainforest) home of unique fauna and flora, with more than 73 beaches and 27 waterfalls of cristalin pure water, the highest mountains are held here. Being a unique ecological ambience, and harboring various endangered species, 84% of the island is a preservation area, protected by the Parque Estadual Ilhabela. The preservation area is also home of the Caicaras, the native community of the region. Caicaras are today a sustainable community still keeping their own tradition and ancient skills. The community is nowadays facing danger of losing their land because of economic growth and interest and local and national organization are helping them keeping their land and way of life. They fish with their own nets and with harpoon to feed their families as well as being their main economic income. The traditional know-how of is one of the main intangible assets of Ilhabela. The island has a rich historical background, from the original indigenous people, Portuguese colonization and settlers, sugar cane fazendas, African influences and English pirates. There is a variety of legends and stories from each place in the island originated in the history of the island and confluence of cultures. Being the largest island in Brazil, it is only populated on one coast, the one facing mainland, and it has 45.000 habitants that live permanently. The rest of the island is national park and protected. There are no high constructions. There is one main road that goes from the south to the north, has two main centers: Pereque, the commercial center where you can find several banks, big supermarkets, paint shops, small art shop, as well as other stores and Vila, the historical center, which was the first center when the island was colonized and still has historical buildings. There is also a museum and a small art gallery, as well as local crafts shops and restaurants, cafes and convenient stores. Beaches are all around the island, urbanized and deserted. Some of them are only reachable by trails, boat or 4×4 vehicles. There are many trails in the island and the walks put yourself in direct contact with nature. Waterfalls can be reached by different trails, of all levels of difficulty. In many of the waterfall you can swim in the natural pools formed by the rocks. It is also possible to hike up to the highest peak of the island, called Baepi, with a guide. The coast also counts with several shipwrecks that can be explored. THE HOUSE Casa Na Ilha Residency programs runs in a house built by an artist above the sea level. It is 800 metres from the beach and 4 km away from the island historical center and town, Is emplaced in the middle of the rainforest on the top of a hill, surrounded with nature and a breathtaking view to the ocean, beach, palm trees and mountains. Located north in the island, the house is walking distance from the beach and waterfalls. The absolute peace and tranquility of the place are perfect for feeding inspiration and disconnection with the world today that generally cause blockages between the artist and their work. Close to natural waterfalls, a garden full of flowers, trees, orchards, and spring water supplies, birds and ocean sounds, creates the perfect environment to relax the mind and focus on projects. To get to town, the bus runs every 30/40 minutes and the stop is a few meters away from the house. It is also possible to reach it walking beach side as well as biking. The house has a main studio and several shared working spaces, indoor and outdoor, as well as gardens and deck. Artists can set the working space they feel most comfortable in any of the places and can be used at any time during the day or night. The private rooms have space for working privately (unless you are working with large scale projects, please contact us) An indoor shared studio for artists to work and develop their projects is on the main floor. The studio is full of windows that look right into the ocean and beach. The studio has a small deck and outdoor area for artists that likes working outside as well as a small covered patio. Also, a general shared indoor area where artists read, work and get together, and an outdoor gallery and deck space surrounding the house as well as an open work area. Gardens are also used as workspace depending on artist’s projects. The house has a front main garden and others that goes up and down the house where some artists love to work in the nature. The studio has its own bathroom as well as places inside and outside to place your materials. There is a space for painters or installations, where you can work freely and with a sink to wash your brushes, rugs and materials.
residencyDescription: Casa Na Ilha is an artist in residence program initiative born from the idea to create a space where creativity and exploration is encouraged, focusing in the construction of the creative process, development and curatorial process of artistic and environmental engaged projects in one place away from the city and distractions of daily routine. Our main art residence home and multidisciplinary program is located in Ilhabela Island, emplaced in the special and unique Mata Atlantica (Atlantic forest) ecosystem, off the coast of São Paulo, Brazil. Here, at our main space, we run each month the multidisciplinary artist in residence program as well as the writing and workshop sessions. Since we opened our doors in 2017, we have hosted over 300 international artists that have expanded their practice, deep dive in their creative processes, work on new ideas as well as conducted field research and ecologically engaged projects away from daily distractions, engaging between them and the local community and culture. While our physical heart and ongoing sessions remain firmly rooted in Ilhabela, Casa Na Ilha has expanded its vision to develop new itinerant, nomadic immersion programs. This expansion allows us to branch out from our main island base and venture into other fragile habitats across South America. Embracing the spirit of a nomadic platform, we invite creators to step into different ecosystems, cultures, and landscapes to observe, decenter the gaze, and dive into deep introspection in the Amazon Rainforest as well as in Patagonia Argentina. By maintaining our steady center in Ilhabela while opening these new doors across the continent, Casa Na Ilha offers creators the rare luxury of absolute peace, time, and geographic exploration. It is an invitation to be both rooted and nomadic—to coexist within different natural habitats and turn deep environmental observation into a vital instrument for artistic transformation.

name: Center for Contemporary Arts
orgDescription: The mission of the Center for Contemporary Arts is to encourage, empower, and inspire artists, children, and the community through the arts. The Center fulfills its mission through three main programs: Exhibitions, ArtReach, and ArtWalk, a quarterly Downtown arts festival. The Center was founded in 1989 with the support of the Abilene Cultural Affairs Council to provide enriching and educational experiences for the region’s communities through the promotion and support of artists. The Center has its roots in an artists’ collective called The Artists League of Texas. The brainchild of photographer Bill Wright and local arts supporter Lynn Barnett, the League began in 1984 and provided a place in Abilene where artists could work, commune, inspire and present their works. Several of the original members of the League remain active Members of The Center for Contemporary Arts. Five years after it began, with a desire to expand their space and their influence, the group formed the not for-profit corporation, The Center for Contemporary Arts. In 1993, the Board of Trustees renovated an historic building located in the downtown cultural district into classrooms, artist’s studios, and created 4,653 square feet of gallery space. In 2002 additional renovations provided improved traffic flow, more visually stimulating galleries and ADA compliance. Since then, the Center has continued to serve the Abilene community as a vibrant nonprofit organization committed to fostering the creation, appreciation, and experience of contemporary visual arts. The Center features multiple galleries with rotating exhibitions, studios for working artists, and a variety of educational programs for all ages. Through exhibitions, workshops, and community events, the Center serves as a hub for cultural engagement, supporting local and regional artists while enriching the lives of visitors and the broader community.
residencyDescription: We are excited to announce the inaugural cycle of the Texas Art Residency, a juried program designed to support emerging visual artists. This residency offers a unique opportunity to focus on your creative practice in a dynamic and supportive environment, culminating in an 8-week exhibition at the Center for Contemporary Arts in Abilene, Texas. We invite artists working in painting, printmaking, sculpture, installation, fiber, and new media to apply for this special inaugural cycle.

orgDescription: The Neumünster Abbey Cultural Exchange Center (neimënster) is located in the heart of Luxembourg city and part of UNESCO’s world heritage. The unique architectural ensemble of the Abbey has witnessed 400 tumultuous years – as military bastion, orphanage and prison – but is since 2004 home to vibrant culture and artistic expression, after opening in 2004 following years years of intensive renovation works. Amidst a truly picturesque and peaceful scenery, neimënster is open to the public daily from 10AM to 6PM with free admission on all exhibitions and offers 200+ events each year, from concerts and kids’ program to conferences and festivals. In fifteen years, neimënster’s raison d’être of encounters of identities and intercultural dialogue has proven to be strongly anchored in our program, celebrating cultural diversity and promoting national and international exchange, thus resulting in an innovative and critical approach to one’s own environment. The values ​​and missions of neimënster as a bearer of cultural and artistic projects, where encounters with different cultures, backgrounds, perceptions and art forms happen daily, broaden the view of the artists and the public and invite them to a dialogue. neimënster actively supports engaged and political art, while promoting emerging artists. name: Centre for Aesthetics, Religion and Contemporary Culture
orgDescription: The Centre for Aesthetics, Religion and Contemporary Culture of the Universitat Pompeu Fabra in Barcelona (UPF) welcomes the academic and artistic activity around religion, its relationship with the arts and literature, and its effects on the cultural movements of our time, taking into account the contexts of tradition that have made them possible. In 2016, Mr. Javier and Ms. Marta Villavecchia, founding members of the Haas Association, began offering scholarships for postdoctoral researchers and / or artists to develop a research project that would justify the use of the Haas Library. The Haas Library, founded in 2003, includes an important collection of around 40,000 books donated by Prof. Alois M. Haas (University of Zurich) to the UPF. This collection constitutes a highly specialized library for the study of the humanities, religious thought and mysticism, with a particular emphasis on the Western tradition. Its catalogue is still growing thanks to recent donations by Prof. Haas, including literature and resources on philosophical anthropology, metaphysics, theology, and aesthetics. The collection is housed at the General Library of the UPF in the stunning Dipòsit de les Aigües (Water Tower) building, which offers a privileged environment for researchers, and a continuous source of inspiration for artists. The Centre for Aesthetics, Religion and Contemporary Culture was born in 2021 to unite the activities and scopes of the researchers in the UPF and the Association, to continue making its rich, specialised bibliographic collection available to researchers and artists. It is presented now to the international community as a place from which to work on new ways of transmitting humanistic knowledge, in a constant dialogue with artists, writers and other creators.
residencyDescription: The Centre for Aesthetics, Religion and Contemporary Culture and the Haas Library at the Universitat Pompeu Fabra are pleased to announce a call for applications for two individual fellowships, permitting the successful applicants to carry out original artistic and/or research projects at the Haas Library for a period of three months during 2022- 2023. We welcome scholarly and/or artistic submissions from any disciplinary background or perspective, though multidisciplinary proposals are particularly encouraged. Candidates from any academic background are eligible to apply. The candidates must show the specific link between their proposal and any aspect or theme of the Haas Library collection.

name: Cerdeira – Home for Creativity
orgDescription: Cerdeira – Home for Creativity is an art school based in a very special place: Cerdeira, one of the classified schist villages in Serra da Lousã, and a secular small place surrounded by fresh brooks and silence, in an ocean of mountains in the centre of Portugal. This village was abandoned in the late 70’s for social and economic reasons and its rural architectural heritage is now almost completely restored, considering the importance of ecological and sustainable aspects, and the aim to give it a new live and meaning. The fifteen traditional houses have all the comfort of a modern one, but with no distractions (there’s no TV and internet access is limited to Café da Videira and Atelier). Each of the houses was intervened by contemporary artisans who created parts and decorations inspired by the village and its natural surroundings. Besides the houses you can find a craft gallery, a library, a coffee and our shared studios prepared for nearly all kinds of artwork with special wood and ceramic facilities. In 2015 we invited the Japanese ceramist and kiln builder Masakazu Kusakabe to lead the construction of his woodfiring Sasukenei Smokeless Kiln for ceramics (800 L) and today, the kiln is part of the equipment for artists and a unique masterpiece in Portugal that recovers ancient techniques used in contemporary ceramics dramatically glazed experience through 36 hours at 1600 degrees: more than firing it’s an experience. In 2017 Cerdeira Arts and Crafts School was launched with the core mission to become a space for teaching traditional techniques that come out of intemporal lineages, and a space for creativity and art-making aligned with contemporary dialogue. Cerdeira – Arts and Crafts School group of experienced Masters share an artistic and cultural pedagogy based on values of respect for the voice and sensibility of each individual as well as the lineage and tradition of their artistic area. We offer structured courses based on a deep understanding of the principles involved in the aesthetic, creative, and manual learning processes and we involve live practical demonstrations, visual displays, and lectures, as well as the time spent practicing together, with moments of reflection and exchange. The largest building in the village is the House of Arts – a four-floor building that hosts our creative group activities – was rebuilt using only schist stone, clay and chestnut wood. In short, the aim of the project is the promotion of creative tourism while encouraging arts, crafts, traditional techniques and nature intersections. Cerdeira is one of the most active members of the Schist Villages Network. The identity and the authenticity of the place, and the positive energy and persistence of this quiet international association, are what make it so special. We want to be surrounded by positive energy!

name: Chinese European Art Center
orgDescription: CEAC (Chinese European Art Center) For more than 22 years, the Chinese European Art Center has hosted and premiered international artists from all over the world. With studios, exhibitions, contemporary film festivals, concerts, lectures, workshops and an artists-in-residence program, the CEAC plays a central role in southeast China&rsquos cultural landscape. The CEAC is widely known for its pioneering role in China as a non-commercial art space and the excellent guidance it provides for artists conducting research and producing their art at work sites and factories in China. Since 2010, CEAC has also organized a series of large-scale group exhibitions featuring invited and past resident artists under the overarching theme “Rolling Snowball” outside of Xiamen and outside China. A total of fourteen exhibitions have been realized in collaboration with cultural organizations in cities including Shanghai Expo Dutch Culture Center (2010), Guangzhou Redtory Design Factory (2012), Quanzhou Live Show Wonderland (2011/13), Datong Yugang Museum International Photography Festival (2017), Art Museum of Nanjing University of the Arts (2018) and Djúpivogur, Iceland (2014 – 2021). CEAC Platform Europe, based in Amsterdam, was launched in 2010 and regularly organizes networking events for European‐based artists and cultural professionals with experience and/or interest in China. It also regularly presents the research results of CEAC residents at various locations to an interested audience. In addition, the European branch of the CEAC strives to promote an exchange of knowledge and collaboration with fellow specialists and artists in other disciplines by organizing lectures, debates, films and video showings.
residencyDescription: The program starts in 2001 and is one of the first and longest running Artist – in – Residence programs in China open to visual artists, architects, designers, curators, composers and writers from around the world. name: Corpus acrobatics
orgDescription: Corpus acrobatics is representing the contemporary circus arts and has performed worldwide in theaters, festivals and events such as The World Expo in Lisbon, festival of Cannes in France, and the World Tourist Forum ( UN) in Brazil. In 1991 travelling trough Brazil the founders created their first performance about the rich nature and cultural heritage of The Amazon Rainforest. Over three decades, Corpus has included other elements such as mime, puppet theater, music, visual art and video art to enhance the visual and choreographic experience creating a new circus theater performance language. The planet earth, the flora, fauna and bio diversity became their main inspiration. Working with a international team of acrobates, musicians, composers, video artists, costume and light designers and specific technicians to create their performances. In the performances using organic and recycled materials, instalations with bamboo and waste objects. name: Creative Body Institute
orgDescription: Creative Body Institute is a nonprofit arts organization and site-responsive research platform dedicated to embodied creative practice across disciplines—including performance, live art, visual art, creative writing, sound, movement, and ecosomatics. We believe the body is central to all art-making: a site of knowledge, transformation, memory, and imagination. Our programs include site-specific residencies, intensive courses, certificate programs, one-on-one and group mentoring, workshops, and curated gatherings. We also support artists through exhibitions and publications that share embodied research with broader publics. Through longstanding partnerships with cultural organizations across the globe, we create opportunities for place-based and cross-cultural exchange—inviting artists to deepen their work by engaging with new terrains, communities, and ways of knowing. Our commitment to translocal collaboration reflects a belief that art is not made in isolation, but in movement and relationship. By working across diverse cultural and ecological contexts, we foster practices that are responsive, accountable, and alive to the complexities of place. Creative Body anchors this work—offering a consistent, intentional space to ground your practice, connect with others, and expand your creative potential through body-centered art, writing, and performance. Artists who move through our site-specific residency programs become part of an expanding, intergenerational, and international community—a web of creative solidarity that spans disciplines, geographies, and life stages. This living network fosters deep connection, mutual support, and meaningful artistic exchange.
residencyDescription: Creative Body Institute offers immersive, site-specific residencies designed to support thematic, cross-disciplinary inquiry. Our residencies are intergenerational and curated for emergent, mid-career, and established artists working across visual art, sound, performance, writing, installation, dance, social practice, and beyond. We welcome artists with existing embodied practices as well as those seeking to deepen or expand their relationship to the body, land, and place.

orgDescription: Cultivarte is a small ecological center built from guadua bamboo, nestled inside a mango plantation in the tropical valley of Anapoima — just 80 km from Bogotá and its international airport. orgDescription: DAIS Ishinomaki is a place where we “continue to question circulative diversities.” What kind of new learning platform will lead to the achievement of SDGs in contemporary society and the development of the next generation? “DAIS” is an abbreviation for Diversity Art Interactive Studio. Perhaps it is a place where variety of people with diverse backgrounds intermingle and create something new? The ones “continuing to question the circulative diversities” are everyone who wish to participate; from children to seniors, an inclusive community as a whole consisting of diverse local settlers and mobile populations; immigrants from abroad, technical trainees, ones with disabilities, local residents, artists, and so on. Alternatively, wild animals and agricultural products in the fields may also be considered participants. Together with them, we are currently doing DIY renovation work on the site of an abandoned farmhouse at entrance area to the mountains of Ishinomaki City, Miyagi Prefecture, where artists from Japan and abroad can stay and create artworks =”DAIS Air”, and an outdoor theater where local citizens can participate, traditional performing arts and performance art = “CHODO-Festival”, and we are preparing to launch a complex facility that will include the “Museum of Living Memories”; a data library of The Great East Japan Earthquake Memorial Hall through citizens’ perspectives (a venue for workshops, storytelling, and permanent displaying of “Filed Trip Project & Field Trip Project Asia”), and “DAIS Farm” a communal farm field and a kitchen. Rather than setting the goal of achieving a specific goal, we continue to ask questions, and while maintaining the awareness that we are always in the process, we move forward in a gradual cycle as it is and organically.

name: DE PROEF.
orgDescription: The gardens in the UNESCO village of Frederiksoord have a rich history dating back to 1884, the year in which the first Horticultural School in the Netherlands was established. In the following years, this school grew into a nationally and internationally recognized institution. It was here that the so-called ‘garden hares’ studied—students who brought Frederiksoord to life and gained practical knowledge that made them experts in the field of horticulture. From the very beginning, the gardens were the beating heart of this educational institution, and today, they are more important than ever, despite a twenty-year period of decline. During that time, an interesting ecology developed within the gardens, which now serves as the essential foundation for our heritage project, DE PROEF. DE PROEF is a unique heritage project focused on horticulture, agriculture, education, ecology, and art & culture. In this socio-ecological project, the former horticultural school is being repurposed, where the rich past and future come together in a functional and sustainable landscape. The project was initiated two years ago by designers Joshua Kelly and Kim van den Belt of 4F.STUDIO, a forward-thinking design practice that combines nature and technology. Since October 2023, the project has become a reality, and they have established an association with seven local entrepreneurs, including themselves, who collectively hold ownership. The success of the project also relies on the growing group of volunteers who form a strong foundation, as well as the ecologically focused landscape advisory team, in which Arborealis and Cruydt-hoeck play a significant role. The association aims to create an ecological and socially inclusive community, together with other creatives, farmers, volunteers, and academic partners such as TU Eindhoven, Wageningen University, Utrecht University, Hanze University of Applied Sciences Groningen, and local entrepreneurs, offering an alternative future. The 8 hectares of botanical garden and arboretum are being restored and managed ecologically, with attention to both flora and fauna. Birds, butterflies, and other insects find a welcoming habitat here, and visitors can enjoy a carefully maintained natural environment. The garden contains no fewer than 530 diverse (mature) tree species, which form the foundation of the entire site. Here, you can attend guided tours, workshops, and lectures on topics such as food, ecology, and heritage. There is also space for (inter)national researchers, artists/designers, and volunteers to stay for three months and set up or carry out a project. The mission of DE PROEF is clear: to create a balance between past, present, and future. By preserving the valuable elements of the traditional school garden and combining them with new ideas and techniques, a unique place is created that honours the rich history of gardening and shapes a sustainable future.
residencyDescription: At DE PROEF, we support artists and makers who are eager to explore nature-related subjects and have a clear vision for their work. Our residency offers a unique balance of freedom and guidance, tailored to each resident’s individual needs. orgDescription: Dentro La Terra is the colloquial expression used to refer to the historic center of the small village of Arielli, situated in the Italian region of Abruzzo. At Dentro La Terra we believe that it makes more sense than ever to plug local communities in global conversations and that – even if globalisation is often associated with the urban capitals of the world – it touches even the smallest village, opening doors, creating opportunities, and – increasingly so – raising apprehensions. We like to use the expression “”tutto il mondo ?? paese””. The initiative is supported by a group of individuals and professionals. As part of this vision and efforts, an ancien palazzo, renovated in 2018, has been made available as a location to create unique opportunities for artistic and cultural growth, as well as for the regeneration of an ancient Italian village.

residencyDescription: The Vilde Spinderi Residency is a textile arts and design residency integrated in a micro spinning mill focusing on spinning wool from local landscape protecting sheep. name: ´ace
orgDescription: Since 2005, the Artist-in-Residence International Program is Fundación´ace‘s core program, and the starting point for many of our activities and projects. To be in residency at ´ace means to work collaboratively, to receive technical, conceptual and artistic assistance, to share the space and process with fellow artists from other parts of the world and to be immersed in Buenos Aires’ vibrant cultural life. While in residency, artists will benefit from an intense production, research and exploration time enhanced by the exchange of ideas and experiences with peers coming from a wide range of mediums and languages. Proyecto´ace holds four open calls a year (deadlines are: January 31st, April 30th, July 31st and October 31st), and artists-in-residence are selected through their submitted proposals. The program focuses on expanded visual art practices (including performance art and curatorial projects), with a special interest in proposals that make use of various medium or dissolve the borders between them. Our printmaking workshop fosters the idea of the multiple in a work of art, involving –but not circumscribed only to– traditional and innovative printmaking, installation, photography, artist book, painting illustration, video, stop motion, sound art and new media. Since 2005, ´ace has been working as a driving force that links not only different artistic practices within the cultures that produce them, but also between the residents and the rich cultural, urban and social community of the City of Buenos Aires. Proyecto´ace’s RESIDENCIES INFORMATION HERE.
residencyDescription: ´ace is an independent, non-profit, artist-run residency center for contemporary arts located in Buenos Aires, Argentina’s capital city. Approaching its 20th anniversary, ´ace is the longest running residency program in Argentina.

name: Edition/Basel
orgDescription: Edition/Basel is a printmaking program for professional artists. The program seeks to foster both creative and socio-cultural exchanges through its two summer sessions, in which 10 international artists come together over a shared interest in the graphic arts. Good working conditions are extremely important for artists to be their most creative. Therefore it is always the aim of Edition/Basel to provide facilities with well-maintained machines, fresh ink and chemicals, and a variety of paper and other materials necessary for an array of printmaking processes. We encourage our residents to experiment. Is your print work an installation? Does it have another element, like sound, or a performance? Does your piece exist outside the gallery, and move into the city of Basel? We welcome your trials, failures, and curious vision regarding ways of bringing printmaking into the world at large. Started in 2012, the founders of Edition/Basel, Megan Adie and Margarit Lehmann, strive to constantly improve the programs, and also to reach out to further diversify their community. To this end, Margarit has organized and secured funding for a 12 day program in Havana, Cuba, and has also forged connections with printmakers in Yerevan, Armenia and Johannesburg, South Africa. The results of these collaborations have been shown in exhibitions in Havana, Zürich, Basel, and San Francisco. Several similar projects are currently in the works. editionbasel.com
residencyDescription: Edition/Basel is a 12 day program for artists working in intaglio, relief, lithography and letterpress techniques at the Druckwerk studio in Basel, Switzerland. Each session has a theme, which is chosen collaboratively and interpreted individually by the artists. An exhibition is presented at the end of the period at one of three local museums or galleries: the Papiermühle Museum, Salon Mondial at Atelier Mondial Basel, or the Kaskadenkondensator Gallery.

name: POSADA DE LA LUZ *
orgDescription: · · POSADA DE LA LUZ es una casa abierta al encuentro entre personas, sueños y paisajes. Donde la luz abraza el asombro y los días transcurren al ritmo del sol, entre el trabajo, la conversación y el canto de los pájaros. El silencio del páramo, el sosiego, la calidez de un hogar y por supuesto, la creación. Son los ingredientes esenciales con los que hemos cocinado nuestras nuevas residencias artísticas: un refugio para quienes deseen resonar con nuestra idea de pausa y quieran darle tiempo de calidad a sus fabulaciones o proyectos. La POSADA surge como un refugio contemporáneo: un lugar donde el arte, la naturaleza y la convivencia se entrelazan para recordarnos la importancia del tiempo sosegado, de la mirada sobre lo esencial. · La POSADA es una idea de Juanan Requena , nacida del deseo de abrir un hogar donde el asombro, la creatividad y la vida consciente puedan convivir llenos de resonancias. Una casa que se ha ido construyendo despacio, con las manos y la memoria, con ayuda constante de su padre y amigos durante más de un año y que han puesto su corazón y su energía en este proyecto y que ahora toma forma para convertirse en un refugio donde cada visitante pueda reconocerse. La POSADA nace como una extensión natural de ese camino: una invitación a estar, a crear, a compartir desde lo interior con honestidad. Una casa donde abrazar el asombro y el silencio, donde ser la introspección y el encuentro. Un lugar para reconectar con la naturaleza, para caminar despacio, para crear desde la intuición y no desde la exigencia. Donde cultivar la creatividad, los procesos, las relaciones amables y la vida sostenible y consciente. · * El fundador es Juanan Requena : www.nodetenerse.com * Y su estudio creativo vecino a la POSADA es : www.estudioelgranero.com

name: ELPA Media
orgDescription: The concept of establishing the ELPA Design and Sustainability Residency in the Latgale region of Latvia originated in the summer of 2023. It emerged from two primary considerations: the end of the Rucka Artist Residency’s operations in Cēsis and the dilemma of determining where to continue the residency activities. Additionally, there was the question of what to do with a small natural farm following the passing of its last owner. On one hand, there existed an idea without a physical space, and on the other hand, a physical space that had lost its original purpose. The convergence of these two aspects formed the foundation for the vision of the new residency space, centered around the concepts of meeting point, taking a breath, and transformation.
residencyDescription: The ELPA Residency Center is a place where artists and cultural practioners from various countries and fields come together. It creates a space for the exchange of ideas, acquiring new knowledge, and implementing ideas that have arisen at intersections. The name of the residency is derived from the Latvian word “elpa,” which translates to “breath.” It symbolizes the concept of taking a breath, the act of breathing in and out, and the idea of giving something a second breath.

name: Empire of Dirt Residency Association
orgDescription: Empire of Dirt (EoD) is an artist residency and nonprofit located on the traditional, ancestral, and unceded territories of the Yaqan Nukiy (where the rock stands) band within the Ktunaxa Nation (Creston, BC, Canada). We create space and time for artists to engage intentionally with place and land, and build artistic community. The residency is situated on thirty acres of forested land on a mountainside outside Creston, BC; this remote setting encourages wild spaces to thrive and allows for careful human interaction. Empire of Dirt cannot be separated from this place, which is inherently informed by Indigenous histories and ongoing relationships. EoD recognizes the stewardship and sovereignty of the Yaqan Nukiy within the Ktunaxa Nation of this territory, the land, waterways, and more-than-human inhabitants since time immemorial and into the future. Within these contexts, EoD works hard to offer a place, time, and space for professional artists to work; in particular, it is a place for artists that have a strong desire to connect with the land and the natural world. Without the expectations of conventional institutions, the residency offers artists an opportunity to reflect, do research, and to develop their work.
residencyDescription: Empire of Dirt (EoD) prioritizes creating space for artists to connect with the land, community, and each other. EoD has grown out of a desire to create residency opportunities for artists experiencing reduced access to rural or non-urban spaces, in particular Black and Indigenous artists. Our annual programs include Black Artists Gather, Indigenous Arts, and Artist-Led Cohorts; these programs prioritize artists connecting with each other in a variety of ways, both over the short and long-term. Artists selected for thematic residencies receive a stipend, and there are no accommodation fees. Artists are responsible for their own travel costs, and meals.

name: Escola Normal
orgDescription: Escola Normal is an independent, artist-run cultural platform based in Portugal, operating between Madeira Island and Porto. The organisation focuses on artist residencies, exhibitions, and interdisciplinary cultural programming that foster dialogue between contemporary art, ecology, and community. Founded by artists and cultural practitioners, Escola Normal emerged from the desire to create a space for experimentation, collaboration, and artistic research outside conventional institutional structures. The platform hosts national and international artists, providing time and space for creative development while encouraging exchange with local cultural contexts. Through residencies, public events, workshops, and exhibitions, Escola Normal supports emerging and established artists working across disciplines such as visual arts, music, performance, and research-based practices. The organisation also actively engages with local communities and landscapes, particularly exploring themes related to environment, sustainability, and alternative futures. By operating from both an island context in Madeira and an urban context in Porto, Escola Normal aims to build bridges between different geographies, artistic communities, and cultural perspectives. name: Eskipazar Space
orgDescription: Eskipazar, a non-profit independent exhibition and research space founded in 2021 in Dalyan, Muğla, describes itself as a “free playground” dedicated to safeguarding the freedom and creativity of art. It seeks to broaden the accessibility of art to a wider audience by engaging with artists and collectives in the southern region, while documenting contemporary art practices in the city. Operating beyond traditional exhibition venues, Eskipazar emphasizes artistic freedom and expression, celebrating the innovative and experimental qualities of art. It functions as both an exhibition space and a platform for the open exchange of artistic research and ideas. Eskipazar’s primary objective is to enhance the visibility of local art through collaborations with artists and collectives in the southern region, enriching artistic endeavors with local nuances, and preserving the contemporary art scene of the city. In pursuit of this goal, Eskipazar seeks to push the boundaries of art, foster new artistic approaches, and communicate with the universal language of art. Emphasizing the significance of creativity, freedom, and archival practices, Eskipazar strives to unite the transformative power of art with society, welcoming all to partake in the free play and transformation of art within its walls.

name: ExtrArtis, Artists Residencies for Creative Economy
orgDescription: “ExtrArtis, Artists Residencies for Creative Economy” è un progetto di Residenza d’Artista europea per la valorizzazione dell’ambiente costruito. ExtrArtis si identifica nella creatività e nella partecipazione i nuovi driver trasformativi del patrimonio culturale. Il progetto si sviluppa a valle di anni di ricerca scientifica universitaria svolta nell’ipotesi che l’identità dei sistemi insediativi sia strettamente legata ai valori e alle competenze del territorio di sperimentazione. e nel 2022 nell’ambito del Premio ITWIIN, Associazione Italiana Donne Inventrici e Innovatrici in riferimento alle STEAM,ExtrArtis è stato premiato nel 2021 nell’ambito del progetto Europeo di Ricerca e Innovazione Horizon 2020 come uno dei migliori “Modelli circolari di investimento nel riuso adattivo del patrimonio culturale”; “ExtrArtis, Artists Residencies for Creative Economy” is a European artist residency project aimed at the enhancement of the built environment. ExtrArtis identifies creativity and participation as the new transformative drivers of cultural heritage. The project has evolved after years of university scientific research, conducted on the hypothesis that the identity of settlement systems is closely linked to the values and skills of the experimental territory. In 2022, ExtrArtis received the ITWIIN Award from the Italian Association of Women Inventors and Innovators, referencing the STEAM fields. In 2021, it was also recognized within the European Research and Innovation Horizon 2020 project as one of the best “Circular models for adaptive reuse of cultural heritage investments”; L’obiettivo specifico di ExtrArtis è rispondere alle sfide del nostro tempo attraverso strategie culturali attente ad uno sviluppo centrato sull’uomo, innescando processi virtuosi di rigenerazione valoriale, puntando all’elaborazione di scenari di interconnessione tra le persone e luoghi, tra attività e territori. ExtrArtis contribuisce ad incentivare sia i processi di connessione e moltiplicazione dei legami nelle comunità frammentate, che di tutela della memoria collettiva e della coesione con il sistema insediativo. The specific objective of ExtrArtis is to address the challenges of our time through culturally informed strategies that focus on human-centered development. It aims to initiate virtuous processes of value regeneration, with a focus on the development of scenarios that interconnect people and places, activities, and territories. ExtrArtis contributes to encouraging both the processes of connecting and multiplying bonds within fragmented communities and the preservation of collective memory and cohesion with the settlement system. Il progetto ha una durata annuale e si divide in 4 quattro fasi principali: The project has a duration of one year and is divided into four main phases: 1. Conoscenza_ Analisi dell’identità del territorio campano per la stesura di un bando di selezione di 6 artisti emergenti che leghino la loro produzione all’identità ed ai valori della Regione ; 1. Knowledge_ Analysis of the identity of the Campania region to draft a call for the selection of six emerging artists who will connect their work to the identity and values of the region; 2. Sperimentazione_Selezione degli artisti coinvolti in qualità di ri-attivatori delle sedi storiche del Grand Tour attraverso la pratica di Residenza d’Artista presso Relais La Rupe a Sorrento per la durata di due settimane e la produzione di opere ispirate al genius loci; 2. Experimentation_ Selection of artists involved as re-activators of the historic sites of the Grand Tour through an Artist Residency at Relais La Rupe in Sorrento for a period of two weeks and the production of works inspired by the genius loci; 3. Coinvolgimento_La partecipazione alla sperimentazione, in qualità di beneficiari indiretti e diretti, prevede l’interazione tra artisti, comunità, associazioni locali, maestranze ed istituzioni attraverso tavoli di concertazione, approcci partecipativi strutturati con il supporto di esperti del settore scientifico, workshop, visite guidate sul territorio ed eventi espositivi, formativi ed educativi volti alla riscoperta dell’identità per le comunità residenti e gli studenti degli Istituti artisti locali; 3. Engagement_ Participation in the experimentation, as direct and indirect beneficiaries, involves interaction between artists, the community, local associations, craftsmen, and institutions through consultation meetings, structured participatory approaches with the support of experts in the scientific field, workshops, guided tours of the area, and exhibitions, educational events aimed at rediscovering identity for resident communities and local art institute students; 4. Diffusione dei risultati_Divulgazione scientifica, conferenze nazionali ed esposizioni temporanee presso Sorrento, Napoli e Capri per la diffusione degli esiti di sperimentazione. La capacità formativa della sperimentazione è resa attraverso convenzioni che il progetto ExtrArtis stabilisce solitamente con le istituzioni (patrocinio morale), le associazioni del luogo, l’Istituto artistico locale, enti sovraregionali e collaborazioni scientifiche universitarie. 4. Dissemination of Results_ Scientific dissemination, national conferences, and temporary exhibitions in Sorrento, Naples, and Capri to share the outcomes of the experimentation. The educational capacity of the experimentation is achieved through agreements that the ExtrArtis project typically establishes with institutions (moral sponsorship), local associations, the local art institute, interregional bodies, and university scientific collaborations.
residencyDescription: ExtrArtis identifica l’ambiente costruito come un laboratorio in cui declinare una nuova prosperità inclusiva che riguarda l’inscindibilità tra i luoghi ei suoi abitanti. ExtrArtis organizza approcci partecipativi per accompagnare le comunità nella transizione culturale del nostro tempo, stimolandole attraverso l’arte a guardare al patrimonio culturale con responsabilità ed educando le persone all’adattabilità dei contesti in qualità di depositari della memoria collettiva.

name: FaveLAB
orgDescription: FaveLAB is a residency, e-Residency, workshop and exhibition platform based in Athens, Greece. Our artist residencies, workshops, lectures, networking meetings and exhibition projects address artists, designers, curators and writers who work – or wish to extend their knowledge and practice – in the field of visual art, performance, film, art in public space, contemporary jewellery art, textile art, literature. FaveLAB focuses on the urban dynamics of Athens, a Mediterrenian metropolis in the epicenter of cultural shifts, and aims at making their social and political significance visible to the international art community – and a broader public. Experimental art practices, alternative presentation formats, integrative art and design approaches are welcome. FaveLAB offers an individual introduction into the life, politics and – ancient and contemporary – culture in Greece. FaveLAB promotes the dialogue between the Greek and international art scene and supports a vital exchange between the public, cultural agents, designers and urbanists. FaveLAB offers accommodation, exhibition opportunities and personal expertise, facilitating the access to the rich cultural tradition of the place and assisting the artists to develop ideas and concepts, realize and present them in Athens. name: Fez Art Residency
orgDescription: Fez Art Residency (FAR) is a flexible, artist-centred residency programme based in and around the historic UNESCO-listed Medina of Fez, Morocco. Rather than being tied to a single location, FAR functions as a collaborative platform – connecting visiting artists with a carefully curated network of accommodation hosts, studios, local artisans, cultural facilitators, and creative professionals. Our goal is to make Fez an accessible and inspiring destination for artists from Morocco and around the world. We do this by offering highly personalised residencies and creative retreats, tailored to the interests, practice, and pace of each individual. This means that whether you’re seeking quiet time to develop a project, explore new cultural perspectives, or engage with traditional Moroccan craftsmanship, FAR provides the structure and support to help shape a residency that’s truly your own. FAR is rooted in values of cultural exchange, ethical collaboration, and creative independence. We’re committed to supporting artists in ways that are locally grounded and globally connected while contributing to the long-term sustainability of Fez’s rich creative ecosystem. Above all, Fez Art Residency is about welcoming artists into place – offering space to explore, reflect, and create within one of the world’s most historic and creatively alive cities.

The outside spaces include colonnaded areas and large gardens, where in the summer months we host our rich artistic programme and welcome guests to lunch and dinner. The surrounding land is covered with grape vines, fields of wheat, fruit trees and a vegetable garden. Our kitchen offers our guests local products from our fields and selected farms. We have also recently opened Casa Flu?Õ_ Relais, a bed and breakfast offering 5 charming rooms, stylishly furnished and equipped with every comfort. orgDescription: Flame Asociación Cultural x Estudio Inverso is a strategic joint venture combining institutional vision, real estate infrastructure, and five years of proven creative community management in Madrid. Asociación Flame is a newly formed NGO dedicated to cultivating, securing, and promoting physical spaces for the contemporary arts. Founded by the property owners of our Carabanchel industrial warehouse facility, Flame’s core mission is to establish a sustainable framework for international art events, festivals, contemporary exhibitions, and robust digital promotion for artists. While the NGO is launching its initial phase of programming, it provides the structural backbone and vision for our expanding cultural footprint. Estudio Inverso serves as the operational partner of this residency. Established five years ago, Estudio Inverso originated as a highly successful “open walls” studio collective hosting 10 artists in Madrid’s central Malasaña district. Building upon this foundation of collaborative workspace management, they expanded their operations last year by partnering with Flame’s founders to open an additional 13 specialized open studios within our newly renovated warehouse in the creative epicenter of Carabanchel. Together, Flame Asociación Cultural and Estudio Inverso merge institutional advocacy with hands-on studio management, offering international resident artists unparalleled space, infrastructure, and deep roots within the Madrid art scene.
residencyDescription: Flame x Estudio Inverso is an independent, specialized contemporary art residency program designed to bridge international creative practice with Madrid’s most dynamic cultural ecosystems. Operating within an industrial open-studio warehouse containing 13 independent creative workspaces, our core objective is to provide international visual artists and researchers with the physical space, critical dialogue, and local network necessary to execute ambitious projects. The residency is strategically structured around a dual-location urban concept: residents live in the central, trend-setting historic district of Malasaña—ideal for cultural immersion—and work in Carabanchel, the recognized epicenter of Madrid’s underground contemporary art movement.

name: Flor del Sol
orgDescription: Flor del Sol is an Art Center run by us, Anita (Architect and artist) and Jose (Anthropologist and artist), in our private living-situation. Our property covers eight hectares of tropical flora and fauna. The majority of the land is covered in rainforest that we keep in its natural state. The developed portion of our land is home to many fruit trees. The buildings, spread throughout the land are integrated in to the natural setting and our daily life is woven between inside and outside spaces. One of the buildings is a studio space. Surrounding Area Buena Vista is the closest village. It is a 45-minute walk or a quick six Boliviano moto-taxi ride. With cafes and restaurants surrounding a beautiful plaza and colonial architecture throughout the center of town, Buena Vista is a very pleasant place to pass time. The adjacent countryside of rolling hills is covered with divisions of forest, fruit trees, and pastures for livestock. As the name says, there are many beautiful views, especially of the mountains of Amboro National Park, the eastern foothills of the Andes. Another attraction is the Surutu river, which is only three kilometers from the village, and is a nice place to take a refreshing dip. We neither receive funding nor ask for it. We finance with our own income. Two people help us mantaining the place. We request a basic rate of 15.- EURO a day for accommodation and meals as well as collaboration in cooking and maintaining clean. our access to internet is very limited. therefore we don`t have WiFi. we just use our smart-phones. nevertheless in case of necessities exceptional we can offer this access to internet.
residencyDescription: Living in the countryside in a beautiful natural setting with our 11 dogs we like to share our unique space with artists who have common interests. a residence with us is mainly appropriate for artists who are inspired by nature or even like to work in or with nature and who like dogs.

name: Fondazione Culturale Officine Saffi
orgDescription: Fondata nel 2011 da Laura Borghi, la Fondazione Officine Saffi, una delle principali fondazioni no-profit che studia la ceramica contemporanea internazionale, adotta un approccio alla ceramica senza pari, a 360 gradi. Promuovendo nuove ricerche e sperimentazioni sulla ceramica, esplorando al contemporaneo il passato, la fondazione amplia ed espande il dialogo tra arte, artigianato e design. Attraverso un programma dinamico e interdisciplinare di mostre, attività didattiche e pubblicazioni, promuovendo attivamente un vivace dialogo sulla ceramica che incapsula un pubblico eterogeneo. Tutte le attività della fondazione sono guidate dalla convinzione che la ceramica sia portatrice di trasformazione artistica, culturale e sociale. Promuovendo un ambiente aperto e partecipativo, la Fondazione Officine Saffi incoraggia sia gli artisti che il pubblico a interrogarsi su cosa significati vivere nel nostro mondo oggi, a relazionarsi con l’Altro e la vita non umana ea creare valore sociale e culturale attraverso il coinvolgimento in un programma multidisciplinare che sottolinea un consorzio unico di interpretazioni e crea slancio attorno alla ceramica nel ventunesimo secolo. La fondazione supporta artisti, designer e creatori attraverso le diverse fasi di produzione, promozione e riconoscimento del loro lavoro, pur essendo una piattaforma per creativi emergenti, nonché progetti e narrazioni che prosperano al di fuori dei sistemi di mercato consolidati. L’impegno della fondazione nell’esplorazione della cultura italiana si accompagna alla sua identità interculturale e al desiderio di creare un dialogo più ampio che risuoni su scala globale insieme a una rete ibrida di talenti, istituzioni e organizzazioni internazionali.
residencyDescription: PROGRAMMA DI RESIDENZA La Fondazione Officine Saffi invita artisti, designer e pensatori a immergersi in un programma di residenza che reinventa la ceramica come lente per esplorare il mondo contemporaneo. Ogni anno, fino a sei menti creative provenienti da diverse discipline e orizzonti culturali saranno accolte in questo spazio unico per l’innovazione e la collaborazione. I residenti godranno di pieno accesso a laboratori all’avanguardia, attrezzature specializzate e la guida di maestri ceramisti, insieme a sistemazioni confortevoli progettate per promuovere concorrenza e ispirazione. Il programma prospera su una cultura di uguaglianza, partecipazione e scambio aperto, creando un ecosistema dinamico in cui le idee fluiscono liberamente e la crescita collettiva prospera.

name: MASEREEL
orgDescription: MASEREEL is a contemporary arts centre that combines an artist-oriented artistic programme with an international residency programme for artists and critics, with a special focus on printed matter at large. As part of its artistic activity, MASEREEL produces and presents contemporary visual art, publishes artist publications and editions, and organizes events such as artist talks and an arts festival. Equally fundamental is its international residency programme, which over the past decades has grown into one of the most challenging and inspiring environments for artists and critics to explore printed matter in all its facets or to integrate it within a broader practice. Located in a wooded area and equipped with a dynamic printmaking studio, the emphasis is on development, creation, and dialogue. Until early 2025, the organization operated under the name Frans Masereel Centrum. However, as of 10 March 2025, it has been renamed MASEREEL. This change embraces its rich history and the name by which it is generally known. At the same time, it clarifies that MASEREEL is not a knowledge centre about the visual artist Frans Masereel, nor does it position itself as an institute. Instead, MASEREEL is an eternal start-up centred on the artist – both as a creator and as a person. The choice of MASEREEL as the new name marks the final step in a recent repositioning as an arts centre with a twofold core mission: artistic and residential. However, this is not an endpoint. Beginning in 2025, MASEREEL will organize the international biennial RHIZOMA every two years on and around its site. Additionally, work is underway to make its extensive collection available to researchers, and from 2026, residents will be able to stay in a brand-new artist pavilion.
residencyDescription: In recent years, the MASEREEL residency programme has become one of the most challenging environments for contemporary artists to broaden and deepen their artistic practice.

name: Residência Artística FAAP – São Paulo
orgDescription: Fundação Armando Alvares Penteado (FAAP) is an institution founded in 1947 in the economic capital of Brazil, São Paulo. It was established according to the last wishes of the artist and businessman count Armando Alvares Penteado to create a Fine Arts School with his assets. The institution initially offered small music and visual arts courses and has since evolved into a large complex for higher education, offering a wide range of academic programs, from undergraduate to postgraduate studies, across various fields including communication, arts, law, and business. Additionally, FAAP has played a significant role in Brazil’s cultural landscape through the activities of its museum, MAB-FAAP, its theater, and its Art Residency Program. FAAP has an annex in the Lutetia building on a plaza called Praça do Patriarca, which is an outstanding example of the predominant architecture of central São Paulo in the first half of the 20th century. The building was restored as part of the process of rehabilitating the former charm of downtown São Paulo. The location symbolically revisits the story of the founder of the Institution since the Lutetia building was erected in the 1920s, when Count Armando Alvares Penteado commissioned Sao Paulo’s renowned architect Ramos de Azevedo, who designed the Municipal Theater and gave the city its style. Lutetia is the central part of three different eight-floor buildings joined by one single façade. It was listed for conservation by the Historical Heritage agency in 1992, and was restored on the lines of a project executed by the Architecture and Urbanism course of FAAP itself, partnered by the ONG Viva o Centro, the municipal government, EMURB, and the Heritage agency, with institutional support from MASP (art museum).
residencyDescription: Residência Artística FAAP, located in the historic Lutetia building in São Paulo, is an artistic residency program designed for Brazilian artists residing outside of São Paulo and international artists active in the field of visual arts. Each semester, selected artists spend 2 to 5 months in one of the ten spacious live-in studios within the building, where they are encouraged to develop their artistic projects. Additionally, participants are invited to engage in academic integration activities, including talks, open studios, and seminars open to students of the institution’s Visual Arts Courses and the general public.

orgDescription: Društvo Photon / Galerija Photon je neprofitna kulturna organizacija s sedežem v Ljubljani v Sloveniji, posvečena sodobni fotografiji in vizualni kulturi. Photon, ustanovljen leta 2003, se je razvil v eno vodilnih specializiranih platform za fotografijo v Sloveniji in aktivnega partnerja na umetniški sceni Srednje in Vzhodne Evrope. Med letom 2005 in 2018 je organiziral festival Photonic Moments – Mesec fotografije, ki je mednarodni poštni del mreže Evropskega meseca fotografije. Photon izvaja tudi programe odprtih pozivov za podporo mladim fotografom iz srednje in vzhodne Evrope, kot je Different Worlds, in razvija izobraževalne pobude, kot je Fotonična šola, namenjena krepitvi profesionalnega razvoja vzhajajočih umetnikov. Poleg galerijskih dejavnosti v Ljubljani je Photon pred upravljanjem Galerije Photon na Dunaju (2013–2024) pred kratkim odprl projektni prostor in knjigarno v Mariboru ter vzdržuje obsežno mednarodno mrežo kustosov, institucij in festivalov. Rezidenčni program organizacije na Ptuju te dejavnosti še dodatno širi, saj umetnikom zagotavlja čas in prostor za umetniško raziskovanje, produkcijo in mednarodno izmenjavo.

name: GlogauAIR gGmbH
orgDescription: GlogauAIR is a non-profit art space and residency created in 2006 by Chema Alvargonzalez and nowadays supported by Memoria Artística Chema Alvargonzalez, in Kreuzberg, Berlin.The residency is located in a historic, modernist-style building that was originally designed to be a school. The building was one of the first projects erected by architect Ludwig Hoffmann in 1896, during his time as the Building Advisor of Berlin. Activities take place in Chema’s former studio building in Berlin Kreuzberg. The word GlogauAIR comes from the phonetic combination of GlogauerStrasse; the name of the street where it is located, and its purpose; an Artist in Residence program where artists can develop their own journey in the city of Berlin; a pioneering metropolis for contemporary global culture. Focused on the principles of exploring, creating, and exhibiting, the residency offers an on-site and on-line program for international artists of all fields. Artists in GlogauAIR’s on-site Residency Program live and work in one of thirteen studios. They receive curatorial and technical support, as well as a diverse program that aims to help them in their professional careers; encouraging not only the development of the artist’s work but also the opportunity to share ideas and opinions with the other artists. Through the on-line Program, the artist has the opportunity to receive curatorial support, regular group meetings, talks by experts, and workshops, from their homes or personal studios located anywhere in the world. This on-line program was set up as a result of the challenges faced in 2020. Far from letting this stop us, we expanded our program to make it available for artists who can’t join us physically in Berlin. Above all, GlogauAIR continues the project created by Alvargonzalez, built on openness, receptivity to new ideas, and support of local and international contemporary art practices.

name: Glosolì International Residency for Artists
orgDescription: “L’anima danza!” Glosolì comes from a Sigur Ros song that reminds of the glowing of the sun, soul and beauty. Glosolì is a space for artists, different art forms, dance and afro contemporary dance in particular. It is a home for artistic research and cultural and artistic métissage, where an art connected to nature is developed and encouraged. It is a beautiful and silent space in the historic centre of Ivrea (Torino), in front of the Teatro Giacosa, the main theatre built in 1834. You can find 2 rooms (a double and a single), a dance studio, a common bathroom and kitchen, and, on summer, a space in the yard for painting or creating. The old town is quiet and tiny, it was the headquarters of the Olivetti computer company, which used to be an avant-guard company with an open interest for art, architecture, music, social development, environment, and respect for the work. Roberta Tirassa, the Director of the residency, is an international dancer and choreographer of afro contemporary dance. Her actual artistic researches are connected to cultural métissage, the feminine, divinities and archetypes in everybody, flowers. And most of all a merging of dance and nature and/or in the nature. As she graduated as an environmental engineer, and has a passion for mountaineering skying and hiking, she or the house colleagues can also accompany any guest in a visit/walks in the near countryside, wonderful lakes (Anfiteatro Morenico di Ivrea) and mountains (Piemonte and Valle d’Aosta), finding amazing locations for the artistic inspiration. As Roberta also personally practices various forms of holistic healing, in an effort to honor the organic connection between body, mind and spirit, some of the activities of Glosolì are dedicated to it. Glosolì is also the space for the Compagnia Roberta Tirassa of afro contemporary dance and for the cultural association Glosolì. There is a partnership among Ass. Glosolì and the Association Transcendance-afro contemporary dance of Gujan Mestras in France. The residency is in connection with the art gallery “Kunsthaus” of Ivrea, which is part of the technical committee for contemporary art, and Music Studio-Ivrea jazz Club for music, Associazione Naturalp for excursions in the nature. In Ivrea and Canavese, there is a big international Jazz Festival twice a year, open to a fusion of different art forms and can be an interesting cultural moment. Glosolì can also suggest other dance schools, art galleries in town. There is an open museum of Olivetti company architectures: www.mamivrea.it and www.maam.ivrea.it. There is a beautiful museum of contemporary art Museo della Carale, www.museodellacarale.it. Ivrea is located in the Anfiteatro Morenico di Ivrea and has 5 lakes: a moraine landscape, left by the glaciers in the Quaternary, full of amazing lakes, woods, hills and at the feet of the mountains. It is really close by car or train to Aosta Valley and its castles and Alps landscape or the town of Aosta or the museum Forte di Bard and just 40 Km far from the intellectual town of Torino and 2 hours from Milano. As we are particularly interested in the connection between art and nature, we can help you finding wonderful locations, inspiration for your artwork. If artists feel the necessity for a culturally alive bigger town, you can easily reach Torino centre with just an hour by train (Ivrea station is 10 minute walk from the residency). Besides that, our Historic Carnival is unique in the world, with famous Battle of the Oranges, and can be exploited from an artistic point of view too, www.storicocarnevaleivrea.it. Glosolì is also a Bed and Breakfast and it’s a no smoking place.
residencyDescription: Glosolì is a residency dedicated to creation and choreography, mainly dance/music shows and performances related to the cultural métissage and exchange, but also a place open to performers, yoga practitioners, visual artists, video artists, photographers, contemporary artists, musicians, actors, new media and for art social projects. The artistic committee cooperates with “Glosolì” cultural association whose aims are the merging of different art forms and different cultures and environment.

orgDescription: The mission of Good Hart Artist Residency is to nurture artists, writers, and composers from various backgrounds and artistic disciplines and to connect them with the local community in enriching experiences that empower people through the arts in the natural beauty of Northern Michigan. The Good Hart Artists Residency is motivated by the three concepts of Art, Place, and Community. Art – The Good Hart Artist Residency welcomes writers and artists working in all visual mediums. The residency provides time and space for writers and artists to create, as well as full room and board to allow residents time to focus on work. Place – Good Hart is a very small town located on M-119, a scenic heritage route referred to as the Tunnel of Trees, in Northern Michigan. The area’s natural beauty includes the Lake Michigan shoreline, inland lakes, and coastal dunes and wetlands. This unique region is home to state parks and forests and more than 25 publicly accessible preserves. Community – The Good Hart Artist Residency believes connecting people from different backgrounds and cultures feeds creativity and creates a more interesting and compassionate world. Artists-in-residence connect to the local community by collaborating with our partnering nonprofit organizations to provide educational workshops, presentations, and open houses.

name: Hafnarborg
orgDescription: Hafnarborg – the Hafnarfjörður Centre of Culture and Fine Art stands in the heart of the town Hafnarfjörður in Iceland. The museum houses a variety of cultural events, art exhibitions, concerts, workshops and lectures. From its inauguration, it has also run an Artist-in-Residence program on the top floor of the museum, the first of its kind in Iceland. The museum has two exhibition galleries, featuring about a dozen different exhibitions each year. The exhibitions explore works both by leading Icelandic and international artists, featuring contemporary artists as well as established artists from the early 20th century. The Hafnarborg Collection currently counts around 1,500 works, with a notable contribution from Eiríkur Smith (1925-2016), a leading 20th century artist in Iceland. Exhibitions from the Collection are a regular part of the museum programme. The museum was formally inaugurated in the spring of 1988, on the foundation set by Dr. Sverrir Magnússon and his wife Ingibjörg Sigurjónsdóttir, who donated their considerable collection of art and their house in the centre of Hafnarfjörður to the town of Hafnarfjörður, to become a museum. The Collection has grown considerably since then, both through purchases and through gifts from artists and collectors. Hafnarborg is run by the town of Hafnarfjörður and conserves the art collection of the municipality. The museum hosts a dynamic educational programme in connection with its exhibitions. Guided tours in English and Icelandic are available as well, upon request. Hafnarborg is also a beloved concert hall, with its unique features, hosting monthly Midday Concerts, the contemporary concert series Phonemes, The Hafnarborg Songfest and more.
residencyDescription: Hafnarborg runs an Artist-in-Residence program, with an apartment and studio space on the top floor of the museum at Strandgata 34, in the heart of Hafnarfjörður. name: HARP Horse and Art Research Program
residencyName: HARP Horse and Art Research Program
orgDescription: The Horse and Art Research initiative is a residency program located in the Hungarian countryside and it was established for those interested in combining equine knowledge and visual arts. We are looking for artists, art historians and researchers, who are interested in horses and the place of the horse in art. The short (usually 2 week duration) intensive summer workshops include theory, lectures, talks and discussions, daily practice and lessons of horsemanship, horsearchery and riding, as well as there is an opportunity to make studio based work. In Artsy an artical was published with the title „11 of the World’s Most Unusual Artist Residencies” and our program is part of it. We began from the point that riding is art. The representation of man and horse developed in parallel in the history of art, with horses appearing repeatedly in contemporary art too. Therefore we thought we would initiate an international discourse around the Horse and Art. The interest was greater, than we expected and after the success of the program in 2015, we decided to continue the project with the aim of further depth. The first Horse and Art program was held in August 2015 in Barnag with international participants. Artists from nine countries arrived with different kinds of art backgrounds, such as fine art, design and contemporary dance. We organise the program regularly since. For each program we can offer places for up to 15 participants. In our new Lovarda Galéria (Arena Gallery) there is the possibility to make exhibitions. Program leaders are Szmrecsányi-Veszely Beáta, artist and researcher and Szmrecsányi Márton, horse trainer and horsearcher. They worked together on several equine- and art collaborations since 2006. They live in Barnag with their three children and horses since 2009. One of the most beautiful small villages of the Balaton-Upperland in Western Hungary is the village of Barnag. A 19. century small holding with its stables, inside riding arena, grazer, medows are owned by the Szmrecsányi family and their sport association. Next to the small lake traditional yurts are placed. We have an official horsearchery track and an outside arena. We keep our horses free in stud, an open stable and a 15 hectare land with forest and park land is available for them all day long. The Balaton-Upperland National Park, which is wellknown for its special bird life, rich wild life and park land is situated right next to our land, in our neighbourhood, offering us the possibilities for tracking and special trainings in cross-country. In the inside arena we created a project space, ideal for exhibitions. Accommodation in rural life settings is offered in simple Hungarian style yurts. There are two bathrooms and a summer kitchen available for the participants, as well as a large old barn, where we hold our discussions, talks and lectures. Summer studios are ready for the artists to use. We can accommodate upto 15 people for a program. We can also offer our historical guesthouse for visitors. The beautiful 19th century farmhouse is fully furnished and accommodates upto 6 people.
residencyDescription: We organise the program with different research themes each year. It is our intention to offer the opportunities for artists with practices coming from both western- and eastern traditions and to open up connections for artists, riders and researchers internationally with the possibility of developing professional collaborations. We would also like to explore points of connection between equine culture and the artworld. We offer the unique possibility for to view and / or participate in trainings. Archery, riding indoor or tracking and equestrian archery can be practiced at our property. It would be our intention to make an exhibtion open to the public at the end of each residency program at our gallery space. name: Haystack Mountain School of Crafts
orgDescription: The Haystack Mountain School of Crafts is an international craft school located on the Atlantic Ocean in Deer Isle, Maine. Founded in 1950 as a research and studio program in the arts, Haystack offers one and two-week studio workshops to participants of all skill levels as well as the two-week, Open Studio Residency program, exhibitions, tours, auctions, artist presentations, and shorter workshops for Maine residents and high school students. We support visiting artists and scholars from a variety of fields including science, literature, music, and the visual arts who are invited to spend two weeks at the school focusing on their work. Haystack also functions as a ʻthink-tankʼ in looking at craft—publishing annual monographs and organizing a variety of conferences and symposia that examine craft in broader contexts. These include collaborations with other institutions such as the MIT Center for Bits and Atoms and the Cooper-Hewitt National Design Museum, Smithsonian Institution. The award-winning campus was designed by noted American architect, Edward Larrabee Barnes, and opened in 1961 when the school relocated to Deer Isle. In addition to the exceptional setting, Haystack provides twenty-four hour access to the studios, and its small scale fosters a collegial atmosphere. Many national and international craftspeople, who are leaders in their field, have taught or studied at Haystack. Textile designer Jack Lenor Larsen glass artists Dale Chihuly and Lino Tagliapietra choreographer Liz Lerman blacksmith and designer Tom Joyce potters M. C. Richards and Toshiko Takaezu weaver Anni Albers metalsmiths Arline Fisch and Robert Ebendorf are among the renowned figures whose work and ideas were also influenced by their involvement with the school.
