orgDescription: Only thirty-five minutes from downtown Auckland by ferry, Waiheke is home to a lively community of New Zealand artists, painters, sculptors, jewellers, photographers, ceramicists and more. Hosting a biennial Waiheke Artists in Residence Programme. Personal development through our Workshop activities facilitated by experienced tutors plus our art appreciation sessions and Gallery trips. name: U.N.A.G.E. IASI ART RESIDENCY (National University of Arts ”George Enescu”, iași)
orgDescription: BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF IASI TOWN: Known as The Cultural Capital of Romania, Iasi is a symbol in Romanian history, it is the second-largest city in Romania, after the national capital Bucuresti, and the seat of Iasi County. Located in the historical region of Moldavia, Iasi has traditionally been one of the leading centres of Romanian social, cultural, academic and artistic life. Iasi is one of the most important education and research centres of the country and its social and cultural life revolves around: “Palace of Culture”, “Vasile Alecsandri” National Theater, “Moldova State Philharmonic”, “Opera House”, “Iasi Athenaeum”, “Botanical Garden” , “Central University Library”, the high quality cultural centres and festivals, an array of museums, memorial houses, religious and historical monuments. BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF ART RESIDENCY PROGRAM: “U.N.A.G.E. IASI ART RESIDENCY” is based in Iasi, Romania and functions within “George Enescu” National University of Arts. AIM OF ART RESIDENCY PROGRAM: The main aim of “U.N.A.G.E. IASI ART RESIDENCY” is to create various and complex events in Iasi, a cultural town with a lots of inspiration sources, to meet the students from “George Enescu” National University of Arts and the local artists, in order to exchange ideas and to share experiences with them as for a future possible collaboration. WELCOMING: The artists will be waited At the airport by the organiser of this residency, they will be hosted either in a students hostel or in a flat, depending on the availability of accommodation spaces, and afterwards they will be presented the studios of the university, the teachers and the students. ACCOMMODATION: The accommodation room is private, but they might share the bathroom and the kitchen with the others. FOOD: The artists can eat either at “Saint Nicholas” Cafeteria which belongs to “Metropolitan Cathedral” or at “Titu Maiorescu” Cafeteria which belongs to “Alexandru Ioan Cuza” University. They are both located in the central area. WORKING FACILITIES: The artists-in-residence will work in the studios of the Faculty of Fine Arts and Design, together with the other students. They have access to the library of our faculty, where they can use our computers and read the available art books. WORKING SCHEDULE: The artists-in-residence will have totally freedom to take their time in order to create their art project, there is no daily schedule. The organiser of the residency together with the volunteer students will take care of their needs, will guide them in town and will accompany them to some important cultural events from the town, but only when they have free time. That’s why, an important aspect is that the artists-in-residence must understand that sometimes they have to manage on their own. EXHIBITION SPACE: The artists-in-residence will have the opportunity to exhibit in “Aparte” Gallery which belongs to the Faculty of Fine Arts and Design, or in another local gallery. It is very important for them to take into account that the exhibition spaces are generally booked one year before and the artists in residence must understand that they will exhibit in accordance to the availability of an exhibition space from Iasi. COSTS: The artists-in-residency must pay for: their round trip flight ticket, for accommodation, for a part of their art materials and for food.The University will cover only a part of the art materials for the artists-in-residence. If necessary, the artists will buy other art materials from the local art supplies. The studios are for free.
residencyDescription: ” U.N.A.G.E. IASI ART RESIDENCY” program is based in Iasi town, Romania and it is focused on an intercultural exchange with international artists from painting area. The Painting Department from the Faculty of Fine Arts and Design within “George Enescu” National University of Arts, Iasi will kindly support ” U.N.A.G.E. IASI ART RESIDENCY”.

orgDescription: Ikalto Micro Art Residence is situated on the 9th floor of a Soviet residential building that had been erected on one of the city’s peaks: Ikalto Hill. Guests and residents are welcome – and can never resist – to observe rooftops, hills, and mountains, different with every season and especially beautiful at the sunrise. Our spacious flat is a result of conjoining two separate flats, one of which was built to be a sculptor’s atelier, and boasts 6 metres high ceiling – a necessary condition also for recording sound. Our mission is to make niche artists proud! “While attending and participating in free improv and experimental music events around the world, I noticed that not only are those events underground by spirit but the locations that host those events are not lush at all. It’s the least money engaged in the most daring art. Experimental music is challenging in all possible meanings. I invested a lot in creating this lush atmosphere to give improvised and experimental music some sort of elite status which that music truly deserves.” Araik Vietinghoff

orgDescription: In Cahoots Residency provides housing and studio space to both emerging and professional artists in a variety of mediums, with a focus on artists books, letterpress, printmaking, writing, and collaboration. The residency hosts from three to five artists at a time for sessions ranging from one to three weeks long. Residents are provided private individual guest houses (with kitchens and full bathrooms) and 24-hour access to the spacious shared studios or the individual writing studio. Artists are expected to pursue creative projects or research while at In Cahoots. For those who desire technical instruction or creative mentorship, demonstrations and mentorship meetings are available for an additional fee. Every session ends with a work-share: a chance for dialogue and sharing works in progress with fellow residents. The spacious printmaking and book arts studios are in a renovated barn, with modern conveniences and historic charm. There is wi-fi in the housing and the studio and good cell service throughout the property. The letterpress studio, located in the former horse barn, is fully equipped with a Vandercook Universal I, a Vandercook Universal III automated press, and a large collection of lead and wood type of a variety of sizes. The printmaking studio houses a Takach 40 x 72 etching press, a Conrad 36 x 54 etching press, a Griffin 32 x 52 etching press, vertical etching tank, large paper soaking tray, utility sink, drying rack, and work tables. The separate book bindery includes large work tables, Jacques board shear, Challenge guillotine paper cutter, drymount press, Kwikprint foil stamp press, and two nipping presses. Basic supplies such as solvents, rags, brayers, and newsprint are provided.
residencyDescription: In Cahoots Residency is a place of collaboration and creative energy, a rare opportunity for uninterrupted work time as well as dialogue with other artists. name: IRIS ART CENTRE
orgDescription: The IRIS ART CENTRE is a place for artistic education and coaching in Greece. We organize summer art workshops and artist residencies in a quiet natural location in Greece. The center is specialized in artistic education and coaching of artists, students and creatives of all ages and abilities. The center is situated on a large estate in the midst of olive groves and vineyards near the village of Afidnes at a 30 minute driving distance from the center of Athens. It is part of the private home of artist/art educator Annette Luycx. In our residencies you get all the guidance and encouragement you need to work on your artistic expression and the development of your personal artistic voice. Residencies are full board so you have the possibility to work concentrated for long stretches of time, and get into a flow. The IRIS ART CENTRE was founded by Annette Luycx M.Ed, a graduate of MICA, Baltimore. She has specialized in artistic coaching. Purpose of the IRIS ART CENTRE is to support artists and art-students of all ages, abilities and backgrounds, in gaining increased self-awareness and understanding of their individual creative process, and to promote artistic growth and development of their artistic voice. Annette Luycx has travelled extensively and studied fine arts, theatre and ceramics with many international artists and art educators all over the world. Originally from the Netherlands, she lives and works in Athens as an artist and free lance art educator, organizing art courses and art workshops for adults in Greek and English. Co-founder of the IRIS ART CENTRE is Andonis Papadantonakis. He has studied Philosophy and Anthropology in the Netherlands, and is an expert on Greek culture and history. He has been organizing summer language courses in Greece for 15 years. He speaks fluent Greek, English and Dutch. The IRIS ART CENTRE of took its name from the ancient goddess Iris. In Greek mythology, Iris is the personification of the rainbow and messenger of the gods. Iris links the gods to humanity. She travels with the speed of wind from one end of the world to the other, and into the depths of the sea and the underworld. As a goddess, Iris is associated with communication, messages, the rainbow and new endeavors. Iris personifies the free movement and exchange of thought, bearing the gift of divine inspiration, which strikes suddenly like the startling appearance of a rainbow in the sky. Like the rainbow’s infinite diversity of hues of color, the IRIS ART CENTRE seeks to gather people from all over the world and to be a place of artistic education, exchange, experimentation, and production. A place that is open to inspiration, creativity… and ever new messages from the gods! We welcome artists with limited mobility. The building, studio, bedrooms, bathrooms, the swimming pool and surrounding natural environment are all wheelchair-accessible. The sink in the studio can be used by people in a wheelchair. The Centre has an elevator.

name: Good Nature Foundation / Budapest
orgDescription: The LuppArt artists’ colony was founded in 2015 by a small group of people united by their fascination with Luppa Island’s beauty and potential to become an inspirational creative enterprise. Founders set up the colony on Luppa Island with the aim of providing an inspirational and welcoming setting for young artists. They gradually built up a place that not only exploited the island’s natural beauty but catered for all needs resident artists may have: from accommodation through tools and materials all the way to an inclusive, motivating atmosphere for all those who came to work at Luppa Island. Thus, the island came to represent the ideal environment for a prosperous artists’ colony. In addition, the Foundation started to manage the works created during the summer months, organising auctions and exhibitions with great success.
residencyDescription: Our popular Residency Programme, held every summer on Luppa Island, has been attracting a steady influx of artists at various stages of their professional career. The ideal conditions provided on the island together with the talent of our residents have resulted in the creation of a plethora of artworks, some of which we have acquired, thereby building our own collection. Following the success of the first few years, we decided to initiate a new phase in LuppArt’s history. Thus began a major expansion accompanied by a number of ambitious changes. From 2018 onwards, prospective residents may gain access to the programme in two different ways: by invitation or by submitting their application online. We have established a new advisory board responsible for the selection and invitation process. Members of this committee comprise a number of distinguished art world professionals representing established art magazines, a high-end commercial gallery, and a prestigious state museum, all of whom have been carefully selected to reflect the integrity of our new programme. Furthermore, we developed a programme of events held by professionals and open to all those interested in broadening their artistic horizons. These include workshops, presentations and discussions on a wide range of topics centred on the arts. Thus, we have opened a new chapter in our history, and hope to attract an increasingly diverse and rich international audience.

orgDescription: Kakslauttanen Arctic Resort is situated north from the Arctic Circle, close to the town Saariselkä in Finnish Lapland, next to Urho Kekkonen National Park. The Resort is built in the middle of a forest, surrounded by wild nature where the reindeer and other animals of the arctic zone wander. So, peace and quiet are guaranteed. The nearest airport is in Ivalo, 40 km from Kakslauttanen. The beautiful Inari -lake area is about 80 km away. Inside the Resort there is also an art gallery and a planetarium. The Kakslauttanen Art Gallery has an area of 450 m2 and holds 2-3 changing art exhibitions a year. The gallery also has an interesting sales collection of contemporary Finnish art.
residencyDescription: Kakslauttanen Arctic Resort provides a rent-free residency for (visual) artists from all over the world. The apartments or log houses are situated inside the resort, surrounded by forests and hills. The houses have a living room with kitchen and a bathroom. The kitchen is fully equipped and also bed linen and towels are provided. The house is free of any cost. Electricity, water and wi-fi are included. There is no separate artists´ studio, so it is preferable to work outside, for example painting, photographing or making sculptures by carving wood. The artists can sometimes also use a big tipi-like glass hut for working inside; it has natural light all around, or other facilities of the Resort. The resident artist is welcome to stay at Kakslauttanen from 1 week up to 3 weeks in the summer/autumn season (from June to end of September). name: Konstepidemin Gothenburg
orgDescription: INFECT SOCIETY WITH ART! Konstepidemin is located close to Linnéplatsen in central Gothenburg and consists of 14 buildings surrounded by a large park. The buildings were originally used as Gothenburg’s Epidemical Hospital. From 1886 until 1970 epidemic diseases were treated here. When a group of artists landed their vision of a center for art and culture in 1987 the initiative was named Konstepidemin. Today Konstepidemin is here with the mission to infect society with art. More than 130 artists from diverse artistic fields have their studios here, for example visual artists, musicians, writers, actors, filmmakers and dancers. Konstepidemin also functions as a cultural platform and offers an extensive public program of visual and performing art events, exhibitions, seminars, workshops and more. ORGANIZATION As an artist run organization, all projects derive from the artists working here and their collective effort to develop Konstepidemin. Konstepidemin is committed to equality, diversity, and preventing discrimination in all areas of the organization and its dealings. Konstepidemin collaborates with Swedish and International organizations and institutions. The organization is financed through rentals, sales, funds and yearly support from the City of Gothenburg, Region Västra Götaland and The Swedish Arts Council. ARTIST-IN-RESIDENCE Konstepidemin’s artist-in-residence program started in 1990. There are five studio apartments which are rented out to approximately 30 international artists, writers, musicians, curators and speakers annually. The productive artistic environment, and the opportunity to develop one’s artistry and projects, are important reasons why artists seek us out, and often return. GALLERI KONSTEPIDEMIN Galleri Konstepidemin exhibits contemporary art by Swedish and International artists and offers multiple venues, such as traditional exhibition space and more experimental venues suitable for installations and site-specific work. On average, 30 exhibitions are presented yearly, along with seminars, presentations and artist talks. ALLAS ATELJÉ – STUDIO FOR EVERYONE Allas Ateljé runs an art education programme for schools and preschools, as well as creative workshops both at Konstepidemin and other sites in the region. The workshops are held by professional artists and are based on an idea of being able to create together, regardless of age, gender or background. The process, imagination and freedom of creativity, rather than the final result, is in focus. EVOLUTION Konstepidemin has been in constant development since the start in 1987 and new projects are always moving forward. Activities are initiated by the members, for example BRA10 lectures and performance events and Ateljé Kollegiet, a residency with the mission to encourage interaction between cultural art expressions of diverse backgrounds. In 2013, Konstepidemin Publishing House was founded with the mission to further an in-depth conversation and nurture the relationship between the audience and the artistic practice. Several actors within music, theater, dance and film based on Konstepidemin develop performing art events and movie screenings for children and adults. Konstepidemin also collaborates with other initiatives in Gothenburg, such as GIBCA Extended, the satellite program of Göteborg International Biennial for Contemporary Art and Gothenburg Culture Festival. EXPERIENCE ART AND CULTURE AT KONSTEPIDEMIN At Konstepidemin you can experience performing art events, exhibitions, talks and other art interactions. In conjunction with Galleri Konstepidemin’s art openings (once a month during fall and spring) you can for example visit workshops, artist talks, performances and more. You can join Konstepidemins Vänner – Friends of Konstepidemin – and get invited to events where the artists at Konstepidemin takes you on a guided journey through their artistic process.

name: Kunstraum
orgDescription: In February 2015, we opened the gallery and artist-hub Kunstraum by the Navy Yard in Brooklyn. As an interdisciplinary team of curators, artists, and architects, we seek to promote emerging art, as well as outstanding exhibition concepts featuring both established and emerging art. Kunstraum is both a gallery and a studio space. Our concept features both a gallery and co-working space spread between two 1,000 square foot lofts. The lofts are situated in a beautifully renovated factory building in the historically artistic neighborhood of Clinton Hill. Kunstraum aims to redefine the way artists and curators collaborate. By opening our gallery to different art professionals interested in sharing engaging ideas, unconventional thinking, and risk taking, Kunstraum pushes the parameters of emerging, international, contemporary art. Kunstraum is born out of a necessity to create community and foster collaboration between artists, architects, curators, designers, filmmakers and writers. The Kunstraum model features excellent studio locations, networking, research opportunities and discourse for creative production. Kunstraum’s global identity is designed to offer and promote international mobility and visibility.
residencyDescription: Kunstraum is an artist-run hub, incubator and gallery space in Brooklyn offering 3 months, 6 months and 12 months residencies which includes studio workspace, studio visits, exhibition opportunities & professional services in Brooklyn.

name: Kyoto Art Center
orgDescription: Kyoto Art Center was conceived and established as a place for encountering various genres of art, as well as for the creation of the new culture through the revitalization of tradition developed in the city over its long history. This encounter will also connect to technology and industry, and furthermore to the everyday life of citizens, to bring a real fertility to the city. The activities of the Center will be divided into these three categories: (1) aid and support for young artists in whatever genre (2) collecting and dispatching of information concerning art and culture by means of various kinds of media (3) affording the chance for communication among the artists or between artists and citizens, especially by welcoming artists coming from in and out of the country as artists-in-residence. By fulfilling these activities, the Center is aiming to be the laboratory of creation for urban culture in the new century.
residencyDescription: Kyoto Art Center stands on the site of the former Meirin Elementary School, which was rebuilt in 1931. Design of Kyoto Art Center took into consideration the cultural value of the history of the school, the building facade, Japanese-style hall, auditorium, Japanese-style room, and other features. Renovations focused on creating an environment that would help stimulate unrestricted artistic activity, with emphasis on the maximum use of existing facilities.

orgDescription: LaSota Artist Studio was founded in order to give local and visiting artists a place to concentrate on projects in a comfortable, collaborative, and creative space. Our facility is located in a renovated historic catholic school building in Patton, PA, an old clayworks and timbering town located in the Appalachian Mountains, surrounded by hiking and biking trails and a 15-minute drive from Prince Gallitzin State Park. With its 12-foot high ceilings and large 7-foot windows, the studios have plenty of natural daylight and spacious workspaces for various artistic disciplines. Newly renovated apartments for artists in residence are conveniently located above the studios, on the second floor. The building is also equipped with a full woodshop, throwing wheels and a kiln, stained glass equipment, a gym, several kitchens, and laundry facilities.

name: La Becque | Artist Residency
orgDescription: Located on an exceptional slice of lakeside land on the shores of Lake Geneva between Vevey and Montreux, in proximity to all cultural and natural points of interest of Switzerland, La Becque | Artist Residency hosts and fosters the creativity of artists of all backgrounds and disciplines. Residents benefit from an exceptional site and infrastructure, conducive to accomplishing the project they have been selected for, whether it is focused on in-depth research or on production. La Becque offers state-of-the-art live and work infrastructure for creative residents. Its vast garden hosts a total of 8 fully-equipped live-and-work apartment, an additional 4 studios including a sound studio, a ceramic and wood workshop, a library and an event/conference space, as well as several rooms intended to facilitate shorter-term stays and projects alongside longer residency stays. Last but certainly not least, the site offers direct swimming access to Lake Geneva, and stunning views of both the lake and the surrounding Alps. The residency also benefits from direct contacts in most cultural as well as scientific institutions in Switzerland and leverages these for the benefit of its residents. La Becque dedicates particular attention to projects exploring the ever more intertwined notions of nature, the environment, and of technology. At the core of contemporary preoccupations and of growing urgency, these themes feed into all disciplines of the arts – and artists are among those best equipped to map out alternative relationships to both technology and nature.
residencyDescription: Participants to La Becque’s Principal Residency Program are selected globally by a transdisciplinary jury of experts. The program is open to both accomplished practitioners and up-and-coming candidates with a high potential for artistic growth. Applicants are evaluated on their practice as well as on the quality and pertinence of a residency project specifically written for their time at La Becque.

OUR MISSION IS TO STRENGTHEN THE ARTS AND CULTURE IN THE REGION OF EL CORONIL AND BROADEN THE OFFER OF CULTURAL AND ARTISTIC EVENTS TO THE PUBLIC AND CONTRIBUTE TO THE EDUCATIONAL SYSTEM IN THE REGION. WITH INNOVATIVE AND COLLABORATIVE PROGRAMS, WE TRY TO GIVE AN IMPULSE TO CREATIVITY AND THE ARTS, CREATING AN LASTING IMPACT IN THE COMMUNITY AND BEYOND. WE ARE A PUBLIC AND MULTI PURPOSE SPACE FOR CREATIVE RESEARCH, PRODUCTION AND PRESENTATION: A SPACE WHERE NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL ARTISTS WORK ON PROJECTS THAT INTENT TO DYNAMICALLY REINTERPRET THE RURAL AREA, CULTURE, CONVICTIONS AND PERCEPTIONS THAT BELONG TO IT. IN THIS WAY STIMULATING THE GROWTH, IDENTITY AND DIVERSENESS OF THE COMMUNITY WITH EXHIBITIONS, PRESENTATIONS, WORKSHOPS, EVENTS AND ACTIVITIES THAT INVOLVE AND ENRICH IT. ASIDE FROM OFFERING AN INSPIRING WORKING SPACE, WE PROVIDE THE MEANS AND SUPPORT TO OUR ARTISTS IN RESIDENCE, GIVING THEM ACCESS TO MATERIAL, TOOLS AND A NETWORK OF PRACTICAL AND PROFESIONAL CONTACTS. THE SQUARE HOUSE BECOMES A MEETING POINT, CULTIVATING AN ATMOSPHERE WHERE IDEAS CAN DEVELOP AND TRANSFORM INTO CONCRETE PROJECTS THAT BENEFIT THE SOCIETY AS A WHOLE.

Además de ser alojamiento rural una parte del año, la casa tiene como principal finalidad acoger propuestas relacionadas con el arte en el entorno rural, con la naturaleza, el cuerpo y los cuidados. La Casa Móvil is a private and self-financed project that opens its doors in the rural and natural environment of the Sierra de Cádiz (Spain), to generate meeting spaces between artists, to democratize art in its various expressions and bring it closer to everyone. . name: La Ceiba Gráfica
orgDescription: Set in a lovingly-restored hacienda dating back to the 16th century La Ceiba Gráfica is an Art Center that specializes in teaching, producing and researching traditional graphic arts. The center is specialized in stone lithography using Mexican marble, Japanese wood-block printing and metal etching. Many artists in Mexico have produced graphic work at our center. There are also workshops dedicated to linoleum, woodcut, paper-making, letterpress and carpentry. The grand and tranquil spaces of the hacienda together with its terraces and gardens are uniquely conducive to creative work.
residencyDescription: La Ceiba Gráfica invites people from all over the world to come and experience an environment where art, natural beauty and traditional manual techniques come together.

name: La Devignère
orgDescription: ‘La Devignère’ is a rambling house dating from the 15th century. It has been a place dedicated to artistic activities since 1992, when it became the headquarters of a theatre company. Since then, it has hosted many artists of all disciplines. The Irish-French owners, Zoë O’Reilly and Alain Servant, are hosts of this exceptional place, now fully restored. They propose residencies in all fields of creative and research activities. Over the years, La Devignère has become part of the local cultural landscape. The house is located in a peaceful rural setting, surrounded by fields and native woodlands, and by a rich human network. The owners live between Ireland and France with their son and their cat. Alain is an actor, theatre director, musician and Tai Ji Quan practitioner. Zoë is a researcher and visual ethnographer working in the area of migration, borders and cultural diversity, and also a yoga practitioner. They love creating an environment for sharing and exchange, and they also love to cook!
residencyDescription: ‘La Devignère’ is open to writers, artists and researchers of all disciplines needing time and space for writing, reflection and research.

We are interested in each person in the house developing his or her own vision. One story is not the same for everyone. We are enriched by relating to each other. Everyone sees something different from the same thing. Curiosity and the desire to know how the other person sees is our way of communicating. This is how we live.

orgDescription: La Macina di San Cresci is an open laboratory for artistic projects, a retreat, a place of contemplation and creativity, founded by two lifelong art lovers skilled in design and architecture, Duccio Trassinelli and Demetria Verduci. We believe art and offer artists an opportunity to work in a social environment that is quite different from the urban milieu that is the usual context of production and distribution of the contemporary arts. This new experience provides artists with a major stimulus to experiment with new ideas, approaches and modes of production, encouraging artists to rethink and renegotiate their role in such unfamiliar social contexts. Our mission is to encourage the mobility of artists and to develop a cultural exchange; As we are in the field of art, we have invested in La Macina to make it a place to accommodate and imagine new forms of dialogue within the context of art and culture. The residency is located in the historic complex of the Pieve di San Cresci, X sec. the oldest in the Chianti area; it began to be mentioned in 948. We have restored this architectural complex for long fifteen years and for us it was like a dream to revive such an extraordinary building.
residencyDescription: Artist residency covers a program based on the personal project proposal presented by the artist and consist of sojourning from 7 to 90 days . name: La Maison Ocre
orgDescription: Founded in 2018 with the idea of ​​creating a cultural space in the heart of the countryside, La Maison Ocre is the result of the renovation of a ruined former agricultural building, incorporating the foundations of a 15th-century chapel. Since 2018, we have organized a variety of artistic events: classical concerts with string quartets, classical choirs, guitar duos, and singers presenting their own compositions. We have also hosted open mic nights for everyone, welcoming actors, musicians, singers, and more. La Maison Ocre has also offered music and painting workshops for adults and children. As artists ourselves, we understand the need to sometimes escape our daily lives to see things differently and begin the creative process. Therefore, hosting artists preparing their work is a natural extension of our activities, whether they are alone, in groups, or with their families. Since then, we have converted a barn on the property into an artists’ studio equipped with basic materials for visual arts, recording, and music rehearsals. Located in a very quiet hamlet between Toulouse and Carcassonne, the house is not completely isolated; you can find the kind of interaction you desire in the countryside, in just the right amount. Nearby towns include Mirepoix (10 minutes), Castelnaudary (20 minutes), Limoux (30 minutes), and the Mediterranean Sea (an hour and a half). The detached building comprises a large, bright studio on the ground floor with two entrances, a toilet, and a sink, along with a kitchenette. Upstairs, a 30m² mezzanine can serve as a small conference room, computer room, or lounge. Both rooms are equipped to accommodate painters, musicians, sculptors, writers… Also on the first floor are two bedrooms with private bathrooms that can accommodate up to four people. At Maison Ocre, just a few meters away, we can supplement your occasional or pre-arranged needs with two additional bedrooms, a large room, and meals; we can also help out in case you forget something… La Maison Ocre est une structure privée auto financée, gérée pas les deux artistes, sans aucune subvention. Les activités se déroulent soit en privé ou soit sous le nom de l’association créativité (loi 1901) créée en 1998. Maison Ocre is a self-funded, privately run organization managed by the two artists without any subsidies. Activities take place either privately or under the name of the association Créativité (a non-profit organization under the 1901 French law), created in 1998.
residencyDescription: There is no fixed residency program, however the artist can organize a private or public presentation in our dedicated hall at the end of their stay; a sound system and audio-visual equipment are at their disposal.

name: La Maison verte du jardin botanique
orgDescription: Since the autumn 2013 the Botanical Garden of Marnay-sur-Seine is running creation and research residencies within the artistic program Pays’Art at La Maison Verte. This place is directly linked to the Botanical Garden and opens itself to artists of all nationalities to have a time of creativity, reflection and production in a rural environment. The Board of the Association has entrusted Guillaume Reby to run the residency program of La Maison Verte. The team of the Botanical Garden is also supporting the artists in their needs. The Botanical Garden of Marnay-sur-Seine is an association created in 1995 on the initiative of sculptor Didier Rousseau Navarre, supported financially by the Tenot Foundation, then by the Tenot Family. The Botanical Garden of Marnay-sur-Seine gave itself as a principal objective the creation of the first Botanical Garden in Champagne-Ardenne. This garden has received the epithets of “Jardin Botanique de France et des Pays Francophones” and “Jardin remarquable”. This place is mainly aimed at environmental education and the initiation into natural sciences, also sensitizing those towards environmental issues. Being a recognized Botanical Garden of France, it also contributes towards scientific research and conservation. To learn more about the Botanical Garden of Marnay-sur-Seine please visit: www.jardin-botanique.org
residencyDescription: The Botanical Garden of Marnay-sur-Seine (one hour from Paris) offers residencies of creation and research at La Maison Verte within the artistic program Pays’Art.

To make the artist feel as if they were in their own studio, working freely, developing, experimenting, researching and achieving the highest quality as a final result. orgDescription: La Manchoza is an independent, artist-run organization dedicated to supporting self-directed artistic practice through residency programs, creative infrastructure, and engagement with place. Located in the mountains near Tapalpa, Jalisco, Mexico, the project brings together art, architecture, sustainable living, and material experimentation within a rural environment. Founded by sculptor Ana Paula Luna and programmer and builder Juan Lanzagorta, La Manchoza operates as a small-scale, hands-on initiative where artists are encouraged to develop their work with autonomy, focus, and access to adaptable creative spaces. The organization supports a range of disciplines, including sculpture, ceramics, painting, writing, and interdisciplinary practices. Rooted in principles of curiosity, craftsmanship, sustainability, and creative freedom, La Manchoza seeks to foster meaningful artistic development while remaining closely connected to the landscape, local knowledge, and the evolving process of making.

name: La Muse
orgDescription: La Muse is first and foremost a large old house nestled in the heart of a village in the Montagne Noire, north of Carcassonne. The ten rooms all overlook a densely wooded valley, a vast and soothing landscape, which promotes concentration. There is a sunny terrace in the afternoon that runs along the building and a small shaded garden to stay cool in the summer. In the library, exchanges and conversations in all languages often are heard in front of the fire. Adjacent to a Gothic, pastel chapel, the artists’ studio sometimes turns into an exhibition space at the end of a residence. And both kitchens are places to share recipes and laughs.
residencyDescription: At La Muse, you come to write, paint, draw, photograph, compose a concerto or a song… It is also the ideal place to reflect on a project, imagine a novel, complete a doctoral thesis, be inspired by nature or its readings and explore new ways of being. Everyone is free, without constraints, to write a hundred pages a day or to dream of the perfect canvas, to spend their days alone or to share the creative energy of other residents, to go to mushrooms in the undergrowth or to (re)read the seven volumes of In Search of Lost Time.

name: La Porte Peinte Centre pour les Arts
residencyName: La Porte Peinte Centre pour les Arts
orgDescription: La Porte Peinte is an international arts centre located in Noyers sur Serein, a medieval village in Burgundy that is recognized as one of the 100 most beautiful villages in France. Based in a rambling medieval half-timbered building that leans out over the village square like something from a fairy tale, La Porte Peinte offers artists, makers, musicians and writers in residence the opportunity to engage in creative exploration and exchange in an unusually inspiring and supportive environment. Doors opened in September 2011 with the first artists in residence and the launch of the 160 m2 ground-floor gallery. 2014 saw the opening of a café/tea room and a shop. La Porte Peinte’s nine comfortable bedrooms can house up to 15 people. Workshop spaces and event spaces are available for classes and performances. Along with private residency accommodation, each creator in residence chooses the private studio space most suited to their practice on a first booked, first served basis. Co-founders: Hiro Ota and Michelle Anderson La Porte Peinte est un centre international pour les arts situé a Noyers sur Serein, un village médieval de Bourgogne reconnu pour sa beauté et son architecture. Notre but est d’offrir des opportunités d’exploration, de travail et d’échange créatif dans un environnement propice à l’inspiration. En septembre 2011 nous avons ouvert la galerie, avec 160 m2 répartis en quatre pièces attenantes, et en avril 2014 notre café/salon de thé et boutique y ont vu le jour. Notre programme de résidence artistique propose des ateliers de travail créatif, des espaces dédiés aux stages et aux évènements, ainsi que de l’hébergement privé pour les artistes, les artisans, les musiciens et les écrivains. Chaque créateur en résidence choisit sa chambre préférée ainsi que l’atelier le plus adapté à sa pratique créative. Co-fondateurs : Hiro Ota et Michelle Anderson
residencyDescription: La Porte Peinte is first and foremost a haven and sanctuary for creative work. A residency here is designed to enable creative exploration, concentrated work and exchange in an inspiring and supportive environment.

orgDescription: La Tempéra is a place for artistic development and exchange in rural areas, created in 2016 by Isabelle de Voldère, a painter who graduated from the Ecole des Beaux-Arts de Paris and restores paintings. La Tempéra comprises several houses in the hamlet of Château-du-Bois, located between the Nièvre and Yonne regions, two hours from Paris. We welcome artists, writers and creative people looking for a quiet place to concentrate on their projects, in the countryside and in contact with other creative people. We also organize painting and sculpture exhibitions, concerts and painting courses. The place is called La Tempéra in reference to a traditional painting technique based on natural products: eggs, blanc de Meudon and pigments, a technique we use to restore old paintings.

name: La Wayaka Current
orgDescription: La Wayaka Current is a fluid & nomadic artist-led project, seeking new ecological and cultural perspectives in our global societies through exchange with indigenous communities in remote natural environments. In reaction to a loss of connection between humans and nature we use art and creative research as ways to explore, reconnect and communicate ideas for a more conscious and sustainable future planet. LWC has made projects in natural biomes across the planet from Northern Norway to Central and South America, working in partnership with indigenous groups, organizations and individuals experienced in fields of culture and ecology. As the project moves we create channels for people to join, explore and connect to social, cultural and ecological themes through our on the ground experiences as well as online platform and community and exhibitions. These channels strive to support and promote awareness of endangered natural environments around the globe alongside local communities whose invaluable knowledge, ancient cultural traditions, cosmology and contemporary practices and relationship to the natural world all provide alternative perspectives to the destructive patterns of economic and political structures in the west that have led to the environmental degradation of many areas.
residencyDescription: Since 2015, we have developed site-responsive programs across our planet. Itinerant in our nature our expeditions lead people to experiment, work and develop projects in vast natural environments. Our fluid programs with local communities and partners, connect to indigenous + ecological knowledge. We relate and connect to the daily life and reality of a place, to engage with relevant issues of our time.

orgDescription: Laboratorio del Eco is a nonprofit that produces unique art experiences such as concerts, exhibitions and immersive experiences with technologies including 3D sound spatialization, data sonification, generative & algorithmic art. We also host “sesiones del eco/club de lo efimero” sessions. A monthly event providing a meeting space in Valparaiso for audiences and artists to share, where we usually have live arts such as music, sound art, sound poetry, performance, dance. We are currently based in Cerro Alegre in Valparaiso in a heritage house with ample space for inspiration and artistic practices.

name: Læsø Artist in Residence
orgDescription: Læsø AiR For many years, art has been an inextricable part of Læsø’s identity, and for almost two centuries the island has played a major role in the life and work of some of Denmark’s greatest artists. What is particularly special is how the unique artistic retreats of two of Denmark’s and the world’s most acclaimed artists – Asger Jorn (1914-1973) and Per Kirkeby (1938-2018) – have been recreated and preserved. The nature, tranquillity, contemplation and the ability to escape from the bustle of the metropolitan art scene whenever they needed to, were essential for these two artists. Now, as a result of collaboration with a number of recognised partners in the Danish and international art worlds, Læsø AiR (Læsø Artist in Residence) will ensure that the retreats of the two artists remain a symbol of history and the artists’ work and residence on the island, serving as inspiration and support for future generations of artists.
residencyDescription: The objective of the Læsø AiR programme for professional visual artists is to support the development of new and valuable relationships with fellow artists, the community on Læsø, the island’s unique nature, and the history of Per Kirkeby and Asger Jorn — all for the benefit of the regional art scene and Nordic contemporary art in general.

name: LAiR Arts Association
residencyName: L’AiR Arts International Arts Research Residency at Atelier 11 Cité Falguière in Paris
orgDescription: L’AiR Arts is a not-for-profit organisation (une association à but non lucratif soumise à la loi 1901) with a mission to support intercultural exchange through international arts residency programs. In collaboration with leading arts institutions and professionals, our residency programs support intercultural exchange, research, professional development and contemporary creation – while promoting diversity, inclusion and international understanding through artistic and cultural heritage. Located in Montparnasse, known as a historic hub for international artists during the 20th century, L’AiR Arts program is dedicated to the intercultural artistic exchange as the legacy of the École de Paris. Working in close partnership with the Cité Falguière Association, since 2021 L’AiR Arts leads a cultural heritage project of preserving the last remaining atelier of the prominent artists community of Cité Falguière. Once home to Gauguin, Modigliani, Soutine, Foujita, and Brancusi, Atelier 11 Cité Falguière now operates as an International Arts Research Residency, hosting artists and cultural professionals from all over the world. As part of this living heritage initiative, L’AiR Arts welcomes local and international professionals for self-directed individual projects, that run in parallel to curated group programs, partner residencies and events open to a broader community. *L’AiR Arts name is a French version of a standard acronym for Artists-in-Residence, it can also be read as Lair, artist’s lair or a studio / atelier where artist lives, works, and develops ideas – a safe haven designed to support the creative process.
residencyDescription: Located in Montparnasse, known as a historic hub for international artists in the beginning of the 20th century, the L’AiR Arts residency program grounds its commitment to contemporary arts within a historical perspective. Focusing on intercultural artistic exchange as the legacy of the École de Paris, the residency not only provides the opportunity to explore Paris and have a space in which to comfortably stay and work, it also offers an insider’s view into the important role that international artists have played in Paris from the late 19th century to the present day.

Artists are invited to apply all year round, though April to October are the more comfortable months in Fiji. The property has a large studio with ocean outlooks and a spacious house with three queen size bedrooms, one with ensuite. The rooms are air conditioned with private decks. There is a large living room with two separate dining areas. Full kitchen, TV , Internet, laundry facilities and shared bathroom. The generous outdoor garden includes a large in ground pool. name: Laura Liebeskind Residencies
orgDescription: Ever since 2022, I, Laura Liebeskind, an artist with a lot of experiences in being an artist in residency myself, have renovated this beautiful retreat in one of the areas of earliest settlements in Germany together with some of my artist friends. From May till September each year, we want to open our gates for fellow international artists at the heart of a small village with 140 people, with a local potterer, a hair dresser and a little Bakery in a nearby village, which is all the immediate local commerce there is. You will be surrounded by fields and woods and little dirt roads lined by fruit trees, ready to be picked. There will be two private rooms and two private work places for 2 artists in residency or up to two couples. But you will most likely be all to yourself. – If there are other artists in residency present, you will share one bathroom and kitchen area as well as one big common room, where there is a grand piano and a lovely lounge area with dinner table. If you wanted to turn the space into a yoga or dance space, you may. The space also allows for concerts. Nearby there are two open pools in summer. One of them recently won the “best open pool of Germany” price. You will also find the museum of “The arch of Nebra” which exhibits one of the eldest evidences of human art, alongside many other museums, castles and vineyards. This part of Germany is called “German Tuscany”.

name: Les Ateliers du Moulin
orgDescription: We are an independent artist residency located in an 11th-century watermill in the heart of the Périgord Noir, France. We welcome artists from all disciplines into a setting where history, nature, and creative reflection come together. Each year, we invite one artist for a fully funded residency in exchange for a site-specific work created during their stay. In parallel, we offer a limited number of self-funded residencies open to international artists seeking time and space for focused work. Stays typically range from two weeks to one month. Our restored mill combines rustic elegance with calm and comfort, providing an inspiring atmosphere for deep creation. Surrounded by forests, rivers, and the rich cultural heritage of the Dordogne, the residency encourages a reconnection with slowness, beauty, and place. In addition to our residency program, we curate a selection of intimate workshops — either led by us or in collaboration with other creators — that explore craft, nature, and artistic experimentation.
residencyDescription: We are a fully independent, artist-run residency. name: LIA-Leipzig International Art Programme
orgDescription: LIA is s a 13 year old institution which welcomed around 400 international artists since 2007. It is based at the Spinnerei, home of over one hundred artist studios as well as galleries and art institutions. Here the Rundgang, Gallery Tour, takes place three times a year, when around 8000 guests from Germany and abroad come to visit and discover art of all media on one weekend. The LIA programme is open to all age groups and nationalities. There are five studios which are given away for three or six months periods. Artists are taken care of by the programme coordinator Marina Diaz and LIA founder Anna-Louise Rolland personally. There is a monthly programme of art critic studio visits, excursions and talks within the art community. Artists may apply directly at LIA. Fellowships are granted by The New York Academy of Art, School of Visual Arts New York City, Brno University of Technology, STAL Gallery in Sultanat Oman, Sydney University and the Goethe-Institut Copenhagen as well as the Goethe-Institutes of the Pacific region publishing regular calls. Currently the projects Nordic-Leipzig and Pacific- Leipzig are running in LIA supported by the Goethe-Institut. For further information please see: www.LIAp.eu. To apply please see the application link on that site.
residencyDescription: LIA-Leipzig International Art Programme is a place for experiment and learning within an international and local art community. The thirteen year old art programme and nonprofit artist residency hosts five international studios at the same time and is based at the Spinnerei Leipzig, a 10 hectare large former cotton factory of over one hundred artist studios as well as art institutions. The Programme philosophy is to create impulses through exchanging ideas and knowledge as well as artistic traditions with the local art community and learning in cooperations. We believe that leaving a comfort zone opens new perspectives, international exchange broadens mind sets and widens creative approaches. The confrontation with the other fosters new ways of thinking and experimenting. It allows tolerance and new ways of thinking. Project partner besides the Atelier für Radierung is the Grassi Museum für Völkerkunde zu Leipzig and its anthropological collection. There is a monthly programme artists may participate in of art critic visits, excursions, community talks, open studios and the Rundgang exhibitions while artists and LIA staff talk about the artists work to the public and engage artists and the public in a dialogue.

name: LINZ FMR
orgDescription: FMR – Festival for Art in Digital Contexts and Public Spaces is a biennial festival showcasing artistic processes and positions that reflect the ephemeral nature of our digitally connected present. The continuous digitalization of everyday life creates an intense overlap and layering of familiar physical and intricately interwoven digital spaces. FMR focuses on the shifts, distortions, and rifts that arise in this process and presents contemporary artistic perspectives in this context. The festival, whose title alludes to ephemerality and transience, presents works whose initial ideas originate in virtual-digital spaces or have a strong connection to it but are displayed — sometimes in a transformed manner — in physical surroundings, specifically in the public and open space. The emphasis is on the interstitial spaces that emerge during these transformations — outside of museums, galleries, or conventional art spaces. At the same time, FMR seeks to update the concept of sculpture for the contemporary era while reflecting on questions of transience, ephemerality and obviousness.
residencyDescription: FMR – Festival for Art in Digital Contexts and Public Spaces is a biennial festival showcasing artistic processes and positions that reflect the ephemeral nature of our digitally connected present. orgDescription: List og Land is a self-directed, multi-disciplinary residency, situated on 4200 acres of land on Arnafjördur, one of the deepest and most beautiful fjords in Iceland. We are 20 minutes from the majestic Dynjandi waterfall, often referred to as The Jewell of the Westfjords. The land is surrounded by black sand beaches, waterfalls, rivers and wildlife including seals, whales, arctic fox, mink and many, many birds. List og Land, (Icelandic for “Art and Land,”) is open to photographers, writers, and painters. We currently do not have a ceramics or music studio, though we are expanding to accommodate more creative disciplines. Our mission is to provide emerging and established artists and writers the time and space to focus entirely on their work. We consider the land and the surrounding beauty of our residency, an environment that fosters inspiration, community and collaboration. We strive to create a warm and inviting space for nurturing creativity and friendship. For more information on our mission click here: https://listogland.com/about/
residencyDescription: List of Land provides shared studio space for seven artists/writers. Some rooms have private studio space. Each artist/writer can choose from our private, comfortable accommodations with gorgeous views of the sea and mountains. For more information on our accommodations click here: https://listogland.com/apply/ and here: https://listogland.com/gallery/ Bathrooms (two in the main house, one in the barn) are shared. A beautiful living area and large dining room with views of the sea all around create a warm and comfortable space for reading, resting and enjoying the company of your fellow artists. The large fully equipped kitchen is shared among residents. We have a hot tub and pool and soon we will also provide a sauna. Internet access, laundry room, linens and towels are provided. Our rates depend on what room you choose. Our largest and newest rooms provide private studio space. Many of the rooms can accommodate collaborative couples for a small extra fee. Please check here: https://listogland.com/apply/ The residency fee must be paid six weeks before arrival. Artists take care of their own expenses for transportation, meals, and art supplies. We will pick you up at the Ísafjörður airport.

name: Literárne rezidencie Košice / Košice Literary Residencies
residencyName: Literárne rezidencie Košice / Košice Literary Residencies
orgDescription: The residency program is overseen by the Club of National Minorities. The Club brings together 11 national communities from Košice and organises significant city events every year. For over 15 years, the Club has also operated the Memorial Room of Sándor Márai. Through its activities and presence on the cultural map of Košice, the Club emphasises and contributes to preserving the multicultural and multiethnic character of the city. In recent years, the Club has expanded its mission to include the establishment of a literary residency centre. Since its foundation, the residency programme has regularly provided residencies for Ukrainian women artists (Olga Bizul, Katya Slonova, Oksana Savchenko, Olga Bragina, Dasha Suzdalova). In 2021, the programme launched the international Epic Residencies programme, which, with partner institutions in Norway and Iceland, has organised 12 residential exchanges of Slovak writers with Icelandic and Norwegian authors through the EEA Grants programme. In 2023, the programme collaborated with the Czech Jiří Orten Prize and provided a residency for the prize winner Filip Kleg. In 2023, residency programme carried out two mobilities – a presentation of Slovak literature in Iceland (Reykjavík Literary Festival) and in Stavanger, Norway (Kapittel – festival of literature and free speech). At these prestigious festivals, the programme presented Slovak authors together with excerpts of works into English, translated by John Minahane, Isabel Stainsby, and James Sutherland-Smith. Writer Residencies Košice also took part in the 2023 conference of the Res Artis network of art residency providers in London. Following the conference, Writer Residencies Košice would like to become a member of the international Res Artis network to channel its open calls to the international space, thanks to Res Artis platforms.
residencyDescription: Literary Residencies Košice were established in 2021 as a residency program in Košice intended for writers from Slovakia and the surrounding region. name: A4 Residency Art Center
orgDescription: Located in Chengdu, China, A4 Residency Art Center is a multidisciplinary international platform integrating creation, networking, and resource-sharing. We are committed to fostering global creative collisions and innovation through residency programs while bridging creative culture with business and community engagement. Since 2011, we have collaborated with 335 creators from over 44 countries and regions, spanning diverse fields such as artists, scientists, writers, poets, scholars, musicians, architects, designers, and brand founders. A4 Residency provides professional cross-disciplinary support, empowering creators to push boundaries. Leveraging extensive industry expertise and a robust global network, we facilitate meaningful connections and resource transformation across industries. As an active advocate for social responsibility, we continuously explore innovative ways to integrate creativity into community development, shaping new lifestyles for the public. By strategically merging creativity with diverse resources, we drive business innovation, offering creators expansive exposure and collaboration opportunities. This synergy cultivates a sustainable ecosystem where art and resources thrive together. History From experimental exploration of contemporary art to community-based interdisciplinary co-creation, we have initiated in-depth exchanges and collaborations with 335 artists/groups, curators, and scholars from more than 44 countries and regions, and have continuously adjusted our systematic structure and goals in the course of more than ten years of exploration. In 2011, as part of the A4 Art Museum’s development strategy, the A4 Artist in Residence International Exchange Program (ARIE) was officially launched. The program is committed to promoting annual exchanges of contemporary art and culture around the globe, encouraging artists or art groups with unique creative ideas and notable accomplishments in art research to create, communicate, and exhibit based on local culture, and further promoting cultural interactions within their regions. Throughout this process, the participants would embark on distinctive experimental endeavors, propelled by the engines of cultural differences and local connections. ARIE is not only built on the remarkable creativity and curiosity of the artists themselves but also on the cross-cultural institutional and social networks, as well as the creators’ aspirations. A profound sense of self-worth motivates us to provide local spaces and planning services for artists and researchers from different countries and regions. In October 2019, upon completion of the A4 Residency Art Center, it connected surrounding public spaces and outdoor areas with itself. The establishment of the Residency Art Center opened new opportunities for artist exhibitions, public art projects, cultural events, regional interactions, and symbiotic innovation. We have also fostered extensive exchanges and collaborations with the surrounding community and businesses, connecting different people and institutions. An important feature of this phase is the transformation from individual experimentation and creativity towards communication and cooperation with the local context. Through this process, we have continuously reflected on the significance of linking to understand the essence of communication better. In 2023, A4 Residency Art Center embarked on a new beginning as a more independent and interdisciplinary cultural institution, committed to serving the public. Aligned with our new goals and mission, we are determined to present ourselves to the public through a more proactive, collaborative, and community-oriented approach, and we are prepared for public inquiries and discussions. name: Mabiang Seni Art Residency
orgDescription: Mabiang Seni starts from the etymology of the word ‘biang’ in the local balinese dialect, meaning ‘mother’. In Bahasa Indonesia itself, ‘biang’ can also represent the roots, the origin of something. It is a tribute to the owner, who is a mother of three, able to support the main vision of the team: to let art be as nurturing and deep-rooted as a maternal figure in your life. With that, our mission is to be able to create an environment that enables artists to develop their own artistic visions, supported by room for growth through their art practice and constructive dialogues –between you and your artwork, between you and other artists. In the future as we develop this on-site and off-site, we would like to strengthen the artistic environment as a whole by promoting other art facilities, museums, galleries, and other art-related facilities in Bali.

name: MacDowell
orgDescription: Founded in 1907 by composer Edward MacDowell and pianist Marian MacDowell, his wife, MacDowell nurtures the arts by awarding Fellowships to artists of exceptional talent, providing time, space, and an inspiring environment in which they can do creative work. The sole criterion for acceptance is talent, as determined by a panel representing the discipline of the applicant. The more than 8,000 artists who have benefited from a residency at MacDowell include such notables as Willa Cather, Aaron Copland, Thornton Wilder, Leonard Bernstein, James Baldwin, Jonathan Franzen, and Suzan-Lori Parks, to name but a few. A registered National Historic Landmark, MacDowell was awarded the National Medal of Arts in 1997.
residencyDescription: A MacDowell Fellowship (awarded through a competitive application process) consists of a residency up to eight weeks and includes a private studio, housing, and three meals per day. MacDowell is designed to facilitate a balance between social interaction and focus on work. Private studios available to artists 24 hours a day, together with the dining and recreation rooms at the main hall, combine to provide an environment adaptable to each individual’s needs. To ensure all autonomy and privacy, no artist-in-residence may visit another’s studio without invitation. Breakfast and dinner are served in the dining room, while lunch is delivered to each studio. After dinner, presentations are a traditional, elective part of the stimulating and supportive environment. Readings, slide shows, open studios, and informal performances allow artists to become acquainted with and inspired by one another’s work. Friendships established among artists-in-residence often lead to collaborations and connections beyond MacDowell.
disciplines: Which disciplines does your residency cater to?:
facilities: What practical facilities does your residency offer to artists?:
fundingDetails: There is no cost for a Fellowship in order to open the residency experience to a wider, more diverse community of artists, however, MacDowell offers two financial assistance programs to those who have financial need and have been awarded a Fellowship. Travel reimbursement grants are available to defray the cost of domestic and international travel to and from New Hampshire. Need-based stipends are available to artists who would not otherwise be able to afford the time away that a Fellowship requires. Stipends may be used to cover rent, utilities, childcare, and other expenses that accrue during a residency. They may also be directed toward equipment costs and to replace lost income. Artists may apply for these stipends and travel grants only if they are awarded a MacDowell Fellowship.

orgDescription: Myself and my husband run 8day retreats in Life drawing, stone carving, journalling and tempera painting during the spring and early summer and then again in the autumn. We pride ourselves in offering a safe and happy environment for people in any stage of their artistc developement to come and work. We offer excellent food and comfortable rooms to make your stay just what you need to immerse yourself in your art. The house has been in the family for 400 years, with most members of the family having been artists, and unspoilt as it is by modernisation, inspiration abounds. I am currently looking into how I can bring the local French community to become a part of this retreat, maybe with exhibiting opportunities or liasing with the Academie D’Art in Avignon.
residencyDescription: Life drawing is the corner stone of most art practices and on this program we offer 5 full days of life drawing with different models daily. The focus is on self-discovery and bringing out ones talent through experimentation with mediums as well as learning the nuts and bolts of constructing the figure. The objective is to deepen one’s understanding of drawing the human figure, by increasing our ability to observe, whilst letting go of old fears and misconceptions.

name: Maison Les Buis
residencyName: Maison Les Buis Rural Artist Retreat
orgDescription: Maison Les Buis is situated in a small peaceful hamlet in South West France. It comprises several historic buildings, surrounding a large enclosed courtyard. Its land extends to four and a half hectares, offering immediate and constant immersion in nature. The ambience is peaceful and simple and has that special energy, calling for the imaginal, the wild, the nebulous. The nature is rich, varied and expansive with mossy trees, flowery meadows and a magical wild pond. It’s a wondrous place with infinite possibilities. We invite artists, creators, makers and all curious daydreamers who seek a place to come to quietness and to create.
residencyDescription: Our objective is to offer space to help connect to the wonder child, to the spontaneity and the innocence of the ‘not knowing’. Receptivity is the keyword, we are all artists for we cannot help but create, the aim is to stay receptive, attentive so that we catch that precious moment of inspiration. This is important and can be a challenge in the midst of a busy world with information overload. This residency is about giving yourself Space and Time to breathe, to become empty so that there is room for new seeds to germinate and grow into a flower that has not been seen before.

name: Maison Losseau
orgDescription: La résidence d’écriture et de création mise en place par la Fondation Losseau et le Secteur Littérature de la Province de Hainaut est située à Mons (Belgique), sur le site de la Maison Losseau, un hôtel particulier Art Nouveau à vocation muséale et un bâtiment contemporain comprenant un centre d’interprétation, des salles d’exposition(s) et un centre de littérature qui regroupent quelques écrivains d’archives littéraires du Hainaut tels que (Marcel Moreau, Claire Lejeune, Fernand Dumont…). le nouveau projet de résidence d’écriture et de création prolongée et complète les missions de la Fondation Losseau et du secteur littérature dans le domaine de la valorisation du patrimoine et, surtout, de l’aide à la création littéraire, en lien avec d’ autres formes d’expression artistique. Nous souhaitons soutenir les écrivains (poètes, romanciers, dramaturges, essayistes) et les chercheurs en leur offrant la possibilité de s’extraire, dans un temps limité, de la vie quotidienne et en les invitant à explorer, sans que cela soit limitatif ou limitatif, le ressources mises à leur disposition sur le site, notamment nos riches archives littéraires ou historiques, dont ils peuvent s’inspirer pour développer un projet original. L’équipe de la Maison Losseau leur fournira le matériel nécessaire au processus de création. Il s’attachera à faciliter les échanges culturels et le dialogue entre les habitants, les artistes soutenus par les Secteurs du spectacle et des arts plastiques de la Province de Hainaut, les créateurs et les habitants du territoire du Hainaut.

name: Maison Saint Joseph
orgDescription: Maison Saint-Joseph (msj) is a transdisciplinary art residency housed in a classified Historic Monument in Crépy-en-Valois, France — a 17th-century family home, ~ 35 minutes by train from Paris Nord train station. Since 2022, msj has offered time and space for the kind of work the world interrupts. Open to all art forms — visual arts, writing, performance, music, architecture, film — it welcomes artists, authors, designers, researchers, and performers for residencies of 1 week to 2 months, individual or collective. msj is run almost entirely by volunteers. Every residency is made possible by hundreds of hours of unpaid work and in-kind support from a transdisciplinary community that believes creation matters. Residents have access to accommodation within the house, shared workspaces, a wood workshop, research library, technical mentoring, and an international artist network spanning France, the United Kingdom, the United States, Tunisia, Morocco, India and beyond. msj does not seek to answer questions. It seeks to formulate them. We believe art is not separate from politics, from memory, from the body, from what we owe each other. The walls are old. The questions are yours. The house is a refuge for creation. Above all, it is a family home.
residencyDescription: msj offers residencies of 1 week to 2 months, open to all disciplines, visual arts, writing, performance, music, architecture, film, and beyond. Residencies are individual or collective, with two formats: a full residency (accommodation and all services included) and a local residency for artists based nearby, with access to workspaces and mentoring without overnight stay.

The residency encourages artists to immerse themselves in the traditional culture of the remote Manang region and respond to this remarkable location through their art practice. The residency aims to introduce participants to the local culture and landscape through periodic excursions and daily interaction with locals. We are open twice a year in Spring and Autumn for a period of two months. Stays from 2 weeks to 2 months are available from April 1 and October 1. residencyDescription: The Manang Artist Residency was founded by Nepali Architect Amar Gurung and Australian artist Jo Rankine. We are an artist-run organisation. orgDescription: MANTILITY is a contemporary cultural platform based in Kavala, Greece, operating at the intersection of art, design, and material culture. The platform has developed partnerships with major museums in Greece, as well as festivals and cultural organizations, expanding its presence within the contemporary cultural landscape. MANTILITY maintains a retail presence in Athens, along with selected collaborations in various Greek islands, creating a distributed network that connects design, production, and audience. Alongside its design identity, MANTILITY has developed EPÀRCHÎA Design Boîte in its home city of Kavala — a hybrid cultural space that operates as an exhibition venue, café-bar, concept store, and MANTILITY Silk Spot. EPÀRCHÎA hosts exhibitions, music events, and workshops across disciplines, functioning as an active platform for contemporary creative expression. name: Mauser Harmony with Nature Foundation
orgDescription: The Mauser EcoHouse is owned by The Mauser Harmony with Nature Foundation, a non-profit 501(c)(3) organization committed to improving the quality of life on planet Earth. OUR VISION We envision a healthy planet. A world where every person has the opportunity to drink clean water, breathe fresh air, eat healthy food and spend time enjoying nature. The earth is our home and we believe it should it should be treated with care and respect. OUR MISSION To educate ourselves and others on how to live, work and play harmoniously within the environment. We support artists, students, businesses, and non-profit organizations who are committed to honoring and respecting our natural world. The Foundation was established in 1998 in memory of our friend and mentor, Dr. Ferdinand F. Mauser, a Professor at Wayne State University in Detroit, MI, Keio University in Tokyo, Japan and University of Munich in Munich, Germany. As a tribute to Dr. Mauser, international author, educator, traveler, we established the Mauser EcoHouse Artist Residency in 2018.

name: MeMe Art Res
orgDescription: MeMeraki Artist Residency is a non-profit organisation based in Limassol. It was founded by Katerina Savvides in 2019, from the need to exist in a multicultural and multidisciplinary artistic community, within which artists can find ongoing stimulation based on feedback exchange and critiques. As an organisation we are working towards bringing to the table anything that is required for the artist to simply step in and work in an environment created by artists for the artists. Our aim is to provide artists with accommodation and workspaces at minimal cost, for a fully immersive residency program running at specific periods throughout the year. Our philosophy stems from the fact that the artist produces “stronger” work when immersed in the process of, uninterrupted by the interventions of small everyday life. The idea here is to take care of everything so that the artists are free to create. We want to work towards bringing all sorts of different parameters of the arts in communication with each other and to initiate a spirit of collaboration and exchange within the artistic community. By reaching out to the international artistic community and by hosting artists from abroad to work and experience art in Cyprus, we aspire to establish what will become a dialogue of exchange, influence and stimulation, both for the local artists as well as the international.

orgDescription: MERZ combines workshop, TV production and art gallery and museum into an artist/maker/architect/author residency programme. MERZ is sited in Sanquhar’s former lemonade factory and includes the Museum of Model Art, formerly the town’s abattoir. Residencies of a month or more include an exhibition at MERZ or the Museum of Model Art. Film-diaries are offered to support artists in residence – with Summerhall TV as required. Artists at MERZ reach virtual as well as physical audiences for work and development. MERZ also runs annual courses in stained glass and art-models which are subject to separate Call-Outs on ResArtis. Residencies are available throughout the year, taking place in what has become Sanquhar’s Cultural Quarter and are typically four to six weeks in duration with a two week minimum. The 2025-26 MERZ Hunker Down Residency is offering a long-term five or six month residency from October thru March for individual artists and writers or those working collectively to undertake project development in our two bedroom cottage with studio. MERZ and the Museum are key components of Sanquhar Cultural Quarter, located in the heart of this small quiet town in scenic Dumfries and Galloway, South West Scotland. Residency Accommodation All our residency accommodation is self-contained, equipped with double beds, shower rooms and kitchen facilities. The Bothy residency building is a unique 1830s converted stone-built building adjacent to the workshop and gallery overlooking a small wood. Our Tadpole residence is converted from a small brick built industrial building from the 1890s adjacent to our Museum. No 5 is a cosy two-three bedroom house with kitchen and studio on ground floor, located opposite the Museum of Model Art. For further details and photographs go to https://www.merz.gallery/residencies For short film clips of artists/writers in residence go to https://www.merz.gallery/news For recommendations go to https://www.merz.gallery/recommendations In addition the Snug residency provides a self contained fully-equipped mini-flat for teaching staff within the MERZ flat overlooking the Museum.

residencyDescription: This old house was built in a time when Japan was not rich yet, the inside structure is simple and minimal. And you will become feeling comfortable after you got used to it, and discover the pure beauty in these, and be able to have new inspirations. Such the experience is just one example, but it would be pleasure if you can experience the real Japanese traditional life which is being lost little by little even in Kyoto now and feel something from them.

name: Miller Art Museum
residencyName: DOME HOUSE AL & MICKEY QUINLAN ARTIST RESIDENCY
orgDescription: ABOUT THE MILLER ART MUSEUM The Miller Art Museum is located on Wisconsin’s Door Peninsula (USA) and is the County’s year-round center for exhibition, education, and creative enrichment in the visual arts. The institution is the Peninsula’s only fine art museum, housing a dynamic permanent collection of 20th c. Wisconsin art. The institution is also home to the world’s largest public collection of artwork by Gerhard CF Miller, a locally celebrated artist and the most influential artist Wisconsin’s Door Peninsula has known. Miller led a distinguished art career that afforded him membership in the prestigious American Watercolor Society, the National Audubon Society, the Wisconsin Watercolor Society, and Wisconsin Painters and Sculptors as well as inclusion in a 1966 exhibit at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York. He was an energetic, generous, comic, and endlessly creative individual whose creative spirit lives on today through the institution he gifted to the Door County community in 1975. Among the most outstanding holdings are works by important figures closely connected to Miller: Roy M. Mason, James J. Ingwersen, Jessie Kalmbach Chase, Lester Bentley, and Charles L. Peterson. In addition to these collections, the museum also houses an extensive collection, comprising more than 1,200 works, of notable Wisconsin artists with works by John Colt, Robert Von Neumann, James Cagle, Theodore Czebotar, Tom Uttech, Alicia Czechowski, Ruth Grotenrath and Schomer Lichtner. The permanent collection is rotated regularly and featured on the second floor Ruth Morton Miller Mezzanine along with a separate gallery of Miller’s work. The Museum’s main gallery features regularly changing exhibitions, embracing a wide range of subjects and media, both historic and contemporary; the second floor Gerhard CF Miller wing surveys the extraordinary life and work of celebrated dean of Door County artists Gerhard CF Miller, the Museum’s namesake, along with a rotating selection of works from its vast permanent collection. For general information about the Miller Art Museum and questions from the media, please call 920.746.0707, use the contact form at www.millerartmuseum.org to e-mail us, or get in touch with us directly info@millerartmuseum.org.
