name: MiSHŌ
orgDescription: MiSHŌ is an organisation that connects international creative practitioners to the vibrant community of Fujino town, located to the west of Tokyo. Fujino (population of 8000 residents) is known as an art village and one of the Transition Movement towns in Japan. With history as an artists’ colony where artists evacuated during the Second World War, Fujino has been the site of several art projects and residencies since the 1990s. It is a decentralized satoyama, consisting of dozens of villages nestled in the valleys overlooked by the Tanzawa Mountains, surrounded by rich forests and streams. Misho (実生) is named after a Japanese word for “seedling.” Just as people have maintained the vitality of forests by improving the environment and taken care of satoyama as areas that sustain their daily lives, our project uses this word with the intention to cultivate the ground for co-creation where artists and local people can interact and spontaneously generate new ideas and creative solutions. By connecting these activities and the network of creative people to the world, we aim to make the area a global hub for the regeneration of natural and cultural ecosystems. We envision MiSHŌ as a welcoming space for educational and cultural events, spontaneous happenings and organized community activities. MiSHŌ is run by Kohei Hashimoto and Vika Množina Hashimoto. Kohei, co-founder and arts manager, studied Sound Arts and Design in London and has extensive experience coordinating arts projects and managing cultural events in Japan before establishing himself in Fujino in 2021. Vika, co-founder and artist originally from Lithuania with a BA in Sound Arts, has been an active member of the Fujino community, using her social photography to explore local life and traditions.

To facilitate these kinds of opportunities and experiences for children and adults, Mlango Farm Foundation (MFF) was established to develop and coordinate educational programs and eventually build a Visitor Centre to host groups promoting green initiatives and learning. name: Nacán Art Residency
orgDescription: nacán – taíno word meaning the center or the middle. It is precisely what we invite to experience: the search for balance, the constant attempts to define ourselves in relation to the outer world, and the ability to see ourselves through our creations. In our unconditional commitment to art and nature, we have created a platform for unhindered creation and imagination, nature being the eternal inspiring muse that accompanies the practitioner at all times. We built an art studio in the middle of the jungle, just a few steps away from the magical El Valle Beach. 30 mts2 (323 sq ft) of pure versatility, a neutral space that does not interfere between the creator and nature, nacán is prepared for the development of individual or collective works in the following disciplines: music production, painting, drawing, photography, tattoos, writing, and any kind of activity that fits. We constructed a carefully designed ‘jungle-inspired’ room, installed custom-built acoustic elements, utilized absorbers and diffusers to control the frequency spectrum, and create that 3D image for users so that they can experience a fresh sense of sound. Therefore – the space offers peace of mind and inspiration to the ears of producers, audio professionals, and music lovers. Most of the soundproofing panels are removable so we can achieve an empty space effect which is ideal for the creative processes in many other disciplines, highlighting the visual arts. For painters, we have prepared easels, stools, brushes, etc. The gear list: – Kali LP-8 Studio Monitor; – SSL – SSL2+ 2-in/4-out Audio Interface (Compatible USB and USB-C); – Arturia KeyStep 37 Key Controller & Sequencer; – Shure SM57 Dynamic Microphone; – sE Electronics XR1 Passive Ribbon Microphone

name: Natimuk Exile
orgDescription: Greg Pritchard has been running art projects for several decades, and has participated in residencies in Asia, Africa and many in Australia. His arts practice looks at the human and animal interactions. It is often satirical, quirky, combining analogue forms with cutting edge digital technologies, but always with a deep philosophical underpinning. Turning from writing to visual art in 2000 and then taking up performance as well in 2006. In 2012 he did a performance on a salt lake north of Natimuk, titled Olver’s Tale. He founded the Natimuk Frinj Biennale in 2000, and was director again in 2022. He has worked with the Natimuk group of artists on the large community celebratory spectacles on the local wheat that made the festival’s name. This group of artists have taken these performances to other places in Australia performing on other iconic structures, and many toured the world with Bambuco, a company that built giant bamboo structures. Dr Greg Pritchard is also an arts administrator, working on many art projects in Victoria and NSW over the last 20 years. These include Artistic Director of the Regional Arts Australia conference Artlands in Dubbo in 2016 and AD of Regional Arts BSW’s Conference Artstate in Tamworth in 2019. He is currently the Creative Producer for Ripple Fest, a multi-arts festival.

Nida Art Colony is on the Curonian Spit, which is a peninsular dividing the Curonian Lagoon and the Baltic Sea. In the year 2000, the Curonian Spit was included into the UNESCO World Heritage List as one of the most beautiful and unique cultural landscapes of Europe. The Curonian Spit is a National park with sand dunes and pitch pine forests as characteristic features of its landscape. Artists like Max Pechstein and Karl Schmidt-Rotluff, writers like the Nobel Prize winner Thomas Mann, composers and actors prized its landscape and ambience.

The university has twelve buildings in the heart of the city. Our campus is easily accessible by transit and surrounded by safe, walkable neighbourhoods. OCAD U has more than 4,500 students and 17 undergraduate programs. Field placement and internship opportunities are available in almost every program. We have over 400 faculty who are practicing artists and designers in their fields. With small class sizes and technical staff in all our shops and studios, you are more than just a number to us. OCAD University is situated on the treaty lands of the Mississaugas of the Credit First Nation. These are the ancestral territories of many nations, including the Anishinaabeg, the Haudenosaunee and the Huron-Wendat who are the original owners and custodians of the land. name: Ottawa School of Art
residencyName: Ottawa School of Art Residency Program
orgDescription: In 1879 by a group of prominent local citizens under the patronage of the Governor General, the Marquis of Lorne and his wife, the Princess Louise founded the Ottawa Art Association. The Association was determined to open as school of art and design in the capital. Classes began in April of 1880 with 18 students enrolled in the Ottawa Art School as it was then called. Over the next 100 years there were many changes and transitions to the school and its community, but the school survived and emerged from the war years as the Ottawa Municipal Art Centre. In 1976 the school was reorganized under its present name and in 1983 it moved into its present location in the By Ward Market district in Ottawa. In 2009 the school expanded with a second campus being added in the Shenkman Arts Centre in Orleans.
residencyDescription: The Ottawa School of Art (OSA) established an artist residency program during its 135th anniversary. The residency program is located solely in the ByWard Market campus in downtown Ottawa. OSA has opened its specialized studios there for ceramics, printmaking & sculpture for use by resident artists during the schools regular hours of operation. OSA will accept a maximum of 2 artists per studio at any time during the year. We suggest that the minimum residency time should be no less than 2 weeks. There is no official maximum length of time – this will be worked out with each resident artist.

name: Out Of The Circle
residencyName: Out Of The Circle Arts Residency
orgDescription: Out of the Circle is an arts entity based in Cairo, Egypt, catering to the MENA region’s digital and new-media arts scene. We offer a platform that facilitates and curates events, residencies, and exhibitions for artists in a two-way exchange between the Egyptian and international art scene. We connect Egyptian and North African artists to the global scene by helping them secure enriching opportunities abroad, and in turn, organise artist residencies for international artists in Egypt. Out of the Circle also curates exhibitions and festivals on several scales, while also providing arts management and curatorial support to other artistic entities in Egypt. In parallel, we also conduct ongoing research projects and compile databases on digital and new media art to better understand and support these mediums. Mission Out of the Circle’s mission is amplifying the voices and stories of new media/digital artists through several channels of support. We aim to cement a platform for young established new media/digital artists from the MENA region while connecting them to the international scene. History Out Of The Circle started as an initiative with the simple goal of supporting and promoting young Egyptian contemporary artists, and has grown over the years to become an arts management organization with a wide-spanning program. In 2008 Out of The Circle was providing young Egyptian contemporary artists with opportunities and support to present their works in exhibitions, projects, and workshops and professionally present their work. After several years of expanding our family of artists and partners in Cairo, Out Of The Circle was registered in 2013 as an organization in Cairo to continue its path with more outreach while offering more professional support in arts management and curation. We have since focused our attention on contemporary art to new media and digital art in particular, noticing them as fast-growing mediums in Egypt. Artworks in these tech-based mediums sit at the intersection between science, art, and society, and our interest lies in exploring the ways in which they can influence and develop our society – giving us insights on our present or helping us imagine a future of possibilities. Over the years our work in new media and digital arts allowed us to explore the breadth and depth of this fast-evolving medium, inspiring us to keep up with it and strive to showcase the artists’ work with excellence. We also began providing arts management and curatorial support for individual visual artists and arts organizations. After years of working on art projects, festivals, and research projects, we were able to extend our contemporary art focus beyond Egypt to the Middle East and North Africa.
residencyDescription: Our ongoing art residency is for international visual and digital artists, curators, and researchers, who would like to explore a unique blend of contemporary Egyptian life, as well as its traditions, arts, and culture. It offers an opportunity for artists working with digital mediums to explore connections and find relevance between technology, society, and art.

orgDescription: PADA is an independent, not-for-profit, artist-led organisation located in Barreiro, Lisbon’s South bay. Set in a derelict industrial park with history dating back to 1885, our location gives artists-in-residence a unique experience. Artists will be surrounded by history as well as local fabricators providing inspiration, material knowledge and resources for experimentation and production. PADA’s facilities reinforce this with large studios and technical support to encourage and facilitate ambitious work. At PADA, we promote interaction with the local community through projects and artistic interventions that engage with the environment. We aim to create a more sustainable residency and encourage artistic practices that share this ethos. Over the last six years, PADA has worked with 400 artists from all over the world. As part of the Studio & Gallery Programmes, PADA has organised more than 50 exhibitions, including the end-of-residency group exhibitions to showcase the work developed by the current Artists-in-Residence.

name: Paleohori eco-art space
orgDescription: Paleohori is an eco-art space organizing and hosting educational programs, workshops and artistic residencies. It is the vision and creation of Kyveli Kouvatsi and Yorgos Sioras Deligiannis, two dance artists and educators from Greece who envisioned a wooded piece of land as a meeting place for moving and sensing experiences. The concept of Paleohori arose from a deep need to reconnect with nature and to meet a community of similar interests and quests. The idea was conceived in October 2021 when there was nothing but trees on the land and by the summer of 2022 the first educational program for Paleohori became a reality. It is a project of Tripudium Collective, an artist-run, non-profit organization, founded in 2015 in Athens and based now in Lefkada, Greece. The organization focuses on dance education, research, and creation, engaging in an active dialogue with the sociopolitical landscape of everyday life. Our vision is to create a meeting point for people and practices that value nature, honor sensorial experiences, welcome diverse corporealities, and dare to reflect through others. Our deepest desire is to grow slowly yet firmly, like a cypress tree, rooting deeply in a sustainable approach that respects and nourishes otherness. We aspire to be part of a ‘forest-like’, broader ecosystem, alongside like-minded individuals and their trajectories.
residencyDescription: Paleohori eco-art space offers a range of residency and educational programs that merge dance, sustainability, and artistic exploration within the serene landscape of Lefkada Island, Greece. These programs provide artists, choreographers, movement enthusiasts, and interdisciplinary practitioners with a unique space to explore movement in connection with nature, community, and ecological awareness.

name: Philotera AS
orgDescription: The Spitsbergen Artists Center is made up of three parts. There are the extensive exhibition rooms which are used for art exhibitions, local functions, and community-building. There are eleven studios for local artists and artisans and an area for craft sales, and the artists residency. The goal of the Spitsbergen Artists Residency is to foster the connection of artists from different countries, disciplines, and media with the reality of the high Arctic. Svalbard is where climate change happens first. There is no more urgent issue facing our world than climate change. At the Spitsbergen Artists Center we believe that while art is not THE answer, it is AN answer in increasing awareness of what is happening to our shared planet and hopefully, together we can be agents for change. The residency is on the second floor of the Spitsbergen Artist Center, which is located in the historic Nybyen section of Longyearyben, Svalbard. On the first floor we have a craft center, studios for local artists, several exhibition spaces of varying sizes and a small cinema. Events are regularly organized. The residency consists of three private rooms, a large common area with a fully equipped kitchen, and two shared bathrooms. There is a laundry machine. Bed linen and towels are provided. Internet is provided. There is one studio available for resident artists.
residencyDescription: The residency program is open-call and individually motivated. Artists of all disciplines are welcome to work on projects related to Svalbard, the Arctic, or polar themes. Artists can stay for a minimum of two weeks to a maximum of three months to work on self-directed projects. Community events are arranged monthly to introduce resident artists to local artists and other visiting artists in Longyearbyen. The residency will provide assistance to help artists find the assistance they need to get out into the wilderness (and back) safely with the help of local guides interested in private trips and local tour companies. Residency artists are asked to have either an exhibition in the gallery space, or give a workshop or lecture for the local community. The residency has hosted performance festivals, traditional art exhibitions, and dance performances. There is a cinema that seats 20 available to media artists for screening their work both privately and for an audience. Activities depend greatly on the time of year artists come. Seasons on Svalbard change dramatically and suddenly. In a three month stay an artist can experience the midnight sun when they arrive, and leave during polar night. In summer it is possible to experience the archipelago by boat and hiking. In spring there are snowmobile excursions, skiing, and dog sledding available to get into the wilderness. Our residents’ safety is paramount. No artist is allowed beyond the town limits without being accompanied by an experienced Svalbard guide who can keep them safe from the dangers both of nature and polar bears. This program replaces the previous Galleri Svalbard residency which is permanently closed.

residencyDescription: Apapacho: “to embrace or caress with the soul.” This is the way we Mexas define apapacho. Curiously, the Nahuatl root of the word apapacho -patzoa or papatzoa-, does not have such a meaning. The verb patzoa means “to squeeze,” “to squeeze between two that are very close together” or “to soften a fruit with the fingers.” The other Nahuatl root to which the origin of the word apapacho is attributed is pachoa, which, among other meanings, includes “hug.” We decided to take the process of metaphorizing the origin of the meaning of apapacho to name our Arts Residency project. For Mexicans apapacho is a gesture or attitude with which love, affection, tenderness, etc. is shown to another person.

name: R.A.R.O. Bogotá
orgDescription: R.A.R.O. is an international residency program that proposes an alternative model based on a wide network of studios and cultural spaces, rather than a single workspace. Through this collaborative structure, over 28 local artists’ studios, art departments from public and private universities, and other interdependent cultural projects welcome residents and support their creative processes across the program’s various formats. Founded in Buenos Aires in 2014, R.A.R.O. has hosted more than 450 artists from all over the world. Since 2024, the program has also operated in Bogotá (Colombia), where it has received over 100 artists, curators, and researchers. Throughout its history, the program has established alliances with various institutions to promote grant programs and strengthen artistic creation, the exchange of knowledge, and co-learning through both short and long-term residencies. The R.A.R.O. proposal invites participants to work alongside artists, curators, managers, and researchers in a dynamic of itinerancy, dialogue, and collaboration, where each space in the network functions as a node for learning and experimentation. In addition to studio work, the program includes complementary activities such as visits to museums and public and private collections, artist talks, field trips, and work critiques, broadening and deepening the experience of every residency. More INFO: http://www.esraro.com

orgDescription: RaumArs is the third oldest residency in Finland and is a non-profit independent association with a volunteer board, exhibition supervisors and a part-time executive director. RaumArs is renting an old, recently renovated wooden building dating from 1925 from the City of Rauma for artist residencies, exhibitions, workshops, events and meetings. The Art House RaumArs locates in the immediate vicinity of the city library, the theatre and the school–culture–sports centre. RaumArs collaborates with local schools, art institutions, art museums, music school, care homes and widely with different associations and festivals. Artists have interesting collaboration opportunities with them and in Rauma’s two World Heritage Sites. The residency is intended for artists working independently or in a community from all art fields. Couples, small groups of three, curators, researchers and families are also welcome. You can also apply for the use of the gallery space (rent) and the garden (free of charge). If the artist wishes to organize an exhibition or hold an open studio during the residency period, this must be applied for at the same time as the residency application.
residencyDescription: At the RaumArs residency, international contemporary art meets a vibrant local community and a historic setting. The residency encourages artists to engage with others — whether local residents, fellow artists or operators from various sectors. At RaumArs, artistic work takes place as part of the city: projects can extend from the gallery to public spaces, courtyards, streets, and unexpected places. The residency offers time to focus, but also the opportunity to experiment, connect, and create something new together.

name: RDW Glass
orgDescription: RDW Glass Ltd is a small, family-run architectural decorative glass company based in the East End of Glasgow, Scotland. Our studio offers the design, manufacture, installation and repair of stained glass, etched glass and fused glass windows. Projects range from small domestic repairs and home renovations to full church restorations. Alongside our commissioned work, we run a wide range of evening and weekend classes in stained glass, welcoming beginners as well as experienced makers. We also offer studio space and equipment hire for artists who wish to work with glass in a supportive workshop environment. A key part of our work involves creating community-made stained glass windows that showcase working-class Scottish histories and local social heritage. These projects are developed in collaboration with community groups across Scotland, and the finished windows are gifted to local libraries or other public buildings so they can be publicly displayed and enjoyed.
residencyDescription: Stained Glass Residency, taking place over 3 weeks in September 2026 (Monday 7th of September to Monday 28th of September). This unique opportunity, led by glass artists Keira Mclean and Rich Welsh, invites artists of all backgrounds to explore stained glass as a storytelling medium. Located in the East End of Glasgow, the residency offers a nurturing environment in a working glass studio to develop your skills, collaborate with fellow artists and contribute to the city’s storied tradition of glass craftsmanship.

The residence not only offers a space for artists, writers, nomads, but also creates a unique international community of creative and conscious people.

Desde 2002 ha presentado exposiciones y eventos culturales interdisciplinarios, con énfasis en la calidad y en prácticas artísticas que desafiaban los marcos institucionales del arte. En 2006 se fundó el programa Artista en Residencia (AIR), que este año celebra su vigésimo aniversario. El programa conecta a artistas regionales, nacionales e internacionales en un auténtico intercambio, trabajando en diálogo con la comunidad artística local, las instituciones culturales y el público en general. Residencia Corazón cuenta con el apoyo del Ministerio de Cultura, el Instituto Cultural de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, la Municipalidad de La Plata y la Universidad Nacional de La Plata (UNLP).
residencyDescription: Residencia Corazón is much more than a residence: it is a home for ideas, creativity and connections. Located in the center of La Plata, Buenos Aires, Argentina, our house was created… 20 years ago! As a refuge where artists from all disciplines, writers, researchers and curators can get away from the noise to focus on what really matters: their art, their voice, their creative journey. We are pioneers in promoting cultural exchange and connections with local creatives and audiences in Argentina and the Latam region, and we are ready to support you in your professional and artistic development!

name: Residência São João
orgDescription: São João Residency is an independent project focused on the intensive development of creative people’s work, processes and experiences. The residency is located in a historic 19th-century coffee farm, with an agroecological approach, near the city of São José do Vale do Rio Preto, in the countryside of Rio de Janeiro. 60% of the farm is constituted by preserved Atlantic forest and there is an ongoing reforestation project. The residency was founded in 2012 by multi-disciplinary artist and farmer Antonio Sobral who believes that contact with nature and reduction of outside stimuli and demands, as well as living together with other residents, are some of the essential factors that contribute to the development and establishment of lines of thought and production for creative minds. Two annual residencies happen in the main building: Verãozão and Somsocosmos, a sound art residency, with an open call. Since 2021 the new space Casa Figueira can host up to 4 artists at a time, with a flexible and autonomous programme that aims to adjust to artists’ needs and demands.
residencyDescription: The São João Residence fosters creative processes, production of artwork, collaboration among participants and interaction with its rural surrounding. On the other hand, it focuses on regional development, through the promotion of local knowledge and arts, and the offering of cultural events. RSJ is located in a historic farm working with organic farming and nature protection, a context which stimulates the resident’s perception of the environment. We bet in the connection city-countryside, as a way of infusing ecological visions and sounds in contemporary culture, therefore we collaborate with strategic partners in big cities such as Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo, where we organize events and publications through Deep editions, our editorial platform.

name: Rimbun Dahan
orgDescription: Rimbun Dahan is the home of architect Hijjas Kasturi and his wife Angela. Set on fourteen acres outside Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, the compound of Rimbun Dahan is a centre for developing traditional and contemporary art forms. It features buildings designed by Hijjas Kasturi, as well as two 19th century traditional Malay houses from Perak and Penang, in an indigenous Southeast Asian garden environment. We offer residencies for visual artists, dancers, choreographers, writers, arts managers, curators and researchers as well as educational opportunities for students of architecture, ecology and botany. We provide workspace and accommodation in this serene garden setting, for artists seeking solitude, silence and/or space to focus on their work as well as the opportunity to meet and network with other artists from around the world. Our focus is on supporting artists from within the Southeast Asian region, especially local Malaysian artists, while still providing space for international artists who are interested in engaging with Southeast Asian and Malaysian culture and art. Established in 1994, the program has hosted hundreds of individuals who have benefited from the unique atmosphere of Rimbun Dahan to build their own artistic practice.

name: Rondo
orgDescription: Rondo Residency is an artist-run organization established in 2024, located in Mexico City. Committed to supporting emerging and mid-career artists, Rondo provides a nurturing environment for artistic production while facilitating connections to the local contemporary art scene. The residency is designed to be accessible, offering subsidized rates for local Mexican artists, supported by the fees of international participants. The residency program is structured around four key axes: Production, Theoretical Engagement, Art Market, and Public Relations. Each axis focuses on different aspects of the artistic journey, allowing residents to concentrate on creating new work while also engaging in discussions and studio visits with curators, critics, and cultural agents. The program culminates in a public presentation, showcasing the work developed during the residency. Rondo hosts up to four resident artists at a time, fostering a collaborative and supportive atmosphere. This intimate setting encourages artists to share ideas and experiences, enhancing their creative processes. Rondo Residency upholds strategic partnerships with organizations such as Clavo Art Fair, Galería Unión, and Plomo Galería. These collaborations enhance the residency experience by connecting artists with opportunities for exposure, networking, and engagement within the vibrant contemporary art scene of Mexico City, ultimately supporting the growth and success of the participating artists.

name: Rothko Museum
orgDescription: In addition to showcasing Rothko’s work and organising temporary exhibitions, the Rothko Museum in Daugavpils, Latvia, maintains a vibrant international residency programme. It hosts regular creative symposiums in different mediums, such as painting, printmaking, textile, ceramics, photography, and sculpture. Inspired by the singular atmosphere of the Daugavpils Fortress, artists create exclusive pieces that grow their individual portfolios and contribute to the Rothko Museum’s expanding collection. Annual events like the Mark Rothko Painting Symposium, the LatgaleGraphic Art Symposium, and the Ceramic Laboratory Symposium have become cherished traditions. The museum offers two residency formats: (1) Annual Open Call Programme, which includes the Mark Rothko Painting Symposium in September, the Graphic Art Symposium in March and the Ceramic Symposium in May. For this programme, artists have to cover only transport costs. The other costs are covered by the organisers. (2) Individual or group residency programme, which is entirely self-funded by the artist or artists.
residencyDescription: The Rothko Museum in Daugavpils, Latvia, is one of the 21st century’s most ambitious cultural projects in Eastern Europe. Located in the historical artillery arsenal of the Daugavpils Fortress, this multifunctional hub for art, culture and education remains an evolving and inspiring place for creative expression and experience.

name: Round Them Oranges
orgDescription: Round Them Oranges Round Them Oranges is an arts Organisation dedicated to supporting experimental, interdisciplinary, and context-responsive practices across contemporary art. Conceived as a platform rather than a single venue, it fosters dialogue between artists, curators, artisans, and communities through exhibitions, residencies, research initiatives, and public programs. The foundation prioritizes process, collaboration, and knowledge exchange, with a particular interest in practices that engage with material culture, ecology, and lived experience outside dominant urban art circuits. Operating between Rajasthan and the Himalayan region of Ladakh, with a residency in Stok near Leh, the foundation creates conditions for slow, reflective work in remote contexts. Its programs encourage cross-cultural encounters and long-term engagement rather than short-term production. Through partnerships, mentorship, and artist-led initiatives, Round Them Oranges seeks to build sustainable cultural infrastructure while amplifying diverse voices and experimental forms of practice.
residencyDescription: The residency supports critical, experimental, and context-responsive artistic practices that engage with landscape, ecology, culture, and community. On the property there are 5 country houses creating a tiny rural community. Artists are hosted at Villa Amati, an early 20th century characteristic villa that offers wide and bright rooms, and studios in a unique set of inspirational common spaces.
residencyDescription: RUC residency supports multicultural dialogue and interdisciplinary exchange between international artists and local traditions in a rural dimension that offers artistic time in solitude and exchanges between peers. Sited in a remote location, RUC residency’s isolated beauty is the ideal environment for intellectual work, and creates optimal conditions for concentration and creativity, international exchange, friendship, and mutual understanding. All artists will enjoy full use of the property and all of its amenities, gardens, courtyards, and common spaces.

orgDescription: THE INSTITUTO SACATAR, a non-profit corporation founded in 2000, runs an artist residency program on the island of Itaparica across the bay from Salvador, Bahia, Brazil. Sacatar occupies a sea-side estate, formerly the retreat of a Catholic girls´ school. The artists have their own bedroom/bathroom suites in a large house with a central courtyard and wide verandahs facing the bay. residencyName: The Artists’ Cottage | SAC Arts Residency Program
orgDescription: Alive with galleries, studios, performances and festivals, Salamanca Arts Centre is both a living link to Hobart’s layered past and a vibrant home for Tasmania’s creative future. Salamanca Arts Centre stands on the lands of the Mouheneener people, the Traditional Custodians of this region and part of the oldest continuing culture on earth. We pay deep respect to Elders past and present, and recognise the enduring connection between this place and the long, rich history of storytelling, creativity, and community. Located in the iconic sandstone warehouses of Salamanca Place, SAC is a vibrant cultural precinct and home to a diverse community of artists, makers, performers, and creative thinkers. Founded in 1976 as a community-led initiative, we’ve grown into one of Tasmania’s most significant arts organisations. It is a place where art is made, shared, and experienced every day. As custodians of these remarkable heritage buildings, we take our role seriously in preserving and enlivening them. Our core purpose is to ensure these spaces remain active and open, places where contemporary art can thrive and where the past and present are held in meaningful dialogue.
residencyDescription: The Artists’ Cottage is utilised for Salamanca Arts Centre’s Arts Residency Program. This Georgian sandstone Cottage (C. 1840), is centrally located in historic Battery Point, and within walking distance to Salamanca Place.

name: Sam Rit Residency
orgDescription: Sam Rit Residency was borne out of the desire to create a flexible, inclusive and authentic residency program in the North Eastern village of Sam Rit, Thailand. With additional opportunities such as guided tours, hands-on demonstrations with village locals, to family dinners and market visits, residents can have the chance to inspire new direction and energy in their work whilst escaping from the daily distractions of home/work/school life. Our program provides options for length of stay around work commitments and enough accommodation for partners and children. We welcome all who are interested – from artists of all mediums, arts managers and arts workers, academics of all disciplines, researchers and students. This cultural residency program offers a rare opportunity of total immersion into real rural Thai life with the comfort and convenience of a self-contained residence with shared facilities and a support network in place. Program Objectives – To provide a comfortable, culturally authentic and inspiring stay for residents – To provide the community of Sam Rit with a chance for cultural exchange and an insight into the interests of the resident through an one open studio day per week, community engagement and daily interactions with village life
residencyDescription: Sam Rit Residency is a model of cultural residency open to creative artists of all mediums, arts managers and arts workers, academics, researchers and students. With options for short and long stays as well as partners and children, Sam Rit Residency program provides an opportunity for those with a creative and cultural interest to experience an authentic rural Thai farming village in the province of Nakhon Ratchasima. Completely self-contained with a support system in place, this is an opportunity to be immersed in traditional Thai culture and connect with a community for inspiration, contemplation and creation in your field.

name: Sansusī
orgDescription: The association Sansusī was founded in 2013 by a group of enthusiasts to organize an event in the courtyard of the guest house on the second weekend of August 2014 – an alternative chamber music festival Sansusī. Since then, the festival has been held annually. The original idea was to create an open-air chamber music festival combined with the atmosphere of a small rock festival – live in a tent, but listen to classical music. Although the festival program includes many chamber music opuses of different centuries and styles, one of the main focuses is the promotion of contemporary chamber music. Starting in 2016, the festival also includes other contemporary stage art forms – circus, dance, theater plays, and performance art. Great attention is paid to the presentation of works of art, which results in their display in non-traditional places and forms. One of the greatest joys of Sansusī is the joy of experimentation, which often surprises the audience. Since 2015, the association Sansusī has expanded beyond the usual weekend in August. Now the association is also engaged in stage work and the production of various events and recordings. During these years, more than ten new works have been commissioned, such as chamber operas, theater plays, as well as stage works for children, and interdisciplinary stage and video works. There are also collaborations with various organizations that organize city celebrations, award ceremonies, corporate events, providing them with musical programs and artists. Since 2016, Sansusī has also hosted a variety of artist residencies, initially featuring works created specifically for the festival, but later followed by various other residency programs. One of the most important Sansusī residency programs is Sansusī Well-being Residencies, established in 2017, where artists interact with the community of Sēlija County, especially with patients and staff of Aknīste Psychoneurological Hospital, residents of the social care center, and children in the area. Since 2017, the former festival home – guest house – has been transformed into the Sansusī Residence Center in Susēja.

orgDescription: Tenjinyama Art Studio Sapporo provides ongoing self-funded residencies for any amount of time up to 3 months as well as occasional thematic residencies that are detailed at the time of open call. Set atop the park in southern Sapporo, the building offers panoramic views of the city and its surrounding mountains. Tenjin-yama Art Studio houses 13 studio apartments, versatile larger spaces, as well as a gallery space on the ground floor. Local residents as well as international artists and residents from a wide range of creative backgrounds use this unique public space. This provides a great forum for local engagement as well as an open dialogue between the artists and the community. Tenjinyama Art Studio opened to the public in May 31st 2014 to celebrate the opening of the Sapporo International Art Festival.

orgDescription: The Sasso Residency program is fluid, transformative, generous, warm, open. We want to be a meeting place for you and for other universes. We understand your artistic work and interest as the basis for processes that you initiate or drive forward in Casa Sasso. Always in discourse with yourself, your fellow residents and beyond.
residencyDescription: With a lot of love and almost no money, we play Casa Sasso on the east side of Lake Maggiore: a beautiful, carefully restored 17th century house. name: Made in Sat / Rural Art Residency in Romania
residencyName: Made in Sat Rural Art Residency in Romania
orgDescription: Made in Sat (grown from MarinArt local project) was created to build a local cultural infrastructure in a rural area where opportunities for creative exchange were extremely limited. Since 2015, the team has been developing cultural, community, and artistic projects in Marin with a commitment to: ethical documentation of local stories, craft practices, and everyday life, curating a textile collection and documenting the practices around textiles strengthening intergenerational dialogue, providing access to cultural experiences for children and adults in the village, supporting collaborative practices between artists and local craftspeople, developing long-term archives related to textiles, traditional knowledge, material culture and contemporary rural lifestyle. Between 2016–2019, we organized gatherings and a local festival; in 2021, we opened the MarinArt village library, which also functions as a studio space and hosts short micro-residencies for Romanian artists leading art-education workshops with local children. Starting from the winter of 2024, the residency opened to international artists, aiming to create a space where contemporary art, documentary practices, anthropology, environmental studies, and rural life can intersect in a respectful and mutually beneficial way. During the year, we focus on long-term documentation of traditional practices, textile knowledge, crafts, and the work of regional artisans. We organize workshops with local embroiderers, cultural heritage and textile tours, collaborate with artisans and researchers, and produce documentary films and visual materials. Our mission centers on ethical ethnographic work, cross-cultural exchange, interdisciplinary collaborations, and the integration of artistic practices within documentation and research. We welcome multidisciplinary artists, especially those working at the intersection of visual arts, cultural studies, environmental research, and social sciences.
residencyDescription: Made in Sat Art Residency is an international program designed for visual artists of all fields, writers, and researchers who wish to temporarily relocate to a rural context in order to develop a new project, deepen an ongoing body of work, or focus on long-term research. .

The artist retreat aims to cultivate creativity and provide a change of scenery, allowing for new perspectives and connections to naturally arise in the artist’s work. It is open to creative practitioners at any stage of their practice and does not have any specific requirements, providing artists with the freedom to explore their artistic development.

Artists are provided with accommodation and a studio. Still, most importantly, they are given the rare gift of solitude, of uninterrupted time to let their creative impulses rise and reveal themselves naturally over time.

name: Scuola Internazionale di Grafica, Venice
residencyName: Venice Artist Residency at Scuola Internazionale di Grafica.
orgDescription: Founded in Venice in 1969, the Scuola Internazionale di Grafica is an independent art institution dedicated to printmaking, artist’s books, education, residencies, exhibitions, and contemporary artistic production. Located in Cannaregio, in the historic center of Venice, the Scuola brings together professional studios, teaching activities, artist residencies, exhibition spaces, and collaborations with artists, universities, academies, and cultural institutions from around the world. In 2026, the Scuola is hosting the Indonesia National Pavilion for the 61st International Art Exhibition – La Biennale di Venezia. The Pavilion’s works are produced on site in the Scuola’s printmaking studios, confirming the Scuola’s role as a place where art is not only exhibited, but made. Past and present collaborations and affiliations include international organizations and institutions such as the Royal Society of Painter-Printmakers, The Boston Printmakers, Los Angeles Printmaking Society, Rhode Island School of Design, Boston University, Indiana University, Pratt Institute, The University of Iowa, and others. Artists who have worked, taught, lectured, or exhibited at the Scuola include Stanley Hayter, Henri Goetz, John Ross, Michael Mazur, Hughie O’Donoghue, Yvonne Boag, Jack Boul, Stephen Chambers, Elizabeth Magill, Robert Storr, Jörg Schmeisser, Clare Romano, and many others.
residencyDescription: Throghout the year, the Scuola Internazionale di Grafica offers Independent and Guided Studio Residencies→ for established and emerging artist working in printmaking, artist’s books, works on paper, and related practices.

name: Scuola Napoletana dei Madonnari
orgDescription: The Scuola Napoletana dei Madonnari, founded in 2008 in Naples, is a cultural organization dedicated to the preservation, promotion, and development of the historic Italian tradition of street chalk painting. Through training programs, artist residencies, international collaborations, and community projects, the School supports both emerging and established artists interested in public space practices. Its activities include educational workshops, participation in festivals, social initiatives with disadvantaged communities, and the creation of open‑air exhibitions. The organization aims to serve as a point of reference for the contemporary evolution of Madonnari art, combining heritage preservation with innovation and international exchange.
residencyDescription: The residency offers artists and cultural practitioners an immersive environment to explore contemporary street‑art practices rooted in the tradition of the Madonnari. Activities include hands‑on training in chalk techniques and 3D pavement art, research sessions, mentoring, and opportunities for interventions in public space. The aim of the program is to support artistic development, foster intercultural exchange, and promote innovation while preserving a unique intangible heritage in a contemporary context.

name: Serlachius Residency
orgDescription: The history of the Serlachius Museums starts with Paper mill owner Gösta Serlachius, who had plans to build a museum in Mänttä to house his growing collection already in 1920. / was established in 1933 with the purpose to build and maintain a museum in Mänttä. At present Gösta Serlachius Fine Arts Foundation maintains two museums. Art museum Gösta exhibits the pearls of the art collection that is one of the largest private art collections in Scandinavia. In summer 2014 alongside the art museum will rise a pavilion with area of over 5000 sq.m. that multiplies the exhibition spaces of Gösta and enables construction of new exhibitions, more versatile than before. Gustaf Museum tells stories. In the former head office of the historical forest combine G.A. Serlachius Ltd. curious and surprising exhibitions associate with the colorful history and magnificent architecture of the building. Mänttä Art Festival is summer exhibition of contemporary art organized by Mäntän kuvataiteen ystävät ry, a registered association of the friends of art in Mänttä. The Festival was first arranged in 1993. A biennial event during the early years, the festival has been arranged annually since 1999. The registered association each year chooses a new curator of the next years festival. The curator alone makes decisions in relation to selection of artists and exhibition architecture. The main exhibition space and exhibition centre is Pekilo, a renovated industrial building. Mänttä art festival has grown to be Finlands most important annual show of contemporary art. The curator compiles each year a new selection of art and artists that best reflect a theme or title chosen by the curator. During recent years also artists from e.g. Estonia have participated. Many side programs offer single artists, members of the cultural audience or the curator possibility to reflect on exhibition, particular artworks or other cultural matters. Concerts and lectures as well as other events have been organized to discuss cultural issues in connection of the Art Festival.
residencyDescription: Serlachius residency is a residency studio maintained by the Serlachius Museums and Mänttä Art Festival. Residencies are intended for creative professionals working in the field of art, such as artists, art historians, researchers or curators.

name: Shangyuan Art Museum
orgDescription: Some Chinese poets and critics speak of Shangyuan Art Museum as an art utopia, which is to say that in a standardized, uniform society, Shangyuan Art Museum is in search of a certain kind of difference, where each creative individual is honored for the way in which they seek their value and meaning of life. This art utopia is the achievement of medical doctor and poet Cheng Xiaobei and a group of artists, poets, writers and architects. Beginning in 2000, they raised funds by themselves and searched for a suitable location north of Beijing, at the foot of the Yan Mountains. After 7 years spent in site-selection, organizing, planning, and actual construction, the first stage of this modern architectural complex, with over 19,700 square meters of total floor space on 30,000 square meters of land was finished in the late 2007. This complex, comprising 21 works of original modern architecture, includes a salon space, library, exhibition hall, open-air platform (from which you can see Yan Mountains), video room, cafe, writers’ apartments, artists’ studios, etc.
residencyDescription: We will offer you free spaces to create, live and exhibit for 3 to 6 months. After your residency period, we will organize a symposium which will also include exhibition, publication and criticism on your work. Our aim is to discover and promote excellent art practitioners. We encourage art pertaining to one’s own existence and life experience, distinguished by creativity and poetic quality. We would like to choose 30 persons each year to participate in our residency program, which runs from March to October. We don’t discriminate based on your age, education, where you from or your race. It is required that you should be the creator of the paintings, sculptures, architecture designs or other art forms which you submit. This fact is affirmed by no less than three committee members of Shangyuan Art Museum.

name: SÍM Samband íslenskra myndlistarmanna / The Association of Icelandic Visual Artists
orgDescription: The Association of Icelandic Visual Artists (SÍM) was founded in 1982 and today serves as an interest organization for roughly 760 professional artists. The goal of SÍM is to improve conditions and present the working environment of artists, and the association has representatives in various committees and boards. The Association runs 146 studios all over the greater Reykjavík area and hosts over 200 foreign visiting artists each year. SÍM Residency is an international residency for visual artists and cultural practitioners in Reykjavík, Iceland. It is run by SÍM – Samband íslenskra myndlistarmanna or The Association of Icelandic Visual Artists. ​SÍM is a non-profit organization without any operating state grants. Currently, SÍM is hosting three locations: Hafnarstraeti, where the SÍM Gallery, Office, and Guesthouse are located, and two residency apartments, Seljavegur, which is a 10-minute walk from the city center, and Korpúlfsstaðir, situated on the outskirts of Reykjavik. ​Having started in 2002 with a small one-bedroom apartment and studio in downtown Reykjavik, our residency now welcomes over 150 artists from all over the world annually. It is the oldest artist residency in Reykjavík and has inspired the establishment of many other artist residencies around Iceland. ​We are currently the only visual arts residency based in the Reykjavík area. SÍM Residency offers two residency locations in the Reykjavík area – Seljavegur in downtown Reykjavik and Korpúlfsstaðir set in an idyllic location on the edge of town. The different settings allow us to cater to each artist’s requirements, allowing them to choose their location regarding their needs and art projects. Seljavegur and Korpúlfsstaðir house around 70 studios used by local artists and three workshop studios for Textiles. ​Throughout the year, SÍM and SÍM Residency host long and short exchanges, collaborations, and partnership projects with European cultural institutions and artist organizations.
residencyDescription: The SÍM Residency is an international self-directed and self-funded artist-in-residence programme in Reykjavík, Iceland. The main objective of the residency is to provide a venue for international artists and cultural practitioners to take part in the Icelandic art scene, thereby creating a broader context within which local and international artists can experience their work.

It integrates the functions of collection, exhibition, academic research and public education. name: Skaftfell Art Center
orgDescription: Skaftfell Art Center, in Seyðisfjörður, serves as the regional visual arts center for East Iceland. It is one of the three cultural centers in the region that operate according to an agreement on cultural issues between the state and municipalities in East Iceland. Skaftfell is an independent, non-profit art organization. It was founded in 1998 in honor of the Swiss-German artist Dieter Roth (1930-1998), who frequently lived and worked in Seyðisfjörður in the last decade of his life and had a lasting influence on the cultural life of the town. The organization takes its name from the original name of the timber building, constructed in 1907, that now houses the art center, including an exhibition space, an art library, a meeting room, guest bedrooms, the Skaftfell office, and the Skaftfell Bistro. Skaftfell fosters and presents contemporary art on an international level through its artist residency program, exhibitions, workshops, artist talks, and collaborations with other arts organizations.
residencyDescription: Skaftfell Art Center offers an international self-directed artist-in-residence program in Seyðisfjörður, a small fishing village located in the East Fjords of Iceland. The residency program’s remote setting provides artists the opportunity to work in relative seclusion in a place that is also home to an international community of working artists. The residency offers space for contemplation, productivity, and collaboration and is ideal for artistic research and experimentation.

name: Story Villa
orgDescription: The premises of Story Villa tell the story of an old village school. Built by the village road in 1908, this two-story log building holds significant cultural and historical value as a protected heritage site. The former, spacious classrooms have been transformed into two bright working spaces. Within this charmingly beautiful house, there are three accommodation rooms, as well as spacious communal areas such as the kitchen and living spaces. The residency is ideal for visual artists, but it also welcomes other creative professionals from various fields. The spacious school classrooms can be adapted as workspaces for musicians, theater artists, and dancers. The serene environment also provides a perfect setting for writers, researchers, producers or artisans. Story Villa is open for creative work throughout the year, providing a cozy and comfortable atmosphere. The house is equipped with geothermal heating. We value recycling and principles of sustainable development, which guide us in our daily practices. We value creative work, culture and artistic integrity. Our values are based on ecological, cultural, and social sustainability. Art Residency Story Villa is run by a non-profit family company. The hosts of the residency live in the neighboring house, offering assistance when needed and occasional shared rides to the city.
residencyDescription: Story Villa supports creative work by offering an opportunity to pause in the peace of nature and engage with the historical layers of the Finnish countryside. The traces of interaction between humans and nature in the landscape creates an inspiring environment for working.

orgDescription: Scottish couple, Julia Douglas and Colin Usher, moved into this stunning mansion house in the centre of the vibrant market town of Nérac in South West France, in 2017 to set up a contemporary arts space. Though they are still renovating the property, it is fast becoming a centre for artistic development, providing self-funded residencies for all types of creative practitioner. Studio Faire is near the centre of the vibrant town of Nérac and less than a ten-minute walk to shops, cafes, bars, weekly market, library, theatre, music hall, cinema, supermarkets, old town, Château and riverside walk. Nérac sits to the south of the Lot-et-Garonne, just over the border of the Gers, on the northern edge of Gascony. Here you will find the ‘real’ unspoilt France. Medieval Villages are surrounded by lush green rolling hills that lead your eye to the horizon via sunflower fields, orchards and vines. The perfect place to slow down and focus. This property is called Studio Faire: Studio (noun) a room where an artist, photographer, sculptor, etc. works. Faire (transitive verb) to make or to do. name: Studio for the Research on the Art of Acting
orgDescription: Studio for Research on the Art of Acting is devoted to artistic, educational, research, and residency activities in the field of arts, realising numerous international projects (co-productions, research and educational programs, artistic exchanges and residencies) and hosting a number of distinguished artists and cultural professionals from all over the world. Our mission is to support, nurture and provide space and safe environment for creation, research, education and residency, while encouraging connection between artists and people from different professions, generations, local and national environments, that are creative in the broader sense of the word, bridging encounter with art and its practice with lifelong learning. Studio holds most of its activities at Krušče Creative Center, an artistic estate at the very edge of a forest in a quiet village near Cerknica with only a few inhabitants. Since the beginning of the estate renovation in 2006, Krušče welcomed performing arts, film, music, fine arts, and literature artists, as well as experts in different fields from more than 40 different countries. One of its regular activities has been also the research and experiential and educational activities in psychodrama and psychotherapy, pedagogy and other disciplines that include group work. Krušče Creative Center is a space of confrontation with challenges in creative processes and of a new response to them. Creativity is understood as a space, as people, as a process and as a creation. It enables residence, work, education, supply, free time and flow. It is a space of testing new, questioning the limits, creating the original on the basis of known without fear of failing. An important part of Krušče’s program is a series of little festivals SPACES, BODIES, CURRENTS and WORLDS and Krušče Little Festival of Psychodrama – five days creative/educational/research retreats that explore creation of temporary communities through experiential workshops, lectures, talks and sharing art in a new context.
residencyDescription: Krušče Creative Center stretches through few plots of land with six buildings. The property is being renovated since 2006 and has almost 1000 m2 of spaces for group work and accommodation. The renovation has been a process of artistic directors collaborating with architects, students of scenic design and others to establish spaces and landscapes that respect cultural heritage, being at the same time contemporary and homey. Krušče Creative Center is being appreciated for its remote position and the nature that surrounds it. Krušče combines the possibility of retreating into creative solitude in the middle of nature and simultaneous access to motorway connections, the capital and the borders with Croatia and Italy.

The 5th Dimension Apartment has a private gated entrance and private garden with plenty of space to create, lounge and entertain. orgDescription: Sunbury House DBA is a coastal property located in the West Village of the small art-focused seaside town (6,600 people) of Cambria, California. We operate an artist residency and retreat space, which is intended to provide a respite for artists and creative professionals to work or rest in a peaceful setting. name: TOMA HOUSE AIR
orgDescription: TOMA HOUSE AIR is an artist-in-residence program and contemporary art space in Nara, Japan, supporting contemporary artistic practice while creating opportunities for artists to engage with traditional Japanese craft, historic architecture, and the cultural environment of Nara. The residency welcomes international artists and creative practitioners from a wide range of disciplines and provides private accommodation, shared studio facilities, and spaces for artistic production, exhibitions, workshops, and exchange. Toma House AIR is based in the former Toma family residence, an 18th-century registered national cultural property in Takabatake-cho, a historic neighborhood that developed as a community of Shinto priest families serving the nearby Kasuga Taisha Shrine. The house is the only remaining preserved former priest-family residence of its kind in the neighborhood. Restoration of the property began in 2017 and remains ongoing. Rather than waiting for the restoration to be completed, the house has remained active through artist residencies, exhibitions, performances, workshops, lectures, and other cultural programs. This evolving project is known as Toma Unrestored, reflecting the idea of an unfinished historic space that continues to develop through its use. The residency is situated in a tranquil part of central Nara, within walking distance of Nara Park, the Kasuga Primeval Forest, historic neighborhoods, and four UNESCO World Heritage sites. As Japan’s first permanent capital, Nara has a long history of art, architecture, religious culture, and craftsmanship that continues to shape the city today. Kyoto and Osaka are also accessible in approximately 45 minutes by train, allowing residents to connect with the wider cultural landscape of the Kansai region. Through its residency programs, exhibitions, workshops, and public programs, Toma House AIR creates a setting where contemporary art, traditional craft, historic architecture, and international exchange can meet. The residency supports artists not only in learning established techniques and practices, but also in considering how materials, craft knowledge, place, and history can inform contemporary artistic practice.
residencyDescription: Toma House AIR is an artist-in-residence program and contemporary art space based in an 18th-century historic house in Nara, Japan. Bringing together contemporary art, traditional Japanese craft, and historic architecture, the residency supports international artists through opportunities for focused practice, learning, and exchange with artists, craftspeople, and specialist studios in Japan.

name: TartAMI Residence
orgDescription: TartAMI = TATAMI + ART TartAMI is an artist residency and creative project based in Osaka, Japan, founded by fourth-generation tatami maker and artist Issay Fujiwara. Guided by the idea of Onko Kasshin — bridging old and new — TartAMI explores new possibilities for tatami beyond its traditional use as flooring. Many of TartAMI’s projects use reclaimed or aged tatami materials, natural materials traditionally used in Japanese living spaces, that would otherwise be discarded. Rather than seeing age as deterioration, TartAMI sees it as transformation and explores how traditional materials can find new life through contemporary art and creative practice. Tatami is not only a material, but also a way to explore Japanese culture, space, craftsmanship, and everyday life. Based within a family-run tatami workshop and guesthouse, TartAMI brings together artists, craftspeople, and visitors through residencies, exhibitions, collaborations, and community activities. By connecting tradition with contemporary creativity, TartAMI hopes to create new perspectives on Japanese material culture and encourage cultural exchange across generations and disciplines. orgDescription: The Corridor Project [TCP] is a not-for-profit multidisciplinary arts and cultural organisation based on Wiradjuri country in the Central West of NSW. name: The Farm Margaret River
orgDescription: The Farm Margaret River is located in the south west of Western Australia, a region of ancient soils and flora, bounded by the Indian Ocean. The Margaret River region is an international destination for those interested in the arts, wine growing, surfing and isolated, unspoilt, natural beauty. In the age of the Anthropocene, our relationship to the environment and the reciprocal impact of each upon the other is a complex topic. Here at The Farm Margaret River we engage with agricultural sciences, visual arts and the community to explore and observe our united possibilities. The visual arts are a conduit to our conversation and our perspective of where we stand today. The Farm Margaret River sits upon a beautiful handful of dirt and clean water, farmed for four generations, and prior to settlement, country of the Wardandi cultural group of the Nyoongar people. The Farm Margaret River is located between Margaret River and Gracetown on a tributary that feeds into Ellen Brook. It is a working farm that has transformed existing buildings, such as the hay and machinery sheds, into working studios. The property is nestled amongst a rural community that is interested in holistic and sustainable living practices. Our project aims to bring together artists and agri-culturalists who are focused on developing projects that are rooted in country, in the soil, air and water of this specific location. We offer residencies for large scale and long term projects, and our studios are available for short term use.

It comprises an area of 38.36 square kilometres and as at the 2021 census had a population of 152,2742. Hurstville Museum & Gallery staff manage the artist in residence program. Hurstville Museum & Gallery is home to approximately 6,000 objects and artworks from the local area. Run by a dedicated team within Georges River Council, Hurstville Museum & Gallery offers a full schedule of high-quality exhibitions throughout the year, a diverse range of public programs for all ages and a suite of education programs for school groups. Hurstville Museum & Gallery aims to educate, engage and inspire the diverse community of Georges River through innovative exhibitions, programs and services. We aim to foster creativity, celebrate local history and identity, and support lifelong learning. Georges River Council acknowledges the Bidjigal people of the Eora Nation, who are the Traditional Custodians of all lands, waters and sky in the Georges River area. We pay our respect to their Elders past and present and extend that respect to all Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples who live work and meet on these lands.

name: The Grant Wood Art Colony
orgDescription: The Grant Wood Art Colony seeks to provide a creative home for the next generation of artists and continue Grant Wood’s creative advocacy in the School of Art & Art History and the Division of Performing Arts at The University of Iowa through artist residencies, teaching fellowships, symposia, and community programs. The vision of the Colony is to nurture creative work and teaching in disciplines relevant to the art and life of Grant Wood: studio art, art history, the performing arts, and eventually expanding to a variety of disciplines. The program exemplifies The University of Iowa’s historic commitment to creative work and pioneering of the MFA degree. The Grant Wood Art Colony will further embody the “Iowa Idea” of bringing artists and scholars together in an academic context, as first formulated in the 1920s by President Walter Jessup and Graduate Dean Carl Seashore. The long-term goal is to create a vibrant colony and cultural center, woven together by gardens and studio space. The Grant Wood Art Colony celebrates the life and legacy of Iowa’s most famous artist, Grant Wood. After painting one of the most recognizable images in the world, American Gothic, Wood joined the University of Iowa faculty. Each year, the Colony provides three Fellowships in Painting, Printmaking, and Interdisciplinary Performance. Fellows teach courses, engage Iowans, and pursue their artistic endeavors. The Colony also hosts a biennial symposium and other public lectures to perpetuate Wood’s legacy as an artist and advocate of contemporary art.
residencyDescription: Sponsored by the University of Iowa, the Grant Wood Fellowship and Art Colony is a year long appointment. name: The John Bauer Pottery Studio and BnB
orgDescription: The John Bauer Pottery Studio has two locations in Cape Town, South Africa. The first being at the home studio in Greenwood Road, and the other is John’s flagship store at the Montebello Design Centre. They produce all of John’s work for his store at these locations, one being the Guesthouse which helps fund his company. Here, artists can reside and work on aspects of ceramics they haven’t yet discovered. John pushes the limits of what is technically possible in ceramics and finds a way to make it easier to do. His motto is innovation. Create in a way that is sustainable and new, push the boundaries of what has come before us, and create an era of pottery that will be marvelled upon. John has put his whole life into ceramics, and that is seen through his work. His team and himself make all the bowls, beads and bespoke matchbox tiles that are in his retail stores. One of our goals is to create jobs through John’s work. The creative industry needs aid, and John is giving to it.

name: Åland Archipelago Guest Artist Residence
orgDescription: The residence is situated on Kökar island in Åland, between Finland and Sweden. The residence house is situated by Hellsö bay, just a few meters from the sea. The house has three floors. In downstairs, there are two apartments. Apartment 1 (about 35m2) has a bedroom/workroom, a kitchen, and a toilet. Apartment 2 (about 50m2) has two bedrooms/workrooms, a kitchen, and a toilet. The apartments share a shower. Upstairs there is one small apartment that is in use occasionally and two private studios. In the basement, there is a sauna, two more showers, and a washing machine. Outside there is a terrace. There’s wifi in the residency. Bed linen and towels are supplied. There are bicycles available for residents to use. The island can be explored by walking, bike, or car. There is no public transportation on the island. There is a taxi service. The residence arranges excursions for the residents to local historical, cultural, and natural sites in the area. The distance from the residence to Karlby village is 7 km. In Karlby there is a post office, a school, a library, a gas station, a hardware store, and a grocery store. Regular trips to Karlby are organized by the residency. The ferry port is 12 km from the residence. We will pick you up from the ferry port when you arrive. OPEN CALL – JANUARY 2026 In January 2026 you can apply for the following time periods: 12.4 – 16.5.2026 1.7 – 15.12.2026 Application deadline: 31.1.2026. APPLICATION GUIDELINES: Who can apply? What to include in the application: Application languages are Swedish, Finnish and English. When applying as an individual, please submit in one PDF file: – an artist statement – preferred residency period(s) and length(s). – a plan for residency – a CV – a portfolio (or a link to an online portfolio such as an artist’s website) / any other material relevant to your application The maximum size of the file is 10MB. name: The Old Girls School
orgDescription: The Old Girls’ School was built in the middle of the 19th century. A grand stone building in the center of the village of Sos in the heart of Gascony. It was a school until the mid 60’s. Today it is a large family home surrounded by large gardens. Sos is small village in the the Lot et Garonne countryside surrounded by fields, hills and woods. You can find the first mention of the village and it’s inhabitants in Julius Caesars « Bellum Gallicum » (Gallic Wars) Book III – Chapter XX and XXI. Nowadays the village has a local grocery store, a restaurant, a pharmacy and a bar as well as a regular market on Wednesday mornings. During July and August there is a night market every Wednesday evening. The Old Girls’ School has a stunning setting : a large garden on both sides of the house, the schools’ former playground with the shade of the plane trees and a beautiful view. It is the ideal setting with a private garden that gives you all the tranquillity needed to focus on your work.

name: The Skopelos Foundation for the Arts
residencyName: Create art on the beautiful island of Skopelos.
orgDescription: The Skopelos Foundation for the Arts was established as a non-profit organization in 1999 by the Founder, Gloria Carr. For years it was her vision to create a studio for artists. She wasn’t sure where it would be set up until 1996 when she visited the island of Skopelos. Skopelos is a unique island with the contrast of light and color. It is the greenest island located in the Northern Sporades. The locals add to the extraordinary flavor of the island and this is where Gloria Carr decided she would call home. The mission of the Foundation is to promote the visual arts and education in the arts through cultural exchanges. Guided by the Hellenic history and culture, the Foundation will promote artistic dialogue between the Greek, American and International communities of artists. The ceramics area is open raw space with a gorgeous view of the neighboring island, Alonnisos. There is an electric kiln and wheel on site and as mentioned, a wood-burning kiln. The Foundation is affiliated with Nikos Rodios, who is a world-renowned potter and is known for his patented firing technique that creates a beautiful onyx and is modeled after ancient utilitarian pieces. The printmaking facilities overlook the Aegean Sea, with lots of windows so that the artists always see the light and the constantly changing colors of the water. The studio has state-of-the-art equipment so it can accommodate from the beginner to the most advanced. The Foundation has a Board of Directors which is made up of business people, artists and University Professors from Washington, DC, Chicago and New York. It is affiliated with some of the top Universities including George Mason University, The Art Institute of Chicago, The Corcoran School of Art, Pratt Institute, The University of Florida and The University of Michigan School of Art + Design.
residencyDescription: The Skopelos Foundation for the Arts offers three-week residencies in ceramics, mixed media, painting and printmaking, from April to October.

name: The Weight of Mountains
orgDescription: The Weight of Mountains (TWOM) is a nomadic artist residency and platform for film and media artists, immersing artists in a new location every 2 – 4 years. In doing so, over decades we hope that TWOM will create a larger ongoing conversation about how humanity is intertwined with global environments. ​ The Weight of Mountains is conceptually based on notions of how the human gaze, cognition, and body meets it’s environment. Ideas encompass psycho-geography, the nature-culture symbiosis, the cosmic or residual echoes of time and place, undercurrents, landscape as character: the truths and myths that humans impress upon the surrounding locations in which they live. We partner with arts organisations globally and curate filmmakers working with these ideas who can work site-specifically and handle extreme changes to their typical context. Past selected filmmakers have gone on to present film or media artwork that they’ve created during our residency at TIFF, RIFF (Reykjavik), 57th Venice Biennale, no.w.here London, Alchemy Film and Moving Image Festival, IFFR, The Weight of Mountains Film Festival, National Geographic, Sundance, KIAC Dawson City, CBC, National Museum of Art Osaka (permanent collection) and a plethora of galleries and film events worldwide.

name: The Yefe Nof Residency
orgDescription: The Yefe Nof Residency is a secluded place in the mountains where writers, researchers, and designers bring their projects for the final stage of execution, one resident at a time for two weeks. The annual competition offers an opportunity for a variety of authors to become reinvigorated by the mountain air and experience the lake while pushing their work to completion. Residents will use their time to construct narratives that captivate, to express what they believe to be true and complex, to remind us of the deep beauty and multilayered poetry in the world, to speculate about futures that we can conceive no matter how still unlikely. Just as they are about to be released into the world at large, the final products are also collected in the house, building upon one another in an ever-evolving collection, a network that acts as both a dedication to progress and a dialogue.

name: Tiapapata Art Centre, Inc.
orgDescription: The Tiapapata Art Centre in Samoa fosters excellence in creativity, diversity and innovation in traditional and contemporary arts and crafts. It is registered with the Government of Samoa as a charitable trust. The underlying principles of the Tiapapata Art Centre are: That all people have a right to express themselves creatively and should be encouraged to learn about and develop their creativity That people with limited access to creating arts and crafts should be provided with opportunities to explore and enjoy these activities. Barriers restricting access to arts and crafts should be removed That creativity conduces to wellbeing and That arts and crafts enrich society. The Tiapapata Art Centre is located 800m above sea level and is much cooler than the coast where most villages are located, including the capital city Apia. The Tiapapata Art Centre conducts occasional special workshops with community-based organisations and schools at their premises. In December 2010, the Tiapapata Art Centre opened its new studio where art classes are now held. The studio is a multi-function classroom able to accommodate up to thirty students comfortably although there is seating for 50. Classes are taught in various media: painting, drawing, printmaking and ceramics. In April 2016, the new Tiapapata Art Gallery with a Wild Foods Cafe attached was opened.
residencyDescription: With regular classes throughout the year for people of all ages and occasional workshops held in the community, the Tiapapata Art Centre provides a valuable service for the development of Samoa’s creative economy and welcomes artists in residence to assist with its teaching programme while also allowing for visiting artists to create works of art that can be exhibited either solo or in combined exhibitions held from time to time.
